Diagnosis:
Neonatal brain MRI reveals a large area of restricted diffusion and T2 prolongation involving the left middle cerebral artery territory, particularly the basal ganglia, posterior limb of the internal capsule, and temporal lobe. Accompanying focal mass effect causes compression of the left lateral ventricle. No intracranial hemorrhage or extra-axial collections are seen.

Impression: Acute left MCA territory ischemic infarct with secondary edema. Follow-up imaging and pediatric neurology consultation are indicated.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a large occipital encephalocele. There is a midline bone defect in the occipital skull measuring 1.2 cm, through which a herniated sac measuring 3.5 x 2.8 cm extends. The sac contains cerebrospinal fluid and dysplastic brain tissue from the occipital lobe. Mild, secondary supratentorial ventriculomegaly is noted, with atrial widths of 10.2 mm.

The cerebellar structures are distorted and displaced posteriorly. The remaining spinal canal and spinal cord are intact. Impression: Midline occipital encephalocele with herniated dysplastic brain tissue and associated mild ventriculomegaly.

Brain MRI shows a generalized absence of normal cortical sulcation with a markedly thickened and smooth cerebral cortex, typical of an agyria-pachygyria complex. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, secondary to white matter hypoplasia, creating a colpocephalic appearance. The corpus callosum is hypoplastic, but no other major midline defects are seen.

Impression: Classic lissencephaly (type I) with associated moderate ventriculomegaly and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum. Findings correlate with the clinical history of infantile spasms and developmental delay.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation shows normal, symmetrical intracranial structures. The brain parenchyma shows smooth cortical margins and early sylvian fissure definition, entirely appropriate for 25 weeks. The lateral ventricles are stable and normal in size, with left and right atrial widths of 5.8 mm and 5.5 mm, respectively. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and posterior fossa are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 25 weeks gestation. No structural, cranial, or spinal anomalies identified.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the heart was performed to evaluate for structurally abnormal congenital anomalies. There is normal biventricular chamber size, wall thickness, and global systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 63% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 61%. No focal myocardial wall motion abnormalities, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement are identified.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No structural congenital heart disease, cardiomyopathy, or focal myocardial scarring is visualized.

The cardiac MRI reveals normal biventricular volumes and preserved systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 64% with an end-diastolic volume index of 72 ml/m². The right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 60%. Real-time cine sequences demonstrate normal septal motion, and there is no late gadolinium enhancement to suggest myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI study. No evidence of congenital heart defect, myocardial dysfunction, or abnormal enhancement patterns.

Cardiac MRI of a 20-year-old male presenting with syncope during mild exercise. Comprehensive evaluation including cine sequences, stress perfusion, and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals normal cardiac morphology. Calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 62% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%, with no regional wall motion abnormalities or ventricular dilation. Myocardial perfusion is completely homogeneous under pharmacological stress, and there is no evidence of LGE or myocardial edema.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study. No ischemic, inflammatory, or hypertrophic cardiac pathology is identified to account for the syncopal episodes.

Cardiac MRI reveals Ebstein's anomaly. There is marked apical displacement of the septal and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve, resulting in a large 'atrialized' portion of the right ventricle. The remaining functional right ventricle is small and demonstrates moderately reduced systolic function (RVEF 39%). Severe tricuspid regurgitation is noted, with a dilated right atrium. The left heart structures are normal but compressed.

Impression: Ebstein's anomaly with significant tricuspid valve displacement, severe tricuspid regurgitation, and right ventricular systolic dysfunction.

Structural MRI of the brain shows normal parenchymal signal and volume. No acute infarction, intracranial hemorrhage, mass lesion, or abnormal enhancement is seen. The ventricles and sulci are normal in configuration. The dural venous sinuses show normal flow voids on all sequences.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No structural abnormality or intracranial pathology detected to account for the patient's syncopal episodes.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed using dedicated epilepsy-protocol sequences, including high-resolution 3D T1-weighted and FLAIR acquisitions. There is no evidence of focal cortical dysplasia, hippocampal atrophy, or signal asymmetry in the temporal lobes. The cerebral ventricles and sulcal patterns are normal for age without intracranial masses or hemorrhage.

Impression: Unremarkable and negative epilepsy-protocol brain MRI. No structural abnormality or epileptogenic focus identified on current sequences.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a classic Dandy-Walker malformation. There is marked hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis, which is upwardly rotated by a large, cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle. The posterior fossa is significantly enlarged, elevating the tentorium and transverse sinuses. The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, with atrial measurements of 10.4 mm bilateral.

The cerebral sulcation pattern is appropriate for 24 weeks gestation. The face, chest, abdomen, and spine show no other major structural defects. Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, an enlarged posterior fossa, and mild ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation shows prominent asymmetry of the lateral ventricles. The right lateral ventricle atrium is dilated, measuring 12.4 mm, consistent with moderate unilateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle is entirely normal, measuring 6.5 mm. Cortical folding and sulcation are advanced and age-appropriate, and the corpus callosum is fully intact. There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, mass, or aqueductal stenosis.

Impression: Isolated right-sided moderate fetal ventriculomegaly. Serial ultrasound evaluations are recommended to monitor for progression or resolution.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation shows robust cerebral development. Symmetrical hemispheric anatomy is present, with advanced sulcation and gyral formation appropriate for 32 weeks, including well-defined parieto-occipital and calcarine fissures. Lateral ventricles are small, symmetric, and normal in caliber, with atrial measurements at 6.0 mm on both sides. Posterior fossa and midline structures, including the corpus callosum and vermis, are entirely normal.

All extracranial structures, including the cardiothorasic ratio, kidneys, and abdominal wall, are normal. Impression: Normal fetal brain MRI at 32 weeks gestation. No structural, migrational, or posterior fossa anomalies identified.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve. There is significant downward displacement of the septal and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle, resulting in 'atrialization' of the inlet portion of the right ventricle. Severe tricuspid regurgitation is noted on flow-velocity imaging. The functional right ventricle is small and demonstrates mild systolic dysfunction (EF 43%).

Impression: Ebstein's anomaly with severe tricuspid regurgitation, marked right atrial dilation, and dynamic atrialization of the basal right ventricle.

Brain MRI shows multiple discrete, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions distributed throughout the periventricular and juxtacortical white matter. Several lesions are oriented perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, consistent with Dawson's fingers. Following administration of gadolinium, two of the periventricular lesions demonstrate active, nodular contrast enhancement.

Impression: Multifocal demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. The presence of both enhancing and non-enhancing lesions demonstrates dissemination in time and space, highly suspicious for pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis.

MRI of the brain reveals an intensely and homogeneously enhancing mass centered within the pineal region, measuring 1.8 x 1.5 cm. The mass compresses the tectal plate, leading to mild narrowing of the cerebral aqueduct and early dilatation of the third and lateral ventricles.

Impression: Pineal region mass with secondary mass effect on the tectal plate, highly suggestive of a pineal germinoma. Recommend CSF cytology and tumor marker evaluation.

Fetal MRI performed at 34 weeks gestation. There is a complete absence of fetal urine output resulting in severe, anhydramnios, which limits the image resolution. Evaluation of the fetal abdomen confirms the bilateral absence of renal parenchymal tissue and renal arteries. The fetal urinary bladder is non-visualized. Thoracic volume is severely reduced, indicative of secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. The brain shows normal cortical folding for age.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe anhydramnios and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter sequence) at 34 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 6-month-old infant with complex congenital heart disease. There is a double outlet right ventricle (DORV) with both the aorta and pulmonary artery arising entirely from the right ventricle. A large, non-restrictive subaortic ventricular septal defect (VSD) is identified, measuring approximately 9.5 mm. Severe infundibular pulmonary stenosis is visualized, causing significant restriction of blood flow into the pulmonary trunk.

Impression: Complex congenital heart disease characterized by a double outlet right ventricle, a large subaortic VSD, and severe infundibular pulmonary stenosis (resembling Tetralogy of Fallot physiology). Left ventricular systolic function is 58%.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates severe shortening of all long bones, consistent with micromelia. The femoral, humeral, tibial, and radial bones are less than the 3rd percentile for gestational age and show significant bowing. There is also a mild degree of chest wall narrowing (bell-shaped thorax), though no significant pulmonary compression or hypoplasia is currently identified. The skull is normal in size and mineralization.

The brain, spine, and intra-abdominal viscera are within normal limits. Impression: Skeletal dysplasia, most compatible with a non-lethal form such as achondroplasia given the absence of severe pulmonary hypoplasia. Genetic evaluation is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior callosal body and genu are present, but there is complete absence of the posterior body and splenium. Associated mild colpocephaly is noted, with prominence of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles; the left atrium measures 12.3 mm and the right measures 11.9 mm. Cortical sulcation patterns are otherwise normal and appropriate for 32 weeks.

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum (posterior body and splenium) with mild secondary colpocephaly at 32 weeks gestation.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates normal anatomical positioning and chamber sizes. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume and mass are normal for the patient's age and body surface area. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%, indicating preserved biventricular systolic function. No late gadolinium enhancement is noted to suggest focal myocardial scar or fibrosis. Valve leaflet morphology and flow velocities are completely unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable pediatric cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular morphology, function, and tissue characterization with no evidence of congenital or cardiomyopathy-related pathology.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates normal structural development of the fetus. Intracranial anatomy is intact with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 5.5 mm at the atrium. The corpus callosum, cerebellar vermis, and posterior fossa are normally formed for gestational age. Sulcation is appropriate, with early Sylvian fissure and parieto-occipital sulcus development visible.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation. No structural, intracranial, or spinal anomalies identified. Normal ventricular caliber and age-appropriate brain development.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe spherical dilation of the left ventricle with global hypokinesis. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is severely increased at 142 mL/m², and the ejection fraction is severely depressed at 26%. There is trace mitral regurgitation. No focal areas of late gadolinium enhancement are seen, suggesting a non-ischemic etiology.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy with marked left ventricular enlargement and severely depressed global systolic function.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal structural development. The cerebral hemispheres show appropriate primary and secondary sulcation for 28 weeks, including well-defined sylvian and parieto-occipital fissures. The ventricular system is normal with the lateral ventricular atrium measuring 6.0 mm. The corpus callosum and brainstem are intact.

No fetal chest, abdominal, or skeletal abnormalities are identified. Amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal brain and body MRI at 28 weeks gestation showing age-appropriate development.

Brain MRI demonstrates a well-circumscribed lesion in the left frontoparietal subcortical white matter measuring 1.2 x 1.1 cm. The lesion shows a characteristic 'popcorn-like' appearance, with a reticulated central core of mixed signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images, surrounded by a prominent rim of hypointensity representing hemosiderin deposition. There is no associated edema or mass effect.

Impression: Classic appearance of a cerebral cavernous malformation (cavernoma) in the left frontoparietal lobe. No evidence of acute hemorrhage or surrounding edema is present.

Multiplanar multisequence brain MRI reveals a well-circumscribed cystic lesion containing an intensely enhancing mural nodule in the right cerebellar hemisphere. The cystic portion measures 2.8 x 2.4 cm, and the mural nodule measures 1.2 cm. There is mild surrounding vasogenic edema and local compression of the fourth ventricle, though no upstream ventricular dilation is visualized on current sequences.

Impression: Right cerebellar cystic and solid enhancing lesion, highly suggestive of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. Neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 30 weeks gestation. There is a complete absence of renal tissue within both renal fossae and the fetal pelvis. No renal arteries are identified, and the fetal urinary bladder is non-visualized, consistent with anuria. Severe, near-complete oligohydramnios is present, which limits visualization of some extremities. The fetal lungs are severely small, with a calculated thoracic volume severely below the 5th percentile for 30 weeks.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with classic Potter sequence, including severe anhydramnios and pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI evaluates status post arterial switch operation for d-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA). The reconstructed neoaorta is stable without dilatation or stenosis. There is mild, focal narrowing at the site of the neopulmonary anastomosis with a localized peak velocity of 2.4 m/s. The coronary artery origins are well-visualized and appear normal.

Impression: Post-arterial switch state with stable neoaortic reconstruction and mild, clinically stable neopulmonary supravalvular stenosis. Biventricular size and systolic function are preserved (LVEF 59%).

MRI of the brain was requested to evaluate the etiology of recent-onset atypical absence seizures. High-resolution multiplanar sequences show symmetric myelination and normal cerebral cortical gyral patterns. Ventricles are normal in caliber and symmetry. No hippocampal atrophy or signal abnormalities are detected in the mesial temporal structures. Major intracranial arteries show patent flow voids.

Impression: Structurally unremarkable brain MRI. There are no cortical developmental malformations, space-occupying pathology, or focal parenchymal signal abnormalities found to explain the clinical seizure activity.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a dorsal neural tube defect in the lumbar spine. There is a defect in the posterior osseous elements of L4-S1 with an overlying sac containing neural tissue (myelomeningocele). Brain findings include a small posterior fossa, downward displacement of the cerebellar vermis (banana sign), and bifrontal narrowing (lemon sign), consistent with Chiari II malformation.

Lateral ventricles are mildly dilated at 10.5 mm. Impression: Lumbar myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates normal myelination patterns for the patient's age. The ventricular system, extra-axial spaces, and basal cisterns are unremarkable. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, focal signal abnormality, hemorrhage, or restriction of diffusion. Structural development of the corpus callosum and brainstem is normal.

Impression: Normal pediatric brain MRI. No structural, myelination, or metabolic abnormality detected to account for global developmental delay.

MR imaging of the brain was performed following a sports-related concussion. The scan shows no intracranial extra-axial fluid collections, cerebral contusions, or microhemorrhages on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). The ventricular system is normal, and there is no evidence of structural parenchymal injury.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No structural correlate or traumatic injury is identified to explain persistent post-concussive symptoms.

Fetal MRI performed at 32 weeks gestation reveals classic features of a Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia and rotation of the cerebellar vermis, accompanied by a markedly dilated posterior fossa fluid collection communicating with the fourth ventricle. Torcular herophili and tentorium are elevated. There is associated bilateral ventriculomegaly, with the lateral ventricular atria measuring 14.1 mm on the left and 13.8 mm on the right. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 32 weeks gestation.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation with severe vermian hypoplasia, cystic dilation of the posterior fossa, and secondary moderate ventriculomegaly. Fetal neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Fetal MRI performed at 26 weeks gestation evaluates intracranial development. There is complete absence of the corpus callosum, with characteristic colpocephaly presenting as tear-drop-shaped lateral ventricles and dilatation of the occipital horns. The third ventricle is elevated and moderately dilated, communicating with the interhemispheric space. The bilateral lateral ventricular atria measure 11.5 mm on the left and 11.8 mm on the right, indicating mild ventriculomegaly. Cerebral sulcation and gyration patterns are appropriate for the 26-week gestational age, showing early formation of the parieto-occipital and calcarine fissures.

The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellum and brainstem, appear normally formed without hypoplasia. The remainder of the fetal survey, including the fetal thorax, abdomen, and spine, is within normal limits for gestational age. Impression: Fetal brain MRI demonstrating complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with mild bilateral colpocephalic ventriculomegaly. Prenatal pediatric neurology consultation is recommended.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation for evaluation of fetal intracranial structures. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate bilateral symmetry and normal early opercularization and sulcation patterns for 22 weeks. The ventricular system is normal in caliber, with the left and right lateral ventricular atria measuring 6.1 mm and 5.9 mm respectively. The corpus callosum is visible and appropriate in length. The posterior fossa, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, is morphologically unremarkable.

Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate brain development and normal ventricular calibers. No intracranial anomalies identified.

High-resolution cardiac MR imaging reveals no structural abnormalities. The heart shows normal d-looping with normal systemic and pulmonary venous connections. Left and right ventricular chamber dimensions and systolic functional parameters are completely normal. No intracardiac shunts, valvular stenoses, or regurgitant lesions are identified on real-time cine sequences.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI. Completely preserved bi-ventricular systolic function and normal anatomy without evidence of congenital anomalies or myocardial scar tissue.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates normal, age-appropriate brain maturation. The sulcation and gyration patterns, including deep secondary and tertiary sulci, are highly appropriate for 34 weeks. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with atrial diameters measuring 6.1 mm and 5.9 mm on the left and right, respectively. The corpus callosum, brainstem, cerebellum, and orbits are within normal limits. The fetal chest and abdomen are also unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI study demonstrating excellent, age-appropriate structural brain maturation at 34 weeks of gestation.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates an open lumbosacral neural tube defect extending from L4 to S2, with herniation of the meninges and neural elements. There is associated Chiari II malformation, characterized by herniation of the cerebellum and brainstem through the foramen magnum. The lateral ventricles show a 'lemon' sign skull deformity and 'banana' sign cerebellum, with ventricular atrial widths of 11.2 mm.

Sulcation is normal for 23 weeks gestation. Impression: Open lumbosacral myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation.

Brain MRI reveals flattening of the posterior sclera bilaterally, prominent fluid surrounding the optic nerves within the optic sheaths, and mild empty sella turcica. There are no space-occupying lesions, venous sinus thromboses, or intracranial hemorrhages. The cerebral ventricles are somewhat narrow but remain within normal physiological limits.

Impression: Radiographic findings of bilateral optic nerve sheath distension, posterior scleral flattening, and empty sella, which are highly suggestive of idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri). Correlation with clinical lumbar puncture opening pressure is advised.

Cardiac MRI shows marked right ventricular dilation with an end-diastolic volume index of 134 mL/m² and regional areas of dyskinesis and microaneurysm formation along the right ventricular free wall and outflow tract. Right ventricular ejection fraction is significantly reduced at 35%. T1-weighted imaging and late gadolinium enhancement demonstrate patchy transmural fibrosis and fat infiltration within the right ventricular free wall.

Impression: Structural and functional abnormalities of the right ventricle meeting major diagnostic task force criteria for Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC).

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal structural development. The fetal brain exhibits symmetric cerebral hemispheres with an age-appropriate sulcul pattern. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with symmetric atria measuring 6.3 mm. The cerebellar vermis, brainstem, and posterior fossa structures are normal.

All fetal somatic structures, including the spine, heart, lungs, stomach, and kidneys, are normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating completely appropriate intracranial development and normal somatic anatomy at 28 weeks gestation.

Multiplanar cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac chamber morphology and size. Left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 62%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of myocardial edema are identified on cine or T2-weighted imaging. Late gadolinium enhancement is absent. The thoracic aorta is normal in caliber.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal biventricular size and function, and no evidence of myocardial scar or active inflammation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe apical displacement of the septal and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve, measuring 29 mm/m² body surface area relative to the mitral annulus. This results in a large 'atrialized' portion of the right ventricle. The functional right ventricle is small, showing moderately reduced systolic function. Real-time imaging reveals severe tricuspid regurgitation, and the right atrium is massively dilated.

Impression: Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve with significant apical displacement, severe tricuspid regurgitation, and severe right atrial dilation. Left ventricular function is normal (LVEF 61%).

Cardiac MRI shows severe dilation of the left ventricle with an indexed end-diastolic volume of 138 mL/m². There is global hypokinesis of the left ventricular free wall with thin myocardial segments. Diffuse, mid-wall linear late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed in the interventricular septum, characteristic of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. The right ventricle appears normal in size and function.

Impression: Severe dilated cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction of 28%) and associated mid-wall myocardial scarring.

Brain MRI shows multiple subependymal nodules lining the lateral ventricles, some of which demonstrate signal drop-out on susceptibility-weighted imaging, indicating calcification. Additionally, cortical and subcortical tubers are visible in the bilateral frontal and parietal lobes. No large mass at the foramen of Monro is visualized.

Impression: Intracranial findings are highly consistent with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. No evidence of a subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) or acute obstructive hydrocephalus at this time.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe mitral valve prolapse of the anterior and posterior leaflets into the left atrium during systole. Phase-contrast flow analysis reveals severe, eccentric mitral regurgitation with a calculated regurgitant volume of 45 mL and a regurgitant fraction of 41%. The left atrium and left ventricle are moderately dilated, demonstrating volume overload with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 118 mL/m².

Left ventricular systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 64% (hyperdynamic). No areas of late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) are identified within the left ventricular myocardium or papillary muscles. Impression: Severe mitral valve prolapse with severe mitral regurgitation and secondary left-sided chamber volume overload. Suggest clinical correlation for valve repair.

Cardiac MRI performed for evaluation of atypical chest pain during exertion. Evaluation of cardiac chambers demonstrates normal cardiac anatomy with normal chambers sizes and wall thickness. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVI) is 74 mL/m2. Left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 65% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 61%. No evidence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging or late gadolinium enhancement to suggest myocardial scar or fibrosis. Visualized coronary artery origins from the aortic root are normal.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular size and function with no evidence of structural heart disease, myocarditis, or anomalous coronary origins.

The study reveals normal cardiac situs and normal d-looped ventricles. Great vessel relationships are normal, with the aorta arising from the left ventricle and the pulmonary trunk from the right ventricle. Myocardial T1 and T2 mapping parameters are within the normal pediatric reference range. No focal late gadolinium enhancement is identified.

Impression: Completely normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No congenital abnormalities, shunt pathways, valvular dysfunction, or myocardial tissue abnormalities are identified. Biventricular function is normal.

Cardiac MRI reveals normal cardiac chamber configuration, normal wall thickness, and fully preserved global and regional ventricular performance. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There are no features of late gadolinium enhancement, and phase contrast flow profiles of the great vessels are normal.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI study. No pathological structural or tissue anomalies are seen.

Cardiac MR imaging displays normal chamber dimensions, but there is global hypokinesis of the left ventricle with a depressed ejection fraction of 44%. T2-weighted triple inversion recovery sequences demonstrate diffuse hyperintensity of the left ventricular free wall, indicative of myocardial edema. Post-contrast late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) images show patchy, subepicardial to mid-myocardial enhancement along the lateral and apical walls, adhering to a non-ischemic distribution pattern.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with acute myocarditis, satisfying the updated Lake Louise criteria with evidence of both myocardial edema and non-ischemic late gadolinium enhancement. Depressed left ventricular systolic function is noted.

Cerebellar tonsils are herniated approximately 7.5 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The third, fourth, and lateral ventricles are normal in size and configuration, with no evidence of hydrocephalus. The cervical spine was partially visualized and shows no evidence of syringomyelia on sagittal T2-weighted sequences.

Impression: Chiari I malformation without associated ventriculomegaly or cervical syrinx.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates semilobar holoprosencephaly. There is partial separation of the cerebral hemispheres posteriorly, but the frontal lobes and thalami are fused. A single, large monoventricle is present anteriorly, with a thin mantle of surrounding cortex. The corpus callosum is absent. Facial structures appear intact. Supratentorial ventricular spaces are dilated.

Impression: Semilobar holoprosencephaly with fused thalami and anterior monoventricle at 31 weeks gestation.

Evaluation for coronary anomalies following Kawasaki disease. Cardiac MRI demonstrates giant aneurysmal dilation of both the left main coronary artery (measuring 7.2 mm in diameter) and the proximal right coronary artery (measuring 6.5 mm in diameter). There is no evidence of luminal thrombus or stenosis. Myocardial perfusion imaging shows no inducible perfusion defects during stress, and no late gadolinium enhancement is present.

Impression: Giant coronary artery aneurysms of the left main and proximal right coronary arteries, consistent with sequelae of Kawasaki disease. Normal global left ventricular function (LVEF 63%) and no evidence of myocardial ischemia or infarction.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a moderate to large, circumferential pericardial effusion, which measures up to 18 mm in thickness adjacent to the right atrium and 15 mm adjacent to the left ventricular apex. Despite the size of the effusion, there is no evidence of diastolic collapse of the right atrium or right ventricle to suggest tamponade physiology on cine sequences. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 58%, and there is no myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement to suggest associated myocarditis.

Impression: Moderate to large circumferential pericardial effusion without MR evidence of cardiac tamponade. The underlying myocardium is normal in size, function, and tissue characteristics.

MR brain study shows severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with a rotated remnant. There is cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle filling the posterior fossa, which is significantly enlarged, elevating the tentorium cerebelli and transverse sinuses. Moderate bilateral lateral ventriculomegaly is noted with rounding of the frontal horns.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation. Associated ventriculomegaly is present, requiring clinical correlation and neurosurgical follow-up.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates severe oligohydramnios, making fetal positioning compressed. Fetal renal fossae are empty bilaterally, and there is no evidence of renal parenchyma or renal arteries on heavily T2-weighted or MR angiography sequences. The fetal urinary bladder is persistently collapsed and not visualized. The fetal lungs are severely hypoplastic, with volumes well below the 5th percentile.

Impression: Classic Potter sequence secondary to bilateral renal agenesis. Severely hypoplastic lungs and profound oligohydramnios are noted.

Normal pediatric cardiac MRI. The study reveals excellent biventricular anatomy, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 64% and right ventricular ejection fraction of 60%. Myocardial wall thicknesses are normal, with no evidence of hypertrophy. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging is completely negative for scarring, and T2 mapping shows no active inflammation.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, or congenital structural anomalies.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates severe micromelia, with all visualized fetal long bones measuring more than 4 standard deviations below the mean for gestational age. The ribs are severely shortened, leading to a narrow, bell-shaped thorax. Prominent pulmonary hypoplasia is noted bilaterally. The skull is relatively large and shows frontal bossing.

No cranial sutural fusion is present. Ventricles and sulcation are normal. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, most consistent with Thanatophoric Dysplasia, with secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MR demonstrates mild global hypokinesia of the left ventricle with a mildly reduced ejection fraction of 48%. T2-weighted and T2-mapping sequences show patchy areas of high signal intensity in the subepicardial region of the lateral and basal free wall, indicating localized myocardial edema. Following administration of gadolinium contrast, there is pronounced, non-ischemic late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) in a mid-myocardial and subepicardial distribution within the basal-to-mid lateral wall, sparing the subendocardium.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of acute myocarditis based on modified Lake Louise criteria, demonstrating both myocardial edema and non-ischemic late gadolinium enhancement. Mildly depressed left ventricular systolic function with trace pericardial effusion is also noted.

Brain MRI of this 3-month-old infant demonstrates complete absence of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles are widely separated and demonstrate a parallel orientation, resulting in a characteristic 'steer-horn' appearance on coronal views, along with dilation of the occipital horns (colpocephaly). The third ventricle is high-riding and mildly dilated.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly. No other major focal cortical developmental migrations abnormalities are resolved on the current scan.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates entirely normal anatomical development. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit age-appropriate sulcal patterns, with clear definition of the parieto-occipital sulcus and cingulate sulcus. The lateral ventricular atria measure 5.9 mm symmetrically, with no intraventricular fluid collections or other signs of distress. The cerebellum and brainstem are structurally intact.

No chest, abdominal, or spinal abnormalities are visualized. Amniotic fluid volume is physiologic. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study, demonstrating appropriate structural development and normal brain anatomy at 29 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal intracranial anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate, age-expected smooth sulcation and migration patterns. The lateral ventricles are normal in size, with the atrial width measuring 5.8 mm. The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, are morphologically unremarkable.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing completely age-appropriate brain development and normal ventricular calibers at 22 weeks gestation.

Three-dimensional magnetic resonance angiography of the thoracic aorta demonstrates a severe juxtaductal coarctation of the aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The narrowest segment measures approximately 4.5 mm in diameter, with a significant post-stenotic dilation of the descending aorta. Extensive collateral vessel development is noted along the internal mammary and intercostal arteries. The left ventricle demonstrates moderate concentric hypertrophy with an end-diastolic septal thickness of 11 mm.

Impression: Severe juxtaductal coarctation of the aorta with prominent collateral circulation and compensatory concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 59%.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate atypical, non-exertional chest pain and palpitations. Quantitative cine analysis demonstrates normal left and right ventricular chamber dimensions and preserved global systolic function, with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 62% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 58%. There are no regional wall motion abnormalities, and myocardial signal intensity is completely uniform on T1, T2, and post-contrast late gadolinium enhancement sequences.

Impression: Completely normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No structural heart disease, anomalous coronary anatomy, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement is identified.

Cardiac and aortic MR angiography demonstrates a discrete narrowing of the distal aortic arch just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, measuring 7.5 mm in diameter compared to the adjacent descending aorta measuring 14 mm. Prominent collateral arteries are visualized arising from the internal mammary and intercostal arteries. The left ventricular mass is moderately increased at 88 g/m2, representing concentric LV hypertrophy. The left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 60%.

Impression: Discrete coarctation of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with evidence of extensive collateralization. Associated mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is present, but global systolic function remains preserved.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates global dilation of the right ventricle with an indexed end-diastolic volume of 122 mL/m2. Right ventricular ejection fraction is severely depressed at 34%. There are regional wall motion abnormalities consisting of dyskinesia and microaneurysms in the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) and apex. T1-weighted imaging and late gadolinium enhancement show focal fatty infiltration and transmural fibrous replacement in the RV free wall. The left ventricle is normal in size and function (LVEF 58%).

Impression: Right ventricular dilation, severe dysfunction, regional dyskinesia, and myocardial replacement fibrosis meeting major Task Force criteria for Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC).

ECG-gated cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate for cardiomyopathy in a patient with a family history. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 114 mL with an ejection fraction of 65%. Right ventricular end-diastolic volume is 118 mL with an ejection fraction of 61%. No myocardial edema is identified on T2-weighted sequences, and late gadolinium enhancement imaging is completely negative for myocardial fibrosis. Normal morphology of all cardiac valves is demonstrated.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of cardiomyopathy, myocardial scar, or structural congenital heart disease.

MRI of the brain using high-resolution epilepsy sequences demonstrates symmetric hippocampal volumes and signal intensities. The temporal lobes are structurally normal, with no evidence of mesial temporal sclerosis or cortical developmental malformations. The remaining cerebral lobes, ventricles, and extra-axial spaces are normal. The major intracranial arterial flow voids are intact.

Impression: Unremarkable high-resolution brain MRI. No structural etiology or epileptogenic focus identified to correlate with the patient's recent onset of absence seizures.

MR imaging of the brain was completed under anesthesia using dedicated pediatric protocols. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal gray-white matter differentiation and normal sulcal patterns for age. There are no focal parenchymal signal abnormalities, mass lesions, or areas of restricted diffusion. Ventricles and cisterns are unremarkable, with normal flow voids.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No structural abnormality, migration defect, or evidence of focal cortical dysplasia to explain new-onset focal seizures.

MR imaging of the brain was obtained to evaluate new-onset focal seizures. Sequences demonstrate completely normal cortical thickness and sulcal patterning throughout both hemispheres. The hippocampal formations are symmetric in size and morphology, showing normal internal architecture and signal characteristics. No focal cortical dysplasia, vascular malformations, or heterotopias are identified.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural epileptogenic substrate or intracranial abnormality is identified on this study.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates significant dilation of the lateral ventricles. The left ventricular atrium measures 14.5 mm, and the right lateral ventricular atrium measures 13.8 mm, indicating moderate-to-severe ventriculomegaly. The sulcation pattern of the cerebral cortex is slightly delayed but still within acceptable limits for 28 weeks. The corpus callosum is present and intact, and no additional intracranial masses or hemorrhages are identified.

Impression: Moderate-to-severe bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. Close monitoring with serial ultrasounds and postnatal neurosurgical follow-up are recommended.

A comprehensive pediatric cardiac magnetic resonance imaging study was performed utilizing cine bSSFP, phase-contrast, and late gadolinium enhancement sequences. The left and right ventricular chambers demonstrate completely normal volumes, wall thickness, and global systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormalities, myocardial edema, or pathological late gadolinium enhancement.

All cardiac valves exhibit normal morphology and excursion, without evidence of stenosis or regurgitation. The thoracic aorta and pulmonary trunk are normal in caliber. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study with no structural or functional cardiovascular abnormalities identified.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniation of the right hepatic lobe, gallbladder, and loops of bowel is visualized within the right hemithorax. This causes severe leftward shift of the mediastinum and compression of the left lung. The total fetal lung volume is severely decreased, estimated at 28% of expected, indicating high risk for pulmonary hypoplasia.

Intracranial anatomy is intact with normal ventricular atria measuring 6.0 mm. Sulcation is appropriate for 33 weeks gestation. Impression: Severe right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniated into the thorax, severe lung hypoplasia, and mediastinal shift.

Magnetic resonance angiography and cardiac cine imaging reveal a focal, severe narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The minimum internal diameter at the coarctation site measures 6.5 mm, with prominent collateral vessels originating from the internal mammary and intercostal arteries. Left ventricular mass index is elevated at 92 g/m2, indicative of concentric concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 68%.

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the thoracic aorta with significant collateral vascularization and associated left ventricular hypertrophy. Recommend pediatric cardiothoracic surgery intervention.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated severe bilateral ventriculomegaly. The lateral ventricular atria measure 16.5 mm on the left and 15.9 mm on the right, presenting a marked colpocephalic configuration. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and dilated. Cortical sulcation is mildly delayed, approximating a 26-week appearance.

No other intracranial abnormalities or migrational disorders are visualized. The spine and major fetal organs are structurally normal. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with severe bilateral colpocephaly/ventriculomegaly and mild cortical sulcation delay.

High-resolution cardiac MRI evaluation demonstrates a structurally normal heart. Cardiac chambers are normal in size without hypertrophy. The coronary ostia arise normally from the left and right sinuses of Valsalva. Wall motion of both ventricles is normal, with an LV ejection fraction of 61% and an RV ejection fraction of 57%. No late gadolinium enhancement is identified.

Impression: Structurally and functionally normal cardiac MRI. No congenital abnormalities or myocardial pathology detected.

Cardiac MRI evaluating an 18-year-old male presenting with acute chest pain, elevated troponins, and diffuse ST-segment elevations. T2-weighted imaging and T2 mapping show focal hyperintensity in the lateral and inferolateral free walls of the left ventricle, indicating myocardial edema. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals patchy, subepicardial-to-midwall enhancement involving the same lateral and inferolateral segments, which is non-ischemic in distribution. Global left ventricular systolic function is mildly depressed with an ejection fraction of 48%.

Impression: Acute myocarditis involving the lateral and inferolateral left ventricular wall based on classic Lake Louise criteria (myocardial edema and subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement). Mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction is present.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 16-year-old male with hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) who has completed the third-stage Fontan palliation. Phase-contrast flow imaging demonstrates a patent, widely caliber lateral tunnel Fontan pathway with laminar blood flow and no focal stenosis. The systemic right ventricle is moderately dilated, exhibiting mildly reduced global systolic function with an ejection fraction of 44%. There is trace-to-mild systemic tricuspid valve regurgitation. No significant thrombi or filling defects are identified in the Fontan circuit.

Impression: Post-Fontan hypoplastic left heart syndrome. Stable systemic right ventricle showing mild dilation and mildly reduced systolic function. No obstruction or thrombus within the Fontan pathway.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates abnormal morphology of the left kidney, which is enlarged and entirely replaced by multiple non-communicating cysts of varying sizes, the largest measuring 2.4 cm. There is no identifiable normal renal parenchyma on the left. The right kidney is normal in position and structure, demonstrating mild compensatory hypertrophy (measuring 4.5 cm in craniocaudal length). Amniotic fluid volume is normal.

Impression: Unilateral left multicystic dysplastic kidney with a normal, compensating right kidney. Normal amniotic fluid level suggests preserved total renal function.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates cerebellar vermian hypoplasia. There is keyhole-like communication between the fourth ventricle and the cisterna magna, though the posterior fossa is not significantly enlarged. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits (atrial width 7.4 mm). Cerebral sulcation is appropriate for 28 weeks.

Impression: Cerebellar vermian hypoplasia consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant.

Multiplanar brain MRI demonstrates a well-defined extra-axial fluid collection in the left middle cranial fossa, measuring approximately 4.5 x 3.0 x 2.5 cm. The collection is homogeneous and follows CSF signal on all sequences (T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI). There is mild remodeling of the adjacent sphenoid wing and temporal bone, but no significant mass effect or midline shift.

Impression: Large, benign-appearing left temporal arachnoid cyst (Galassi Type II) with minimal adjacent mass effect and no evidence of hemorrhage or rupture.

Cardiac MRI assessment shows normal myocardial anatomy and biventricular function. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. The ventricular septum is intact, the atrial septum is unremarkable, and all four heart valves demonstrate normal morphology and competent closure without stenosis or regurgitation. T1/T2 mapping and late gadolinium enhancement sequences are normal.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No structural congenital anomalies or signs of cardiomyopathy.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomical development. The cerebral cortex shows well-defined, age-appropriate sulcation patterns, including deep central, parieto-occipital, and calcarine sulci. The lateral ventricles are symmetric with ventricular atrial measurements of 5.8 mm on the left and 6.0 mm on the right. The corpus callosum is well-visualized, demonstrating normal thick segment development from rostrum to splenium.

The fetal visceral organs, diaphragm, and skeletal structures are normal. No signs of fetal hydrops are detected. Impression: Normal fetal brain and body MRI at 32 weeks gestation, showing expected development and normal ventricular sizes.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation. The cerebral cortex demonstrates advanced, age-appropriate sulcation with well-defined central, precentral, and postcentral sulci, along with secondary sulcation patterns expected for late third trimester. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and normal in caliber, with atrial measurements of 5.1 mm on the left and 4.9 mm on the right. The corpus callosum, cerebellar vermis, and brainstem are completely intact and structurally normal. Visualized fetal thoracic and abdominal viscera are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation. Intracranial structural development, ventricles, and sulcation patterns are entirely normal and appropriate for gestational age.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed using multiplanar, multisequence protocols. Brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity and morphology without evidence of acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or mass effect. Ventricles, sulci, and extra-axial CSF spaces are within normal limits for patient age. The brainstem and cerebellum are unremarkable, and vascular flow voids are normal.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No structural abnormality, mass lesion, or demyelinating process identified to explain chronic migraine symptoms.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 22 weeks gestation shows a marked anatomical abnormality of the posterior fossa. There is severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with a huge, fluid-filled cystic structure in the posterior fossa that communicates widely with the enlarged fourth ventricle. The tentorium cerebelli and torcula are elevated, demonstrating classic torcular-lambdoid inversion. Supratentorial ventricular caliber remains normal with atrial width measuring 7.1 mm.

Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation. Normal supratentorial brain development, but marked posterior fossa cystic distension and vermian hypoplasia. Counseling regarding developmental expectations is advised.

MR brain imaging reveals multiple cortical tubers demonstrating high T2/FLAIR signal intensity scattered across the cerebral hemispheres. In addition, there are several small, subependymal nodules lining the lateral ventricles, some of which demonstrate susceptibility artifact consistent with calcification. No enhancing subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) is identified at the foramina of Monro.

Impression: Intracranial features of tuberous sclerosis complex, including multiple cortical tubers and subependymal nodules. No evidence of a subependymal giant cell astrocytoma or ventricular obstruction.

Evaluation of a secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD). The defect measures 14 mm in diameter, demonstrating a significant left-to-right shunt with a measured Qp/Qs ratio of 1.9. This has resulted in moderate volume overload, with dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle. Biventricular systolic function is preserved (RVEF 57%, LVEF 62%).

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt and secondary right-sided heart dilation.

A lobulated, cystic and solid suprasellar mass is identified, measuring 2.4 x 2.2 x 2.0 cm. The solid component demonstrates vivid enhancement and peripheral calcifications are noted on the susceptibility sequences. The mass exerts pressure upwards on the optic chiasm, which is superiorly displaced and flattened, and causes mild indentation of the third ventricle.

Impression: Suprasellar cystic-solid mass, highly characteristic of an adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma. Optic chiasm compression is noted, requiring ophthalmological evaluation and neurosurgical consultation.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates a large occipital encephalocele. There is a defect in the occipital bone with herniation of a meningeal sac containing a small amount of dysplastic cerebellar tissue. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with atrial measurements of 12.1 mm. The cortical sulcation pattern is simplified but within normal variations for 27 weeks.

The remainder of the spine and intracranial anatomy is unremarkable. Impression: Occipital encephalocele containing meninges and dysplastic neural tissue, with mild-to-moderate associated ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly with dilation of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles, with atrial widths measuring 11.8 mm on the left and 12.1 mm on the right. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and dilated, and the lateral ventricles are widely spaced and run parallel to each other. Interhemispheric sulcation shows a radial pattern pointing towards the third ventricular roof, confirming the absence of the callosal band.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild bilateral colpocephaly. No other intracranial anomalies or extra-axial fluid collections identified.

Brain MRI utilizing a dedicated pediatric epilepsy protocol was performed. There is symmetric development of the hippocampus and parahippocampal gyri with normal internal architecture and signal intensity on coronal T2 and FLAIR sequences. Cortical gray matter thickness, sulcation, and gray-white matter junctions are completely normal. No focal lesions or abnormal enhancement are visualized.

Impression: Normal brain MRI with no structural epileptogenic focus identified, specifically demonstrating symmetric and structurally normal hippocampi.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 24 weeks gestation reveals normal intracranial anatomy and development. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate sulcation and migration patterns for the stated gestational age. The ventricular system is normal in size and morphology, with the lateral ventricular atrial width measuring 5.8 mm bilaterally. The corpus callosum is fully visualized and structurally intact, and the posterior fossa structures are normal.

Fetal chest, abdomen, spine, and extremities are grossly intact without visible structural abnormalities. No extra-axial fluid collections or fetal anomalies are visualized. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural and neurological development.

MRI of the brain and orbits reveals completely normal brain parenchyma without mass, ischemia, or hemorrhage. The optic chiasm, optic tracts, and intraorbital segments of the optic nerves are symmetric, showing normal signal intensity and caliber. The cerebrospinal fluid space surrounding the optic nerves is within normal limits, and the pituitary gland is unremarkable.

Impression: Normal brain and orbital MRI. No structural etiology identified to explain the patient's visual symptoms.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate for acute myocarditis following a recent viral prodrome. T2-weighted and T2-mapping sequences demonstrate focal areas of increased signal intensity/edema within the epicardial-to-midmyocardial regions of the lateral and anterolateral left ventricular walls. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) images confirm patchy, non-ischemic epicardial and mid-myocardial enhancement in the same regions, satisfying the updated Lake Louise criteria.

Impression: MRI findings are highly suggestive of acute active myocarditis with localized myocardial edema and associated epicardial late gadolinium enhancement. Left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly depressed at 52%.

Brain MRI demonstrates multiple, bilateral, asymmetric areas of increased T2/FLAIR signal intensity involving the subcortical white matter, deep gray matter, and brainstem. Several of these lesions show faint, incomplete ring-like or nodular enhancement patterns following gadolinium administration. No evidence of mass effect, hemorrhagic transformation, or main vessel occlusion is seen.

Impression: Multifocal demyelinating lesions. In a pediatric patient post-viral infection, this appearance is highly suggestive of Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM).

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation reveals a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. There is herniation of the stomach, several loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left lobe of the liver into the left thoracic cavity. This results in severe rightward mediastinal shift and compression of the developing lungs. The observed-to-expected total lung volume is calculated at 42%, indicating moderate pulmonary hypoplasia.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver-up component and associated moderate lung hypoplasia. Multi-disciplinary prenatal counseling is recommended.

Cardiac MRI of a 7-year-old child demonstrates normal myocardial architecture, normal chamber sizes, and intact cardiac valves. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities are present. Delayed contrast-enhanced imaging is negative for myocardial scar or fibrosis. T2 weighted images demonstrate no evidence of edema.

Impression: Completely normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No structural, congenital, or inflammatory anomalies identified.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows normal, symmetric intracranial structures. The atrial widths of the lateral ventricles are 5.9 mm. The corpus callosum is intact and appropriate for gestational age. The brainstem and cerebellum are completely normal with no mass effect or fluid collections. Sulcation is within normal limits.

Fetal chest, heart, abdominal organs, and spine are normal. No fetal anomalies are detected. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large, solid mass centered within the fourth ventricle measuring approximately 3.8 x 3.6 x 3.5 cm. The lesion shows heterogeneous enhancement following contrast administration and restricts diffusion on DWI sequences. Marked mass effect is noted on the brainstem and cerebellar vermis, resulting in obstruction of CSF outflow and moderate-to-severe dilatation of the lateral and third ventricles with transependymal flow.

Impression: Large fourth ventricular mass causing obstructive hydrocephalus, most consistent with a medulloblastoma or ependymoma. Emergent neurosurgical referral is indicated.

Cardiac MRI of a 3-month-old infant demonstrates both the aorta and the pulmonary artery arising almost entirely from the morphologic right ventricle, consistent with a double outlet right ventricle (DORV). A large, subaortic ventricular septal defect (VSD) is noted. There is mild stenosis of the pulmonary valve with a peak systolic gradient across the RVOT of 20 mmHg. Biventricular function is globally preserved.

Impression: Double outlet right ventricle with a large subaortic VSD and mild pulmonary valve stenosis.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal septal thickness measuring 22 mm at the mid-ventricular level. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve leading to moderate eccentric mitral regurgitation and dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals patchy intramyocardial hyperenhancement within the hypertrophied septal segments.

Impression: Severe asymmetric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with LVOT obstruction and patchy myocardial fibrosis. Ejection fraction remains hyperdynamic at 75%.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of the left kidney in the left renal fossa. The right kidney is present and measures larger than expected (compensatory hypertrophy), showing normal signal intensity. Normal amniotic fluid index is present, suggesting adequate renal function from the single kidney.

Fetal brain shows advanced sulcation patterns appropriate for 31 weeks. The lateral ventricular atrium is normal at 6.3 mm. Impression: Congenital left unilateral renal agenesis with compensatory right renal hypertrophy. Amniotic fluid volume is normal.

Brain MR evaluation reveals severe, symmetric dilation of both lateral ventricles and the third ventricle. The fourth ventricle is normal in caliber. Marked thinning of the surrounding cerebral cortex and stretching of the corpus callosum are present. Faint periventricular FLAIR/T2 hyperintensity suggests transependymal flow of cerebrospinal fluid.

Impression: Congenital obstructive hydrocephalus secondary to aqueductal stenosis. Urgent neurosurgical consultation is recommended for cerebrospinal fluid diversion.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach, several loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe are herniated into the left hemithorax. This has resulted in a severe contralateral mediastinal shift to the right, with marked compression of the right lung. The total fetal lung volume is significantly reduced, indicating severe pulmonary hypoplasia. Intracranial structures demonstrate normal sulcal progression and normal ventricles measuring 5.5 mm.

Impression: Severe left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant intrathoracic herniation of abdominal viscera and secondary bilateral lung hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI performed for further assessment of an equivocal pediatric echocardiogram. The study demonstrates entirely normal cardiac chamber sizes, wall thickness, and ventricular function (LVEF 63%, RVEF 59%). There is no evidence of intracardiac shunts, valvular dysfunction, or myocardial scar. The thoracic aorta and pulmonary vasculature are normal in size and course.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular size and function, with no evidence of structural or functional cardiovascular pathology.

Follow-up brain MRI shows completely resolved leptomeningeal enhancement compared to the prior examination 6 months ago. The brain parenchyma is normal with no areas of focal restricted diffusion or chronic gliosis. The ventricular system and extra-axial CSF spaces are unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain demonstrating complete resolution of previously documented leptomeningeal enhancement. No chronic sequelae of prior meningitis.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed to evaluate persistent non-specific dizziness. Visualized intracranial structures demonstrate normal morphological characteristics for the patient's age. The ventricular chambers, sulcal markings, and basal cisterns are completely normal in size and appearance. No evidence of restricted diffusion, intracranial mass, hemorrhage, or abnormal tissue enhancement is noted.

Impression: Unremarkable and normal brain MRI. No structural abnormality, extra-axial collection, or vascular anomaly is identified to account for symptoms.

Brain MRI demonstrates multiple, bilateral, asymmetric, poorly-demarcated areas of high T2/FLAIR signal intensity within the subcortical and deep white matter, basal ganglia, and brainstem. Some of these lesions display faint, incomplete ring-like enhancement on post-contrast imaging. No mass effect or significant surrounding vasogenic edema is present, and there is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage.

Impression: Diffuse, multifocal demyelinating-appearing lesions in a pediatric patient, highly suggestive of acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM), particularly if preceded by a viral illness or vaccination. Clinical and biochemical correlation recommended.

Cardiac MRI of a 2-year-old male demonstrates anatomical alignment of the great vessels and intact septal structures. Ventricular volumes are normal for the child's body surface area. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 65%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 62%.

No abnormal myocardial edema, perfusion defects, or late gadolinium enhancement is visualized. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study showing preserved biventricular systolic function and no congenital anomalies.

Cardiac MRI evaluates status post-surgical repair of Tetralogy of Fallot. There is significant dilation of the right ventricle, with a right ventricular end-diastolic volume index (RVEDVI) calculated at 162 ml/m2. Phase-contrast imaging of the main pulmonary artery demonstrates severe pulmonary regurgitation, with a regurgitant fraction of 44%. The right ventricular outflow tract is patent but dilated, without focal stenosis.

Right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 45%. The left ventricle is normal in size with preserved systolic function (EF 59%). Impression: Status post Tetralogy of Fallot repair with severe pulmonary regurgitation and moderate-to-severe right ventricular dilation, indicating potential candidacy for pulmonary valve replacement.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates severe shortening and bowing of all long bones, consistent with a rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia. The femur and humerus lengths are significantly below the 5th percentile for gestational age. The thorax is remarkably narrow and bell-shaped, indicating pulmonary hypoplasia. 

Intracranial anatomy, however, is structurally normal for 27 weeks, with age-appropriate sulcation and symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 5.9 mm at the atrium. Impression: Skeletal dysplasia with severe micromelia and thoracic narrowing, raising concern for a lethal form of skeletal dysplasia. Genetic evaluation is recommended.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 19 mm adjacent to the right ventricle and apex. Real-time cine imaging shows evidence of early diastolic collapse of the right ventricular free wall, indicative of tamponade physiology. The myocardium itself exhibits normal signal intensity, wall thickness, and overall contractility, with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 64%.

Impression: Large circumferential pericardial effusion with signs of early hemodynamic compromise (early tamponade physiology). The myocardium is uninvolved with normal biventricular function and no signs of acute myocarditis.

A cardiac MRI is obtained for a 10-year-old female presenting with dyspnea, muffled heart sounds, and elevated inflammatory markers. There is a large, circumferential pericardial effusion, which measures up to 18 mm along the left ventricular free wall and 15 mm adjacent to the right atrium. Diastolic flattening and early collapse of the right atrium are noted, indicating elevated intrapericardial pressures and early hemodynamic compromise. Left and right ventricular systolic functions are normal (LVEF 60%, RVEF 55%).

No evidence of underlying myocardial inflammation or thickening is seen on T2-weighted or late gadolinium enhancement sequences. Impression: Large circumferential pericardial effusion with MRI findings suggestive of early tamponade physiology. Clinical correlation is advised for immediate therapeutic intervention.

MRI of the brain was completed for structural evaluation in a 1-year-old female presenting with global developmental delay. High-resolution imaging demonstrates symmetric, normal progression of myelination appropriate for age. The corpus callosum is intact, showing normal morphology. No structural abnormalities, migration defects, cortical gyration errors, or ventriculomegaly are noted.

Impression: Normal brain MRI for a 1-year-old child. No structural, ischemic, or metabolic/demyelinating anomalies identified to account for global developmental delay.

Cardiac MR assessment reveals normal cardiac anatomy and function. The systemic and pulmonary venous connections are intact, and the ventricular septum is entirely intact with no evidence of shunt. Both right and left ventricles demonstrate normal size, thickness, and systolic function (LVEF 64%, RVEF 61%). The thoracic aorta is structurally normal and left-sided.

Impression: Unremarkable and completely normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No congenital or acquired heart disease identified.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach and several small bowel loops have herniated into the left hemithorax, resulting in a severe mass effect with rightward shift of the mediastinum and heart. The left lung is severely compressed and barely visible, while the right lung is moderately hypoplastic. The fetal lung volume (FLV) is calculated and falls below the 25th percentile for gestational age.

Intracranial anatomy is normal; the ventricles are symmetric with atrial measurements of 6.2 mm. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant mediastinal shift and pulmonary hypoplasia. Recommend multidisciplinary prenatal counseling with pediatric surgery and neonatologists.

Brain MRI of this 8-month-old infant demonstrates a focal area of cortical thickening and blurred gray-white matter junction within the posterior aspect of the right frontal lobe. T2/FLAIR hyperintensity is noted extending from the subcortical white matter toward the lateral ventricle, displaying a 'transmantle sign.' The remainder of the myelination is age-appropriate and ventricles are of normal caliber.

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia within the right frontal lobe, a common pathological substrate for focal epilepsy in infants. Recommend clinical correlation with electroencephalographic (EEG) localization.

MR study of the brain reveals cerebellar tonsillar ectopia, with the cerebellar tonsils herniating approximately 7.5 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. There is crowding of the craniocervical junction with effacement of the surrounding CSF spaces. Phase-contrast CSF flow studies demonstrate diminished CSF flow velocity posteriorly at the level of the foramen magnum. The remainder of the brain parenchymal structures and ventricles are normal. No evidence of cervical syringomyelia is observed on the visualized upper cervical spine.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with associated CSF flow restriction at the craniocervical junction. No spinal cord syrinx detected within the visualized cervical segment.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 13.5 mm in its maximum diameter. There is significant dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, with the right ventricular end-diastolic volume index measuring 118 ml/m². Phase-contrast flow analysis indicates a substantial left-to-right shunt with a Qp/Qs ratio of 1.95.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with significant right-sided volume overload and a highly elevated shunt fraction (Qp/Qs = 1.95). Biventricular systolic function is preserved.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation shows normal cerebral operculization and age-appropriate secondary sulcation. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits (6.2 mm). However, examination of the left retroperitoneum reveals that the left kidney is replaced by multiple large, thin-walled, non-communicating cysts, with no visible normal renal parenchyma, consistent with multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK).

The right kidney is normal in size and appearance, and there is a normal bladder and amniotic fluid volume. Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The contralateral kidney is completely normal and amniotic fluid volume is preserved, suggesting adequate overall renal function.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates asymmetric dilation of the lateral ventricles. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 14.2 mm, indicating moderate ventriculomegaly, while the right lateral ventricle measures 9.5 mm. No intraventricular hemorrhage or aqueductal stenosis is identified. The corpus callosum is present and shows normal morphology, and the cerebral cortex exhibits appropriate sulcation for 26 weeks gestation.

The thoracic, abdominal, and spinal structures are grossly normal. Impression: Unilateral left-sided moderate ventriculomegaly. Close prenatal ultrasound surveillance is recommended to monitor ventricular size.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates a markedly distended fetal urinary bladder (megacystis) with bilateral severe hydroureteronephrosis. The renal parenchyma is thin bilaterally with increased T2 signal, suggestive of dysplastic changes. The amniotic fluid volume is significantly reduced (oligohydramnios). The intracranial structures are normal, with mature sulcal patterns appropriate for 34 weeks gestation, and the ventricular atrium measures 5.8 mm.

The thoracic cavity is mildly compressed, suggesting secondary risk for pulmonary hypoplasia. Impression: Severe fetal megacystis with bilateral hydroureteronephrosis and oligohydramnios, highly consistent with posterior urethral valves (PUV) and secondary renal dysplasia.

Post-Fontan status evaluation of a child with hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) demonstrates patent Fontan pathway/conduit with laminar flow and no evidence of thrombosis or narrowing. The systemic right ventricle is moderately dilated with mild global hypokinesia, demonstrating an ejection fraction of 44%. Mild-to-moderate atrioventricular valve regurgitation is noted.

Impression: Status post Fontan palliation for HLHS. There is stable systemic right ventricular dilatation with mildly depressed systolic function, and no evidence of Fontan conduit obstruction.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion, measuring up to 18 mm adjacent to the right atrium and 14 mm along the lateral wall of the left ventricle. There is associated diastolic collapse of the right atrial free wall, suggesting elevated intrapericardial pressures and impending hemodynamic compromise. The myocardium demonstrates normal signal intensity without evidence of active edema or late gadolinium enhancement. Bi-ventricular systolic function is normal, with an ejection fraction of 60%.

Impression: Moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion with signs of elevated intrapericardial pressure (early tamponade physiology). Close clinical monitoring and consideration of pericardiocentesis are advised.

Evaluation of the heart reveals a large perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 1.1 cm in maximal diameter. There is a prominent left-to-right shunt visualized via phase-contrast flow profiling, with a calculated Qp:Qs ratio of 2.1. Moderate dilation of the left atrium and left ventricle is present, consistent with volume overload. Right ventricular and pulmonary artery pressures appear moderately elevated.

Impression: Large perimembranous ventricular septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt and secondary left heart volume overload. LV ejection fraction is 64%.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed utilizing pediatric multiplanar, multisequence protocols. The brain parenchyma is normal in appearance with age-appropriate myelination. There is no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial mass lesions, restricted diffusion, or intracranial hemorrhage. The ventricles and sulci are normal in caliber and configuration.

Impression: Completely normal pediatric brain MRI. No acute intracranial process or structural abnormalities seen to explain the patient's headaches.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate gyral and sulcal progression, including early formation of secondary sulci. The ventricular system is normal in shape and size, with the atrial width measuring 6.1 mm. The posterior fossa structures, corpus callosum, and brainstem are morphologically intact. No other fetal organ system anomalies are detected.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating appropriate cerebral maturation and unremarkable fetal anatomy for 29 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals features highly characteristic of skeletal dysplasia, likely thanatophoric dysplasia. There is marked shortening of all long bones with curvature of the femurs (telephone-receiver appearance). The fetal chest cavity is extremely narrow and bell-shaped, resulting in severe pulmonary hypoplasia. There is ventriculomegaly with an atrial measurement of 13.0 mm and macrocephaly.

Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia with narrow thorax and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia, most consistent with thanatophoric dysplasia. Fetal ventriculomegaly is also noted.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates expected intracranial development. The brain parenchymal signal is normal, and the cerebral sulcation matches gestational age expectations. The lateral ventricles are symmetric with an atrial width of 6.2 mm. The posterior fossa structures are normal, and the corpus callosum is fully formed. The fetal chest, abdomen, and extremities appear grossly normal on these sequences.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 30 weeks gestation. No structural anomalies of the central nervous system or body cavities visualized.

Cardiac MRI shows normal positioning and cardiac connections. The ventricles exhibit normal end-diastolic volumes, stroke volume index, and mass indices.
