Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%. Myocardial tissue characterization via T1 and T2 mapping techniques is entirely within the normal reference range. No focal late gadolinium enhancement is observed.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with preserved biventricular systolic function, normal chamber dimensions, and no evidence of scarring or inflammation.

Fetal MRI performed at 32 weeks gestation reveals marked bilateral ventriculomegaly. The atrium of the left lateral ventricle measures 14.5 mm, and the atrium of the right lateral ventricle measures 15.2 mm, indicating severe ventriculomegaly. There is associated thinning of the surrounding white matter parenchyma and mild colpocephaly. However, the third and fourth ventricles are within normal limits, and the corpus callosum is completely visualized and intact. Sulcation is otherwise appropriate for gestational age.

Impression: Bilateral severe fetal ventriculomegaly at 32 weeks gestation, without clear evidence of aqueductal stenosis or associated midline structural anomalies. Close postnatal neurosurgical follow-up is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal development. Brain biometrics are normal, and the lateral ventricular atria measure 6.2 mm. Cerebellar hemispheres and vermis are normal. Sulcation pattern is appropriate for 27 weeks.

No spinal or visceral anomalies are visualized. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation.

Brain MRI performed for developmental delay workup. The myelination pattern is appropriate for age. Cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, and cerebellum are symmetric and structurally normal. No abnormal enhancing focus is seen.

Impression: Normal pediatric brain MRI. No structural abnormality, congenital malformation, or myelination delay.

Brain MR imaging demonstrates multiple nodular subependymal lesions bilaterally, typical of subependymal nodules. Additionally, several subcortical T2/FLAIR hyperintense tubers are identified in the frontal and parietal lobes. A single lesion near the right foramen of Monro measures 1.1 cm, showing mild enhancement, but without ventricular obstruction.

Impression: Intracranial features are consistent with tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC). Subependymal lesion near the foramen of Monro likely represents a small subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA); serial imaging is advised to monitor for growth or obstruction.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates late third-trimester brain development. Cortical folding is highly complex with deep, well-demarcated sulcations. The ventricular system is small, with atrial width measuring 5.9 mm. The corpus callosum is thick and completely formed. Visceral organs are normal; both kidneys show appropriate corticomedullary differentiation, and the bladder is filled with urine. Amniotic fluid volume is physiologic.

Impression: Normal, mature fetal MRI study at 36 weeks gestation. No structural, intracranial, or spinal abnormalities detected.

Cardiovascular MR imaging shows normal left and right ventricular chambers. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% (LVEDVI 72 mL/m2) and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58% (RVEDVI 74 mL/m2). No valvular stenosis or regurgitation is identified. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging is negative for focal myocardial scar, and T2-weighted sequences show no tissue edema.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural, valvular, or myocardial pathology.

An evaluation of the atrial septum demonstrates a moderate-sized secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring approximately 12 mm in diameter. Phase-contrast flow quantification indicates a significant left-to-right shunt with a pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp:Qs) calculated at 1.7:1. There is mild dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, with a right ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 112 mL/m². Left ventricular size and ejection fraction (64%) remain within normal pediatric limits.

Impression: Secundum atrial septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt, resulting in mild right-sided cardiac chamber enlargement.

High-resolution brain MRI performed for seizure workup demonstrates multiple cortical and subcortical tubers, primarily located in the frontal and parietal lobes, characterized by T2/FLAIR hyperintensity and lack of contrast enhancement. In addition, several subependymal nodules (SENs) are seen along the lateral ventricles, some demonstrating calcification. There is no evidence of a subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) near the foramen of Monro, and ventricles are normal in size.

Impression: Intracranial features highly characteristic of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC), including multiple cortical/subcortical tubers and subependymal nodules without signs of malignant transformation or ventricular obstruction.

Cardiac MRI evaluates status post stage III Fontan palliation for hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS). The extracardiac Fontan conduit is widely patent without stenosis, thrombosis, or narrowing. Systemic right ventricular function is moderately depressed with an ejection fraction of 42%. Mild-to-moderate systemic tricuspid valve regurgitation is identified.

Impression: Post-Fontan evaluation with a patent conduit, moderately depressed systemic right ventricular function, and mild-to-moderate tricuspid regurgitation.

Brain MR examination performed for chronic tension-type headaches reveals normal brain architecture. No focal parenchymal lesions, demyelinating plaques, or mass lesions are present. The gray-white matter differentiation is sharp and appropriate for age. The ventricles and subarachnoid spaces show normal volume and distribution, and the skull base structures are grossly intact.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or inflammatory processes are identified to explain the clinical history of chronic headaches.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles are widely separated and show marked colpocephaly, with dilation of the occipital horns measuring 12.1 mm on the left and 11.8 mm on the right. The third ventricle is high-riding and dilated. Cavum septum pellucidum is absent.

The cortical sulcation pattern is appropriate for the gestational stage. No other central nervous system anomalies are identified. Impression: Agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated moderate colpocephaly. No secondary brain abnormalities visualized.

Brain MRI of this 5-month-old infant demonstrates a severely hypoplastic cerebellar vermis, which is rotated superiorly. There is massive cystic dilation of the posterior fossa CSF space, which freely communicates with an enlarged fourth ventricle. The tentorium cerebelli and transverse sinuses are elevated. The lateral and third ventricles show moderate symmetric dilation, consistent with early hydrocephalus.

Impression: Diagnostic features of Dandy-Walker malformation associated with mild-to-moderate supratentorial ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI evaluates valvular structure and function. There is thickening and doming of the anterior mitral valve leaflet during diastole, with restriction of the posterior leaflet, consistent with chronic rheumatic changes. The mitral valve orifice area is restricted, measuring 1.2 cm2 by planimetry, indicating moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis. There is also moderate mitral regurgitation (regurgitant fraction 25%) and moderate left atrial dilation. Both the left and right ventricular systolic functions are preserved (LVEF 60%, RVEF 55%).

Impression: Mitral valve pathology demonstrating classic rheumatic morphology with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis and moderate regurgitation, accompanied by left atrial enlargement. Follow-up for potential valvuloplasty is suggested.

Cardiac MRI confirms anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA). The left main coronary artery arises directly from the posterior aspect of the pulmonary trunk. There is significant retrograde flow from the left coronary system into the pulmonary artery, with massive dilation of the right coronary artery providing collateral flow. The left ventricle is dilated with moderately reduced systolic function (LVEF 42%) and subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) with evidence of chronic subendocardial ischemia and left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

Brain MRI was performed for evaluation of macrocephaly. There is symmetric enlargement of the subarachnoid spaces, particularly within the frontal lobes and along the interhemispheric fissure. There is no ventriculomegaly, subdural fluid collection, or mass lesion. The brain parenchyma shows normal development and myelination patterns appropriate for a 12-month-old infant.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with benign expansion of the subarachnoid spaces of infancy (benign macrocephaly). No signs of hydrocephalus or intracranial mass.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation shows age-appropriate brain development. The cerebral cortex demonstrates a smooth, normal-appearing bilaminar structure, completely typical for early 22-week sulcation. The ventricular system is normal in size and symmetric, with the atrium of the left and right lateral ventricles measuring 5.8 mm. Posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, are intact.

Fetal chest, abdomen, and limbs are unremarkable. Amniotic fluid volume is subjectively normal. Impression: Completely normal 22-week fetal MRI scan with no intracranial, thoracic, or abdominal abnormalities identified.

ECG-gated cardiac MRI was acquired to evaluate for potential structural heart disease. The ventricles demonstrate normal internal dimensions and wall thickness. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 75 mL/m2 with an ejection fraction of 64%. Right ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 78 mL/m2 with an ejection fraction of 60%. Myocardial T2-weighted imaging and late gadolinium enhancement sequences show no areas of hyperintensity or focal fibrosis.

Impression: Completely unremarkable pediatric cardiac MRI. Preservation of biventricular size and function without evidence of shunt, cardiomyopathy, or myocardial scarring.

A cluster of serpiginous flow voids is identified in the left parietal lobe, measuring approximately 2.2 cm in maximal dimension, consistent with an arteriovenous malformation. There is a prominent feeding artery arising from the left middle cerebral artery branch and drainage via a single dilated cortical vein into the superior sagittal sinus. No surrounding parenchymal edema, restricted diffusion, or evidence of recent hemorrhage is observed.

Impression: Left parietal lobe arteriovenous malformation (AVM) with a single draining cortical vein. No acute hemorrhage or ischemia is present. Neurosurgical and interventional neuroradiology referral is recommended.

Fetal magnetic resonance imaging performed at 22 weeks gestation shows completely normal intracranial anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit smooth, age-appropriate sulcal development. The lateral ventricular system is symmetric and normal in caliber, with the atrial diameter measuring 6.1 mm. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and posterior fossa structures are well-formed and intact.

No other structural abnormalities of the fetal face, thorax, abdomen, or spine are visualized. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation with normal intracranial architecture and age-appropriate sulcation.

ECG-gated cardiac MRI demonstrates the classic anatomical features of Tetralogy of Fallot. There is a large, non-restrictive malalignment ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 1.4 cm with 50% overriding of the aorta. Marked right ventricular hypertrophy is noted, with the right ventricular free wall measuring 8 mm. Severe infundibular and valvular right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) obstruction is visualized, leading to high-velocity turbulent jetting.

Impression: Tetralogy of Fallot with severe RVOT obstruction and significant right ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular function remains preserved with an ejection fraction of 60%.

MRI of the brain demonstrates caudal herniation of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum, measuring approximately 7.5 mm below basion-opisthion line. The fourth ventricle is normally positioned, but the cisterna magna is effaced. A small, non-tension syrinx is noted extending from the C1 to C3 levels of the visualized cervical spine. Brain parenchyma is otherwise structurally normal with no signs of intracranial space-occupying lesions or ventriculomegaly.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with cerebellar tonsillar ectopia of 7.5 mm. Associated small cervical syrinx, suggesting the need for dedicated spinal MR imaging and neurosurgical consultation.

Dedicated orbital and brain MRI demonstrates fusiform enlargement and T2 hyperintensity of the intraorbital and canalicular segments of the left optic nerve, extending posteriorly to involve the optic chiasm. There is associated post-contrast enhancement. Bilateral globes and the contralateral optic nerve appear normal. Multiple focal areas of signal intensity (FASI) are noted in the basal ganglia.

Impression: Left optic pathway glioma with involvement of the chiasm. In conjunction with basal ganglia FASI, findings are highly characteristic of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1).

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation shows severe oligohydramnios/anhydramnios, which significantly limits spatial resolution but demonstrates empty renal fossae bilaterally. There is no evidence of functioning renal tissue or urinary bladder filling. The adrenal glands are lying flat within the renal beds ('lying-down' adrenal sign). The fetal lungs are severely compressed and hypoplastic. The fetal brain shows normal biometry for gestational age with an atrial measurement of 6.5 mm.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios and severe pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter's sequence). This constitutes a lethal fetal anomaly.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation reveals a completely normal singleton pregnancy. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal, age-appropriate sulcation patterns with well-developed central, cingulate, and parieto-occipital sulci. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, with the left atrium measuring 6.2 mm and the right atrium measuring 6.0 mm. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal.

Impression: Normal fetal brain MRI at 32 weeks gestation showing symmetric ventricles, intact corpus callosum, and excellent, age-appropriate sulcation.

Brain MRI demonstrates a compact nidus of abnormal, tortuous vascular flow voids located in the left parietal lobe, measuring approximately 2.2 x 1.8 cm. There is a prominent arterial feeder arising from the left middle cerebral artery and a dilated draining vein emptying into the superior sagittal sinus. Adjacent brain parenchyma shows mild gliosis on FLAIR imaging but no signs of recent hemorrhage or edema.

Impression: Left parietal lobe arteriovenous malformation (AVM) with no evidence of acute or subacute rupture.

Brain MRI was obtained to evaluate chronic daily tension-type headaches. The study reveals completely unremarkable intracranial structures. There is no evidence of space-occupying lesions, focal cortical dysplasia, or abnormal meningeal enhancement. The ventricular system, extra-axial spaces, and major arterial flow voids are within normal limits.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or inflammatory etiology identified to explain the patient's headaches.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals findings characteristic of a severe skeletal dysplasia. There is marked shortening of all long bones, with bowing of the femurs and humeri (severe micromelia). The fetal thorax is extremely narrow and bell-shaped with short ribs, leading to secondary bilateral pulmonary hypoplasia. Platyspondyly is noted throughout the spine.

The fetal brain shows normal cortical sulculation for 31 weeks. The lateral ventricles are normal in size, measuring 6.3 mm. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia, highly suspicious for thanatophoric dysplasia given the bell-shaped chest, short ribs, and profound micromelia. Associated pulmonary hypoplasia is noted.

Fetal MRI performed at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral asymmetric enlargement of the lateral ventricles. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 14.2 mm and the right measures 11.5 mm, consistent with moderate bilateral ventriculomegaly. The cerebral sulcation pattern is appropriate for the stated gestational age. The corpus callosum appears completely formed, and no other intracranial structural anomalies are identified. The fetal posterior fossa, chest, and abdomen are unremarkable.

Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly, left greater than right, without associated intracranial structural anomalies on current imaging. Follow-up imaging and postnatal clinical evaluation are recommended.

Brain MRI reveals bilateral, diffuse enlargement and T2 prolongation of the optic pathways, particularly involving the optic chiasm and pre-chiasmatic optic nerves. Additionally, multiple focal areas of signal intensity (FASI) are identified in the globus pallidus, brainstem, and cerebellum. No other focal parenchymal lesions are identified.

Impression: Optic pathway glioma and multiple characteristic FASIs in a patient with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1).

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 2-month-old infant post-arterial switch operation for d-transposition of the great arteries. The surgical reconstruction site shows mild supravalvular pulmonary stenosis with a localized luminal narrowing in the main pulmonary trunk, measuring 5 mm. There is mild right ventricular hypertrophy, but right ventricular ejection fraction is normal at 56%. The neo-aortic valve and coronary arteries are widely patent with no stenosis.

Impression: Status post-arterial switch operation with mild supravalvular pulmonary stenosis. Preserved bi-ventricular systolic function.

MR imaging of the brain with and without contrast reveals a well-circumscribed cyst with a highly enhancing mural nodule located within the right cerebellar hemisphere. The lesion measures approximately 2.8 x 2.4 x 2.6 cm. There is associated moderate local mass effect on the fourth ventricle, although the ventricular system shows no current signs of active obstructive hydrocephalus. Surrounding vasogenic edema is minimal.

Impression: Cystic cerebellar lesion with an enhancing mural nodule, highly characteristic of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. Recommend pediatric neurosurgical consultation for elective resection.

MRI demonstrates a large, heterogeneous, enhancing mass centered in the pineal region measuring 2.8 x 2.5 x 2.6 cm. The mass compresses the tectal plate and aqueduct of Sylvius, resulting in significant dilatation of the third and lateral ventricles. Focal hyperintensities indicative of intratumoral hemorrhage are identified on T1-weighted images.

Impression: Pineal region mass with secondary compressive aqueductal stenosis and hydrocephalus, highly suggestive of pineoblastoma or germ cell tumor. Urgent neurosurgical intervention for CSF diversion and biopsy is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates mild bilateral lateral ventriculomegaly. The left atrial diameter measures 11.2 mm and the right measures 11.4 mm. There is no evidence of periventricular nodularity or intraventricular hemorrhage. The sulcation and operculization of the sylvian fissures are appropriate for 27 weeks gestation, and the corpus callosum is intact.

Impression: Mild, symmetric, isolated bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommended follow-up in 3-4 weeks to monitor ventricular size.

Brain MRI/MRA demonstrates a nidus of tortuous vascular structures within the left parietal lobe, measuring approximately 2.5 x 2.2 cm. Multiple prominent arterial feeders are visualized arising from the branches of the left middle cerebral artery, with early venous drainage into the superior sagittal sinus. Surrounding parenchymal edema is minimal, and there is no evidence of acute intraparenchymal or subarachnoid hemorrhage.

Impression: Brain arteriovenous malformation (AVM) in the left parietal lobe. There is no evidence of acute hemorrhage, but prompt neurovascular intervention evaluation is recommended.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates normal intracranial architecture. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate gyral development, and the primary sulcation patterns are entirely appropriate for the stated gestational age. The ventricular system is normal in size, with the left and right ventricular atria measuring 5.8 mm and 6.0 mm, respectively. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and posterior fossa structures are intact without visible structural defects.

Visualized fetal chest, abdomen, and spine demonstrate no abnormal signal or anatomic malformations. Amniotic fluid volume is subjective within the normal range. Impression: Normal fetal MRI showing age-appropriate central nervous system and visceral development at 24 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 3-year-old female with suspected double outlet right ventricle (DORV). High-resolution cine imaging demonstrates that both the aorta and the pulmonary trunk arise almost entirely from the morphologic right ventricle. A large, non-restrictive subaortic ventricular septal defect (VSD) is noted, measuring 11 mm. There is significant subpulmonic infundibular stenosis producing right ventricular outflow tract obstruction. Moderate concentric hypertrophy of the right ventricle is visualized. Systemic left ventricular function is preserved (LVEF 55%), while right ventricular ejection fraction is 45%.

Impression: Double outlet right ventricle (DORV) of the Taussig-Bing variant, presenting with a large subaortic VSD, subpulmonic stenosis, and associated right ventricular hypertrophy.

Brain MRI demonstrates multiple focus-like lesions of high T2/FLAIR signal intensity involving the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. At least two of these lesions, including one in the left corpus callosum, demonstrate subtle nodular enhancement on post-contrast imaging. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows no restricted diffusion, and no mass effect is visualized.

Impression: Disseminated demyelinating lesions in space and time, strongly supportive of pediatric-onset Multiple Sclerosis (MS) or Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM). Pediatric neurology consultation is recommended for clinical correlation.

MR evaluation of the brain reveals localized thickening of the cortex within the anterior right frontal lobe, associated with blurring of the gray-white matter junction and a transmantle sign of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity extending to the ventricle. The hippocampus and amygdala structures are symmetrical and normal in appearance. No signs of pathological enhancement or intracranial mass effect are present.

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD Type II) in the right frontal lobe. This represents a highly probable epileptogenic zone correlation with the patient's refractory seizures.

The study demonstrates normal intracranial structure. Myelination pattern is progressive and appropriate for an 18-month-old child. The ventricles and extra-axial spaces are normal in caliber. No evidence of hydrocephalus, intracranial mass, extra-axial collections, or restricted diffusion is present. Visualized cranial nerve complexes are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal brain MRI with age-appropriate myelination. No structural or developmental brain anomalies detected to explain developmental delay.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular volumes and preserved left ventricular systolic function with an ejection fraction of 54%. High-resolution T2-weighted and T1-mapping sequences reveal diffuse myocardial edema, predominantly involving the basal to mid-lateral left ventricular wall. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows matching subepicardial and mid-myocardial hyperenhancement in these same lateral wall regions, without subendocardial involvement.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of acute myocarditis involving the basal to mid-lateral left ventricular wall, satisfying the updated Lake Louise criteria. Left ventricular systolic function remains overall preserved.

Brain MRI shows a markedly enlarged posterior fossa with a cystic fluid collection communicating directly with an expanded fourth ventricle, associated with hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis and an elevated tentorium. There is prominent enlargement of the third and lateral ventricles, indicating progressive hydrocephalus.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation with associated obstructive ventriculomegaly. Neurosurgical evaluation for shunt or fenestration is advised.

MR imaging of the brain utilizing a high-resolution epilepsy protocol demonstrates localized thickening of the cortex in the left frontal lobe along the superior frontal gyrus. There is blurring of the gray-white matter junction and a hyperintense T2/FLAIR signal extending from the cortex to the lateral ventricle (transmantle sign). The hippocampus and ventricles are otherwise normal.

Impression: Findings in the left frontal lobe are highly characteristic of focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) Type II. This correlates with the patient's clinical history of drug-resistant epilepsy.

Cardiac MRI shows a moderate-sized ventricular septal defect (VSD) in the muscular portion of the septum. The shunt is predominantly left-to-right, with a calculated Qp/Qs ratio of 1.4:1. The left ventricle is minimally dilated, with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 88 mL/m². Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 63%, and right ventricular function is normal at 58%.

Impression: Moderate muscular ventricular septal defect with mild left ventricular volume overload and preserved biventricular systolic function.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates a large posterior fossa fluid collection communicating widely with an enlarged fourth ventricle, consistent with Dandy-Walker malformation. The cerebellar vermis is severely hypoplastic and rotated superiorly. The torcular herophili and tentorium are significantly elevated. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with atrial measurements of 13.5 mm on the left and 12.8 mm on the right.

The cerebral sulcation pattern is appropriate for 30 weeks gestation. No additional cerebral cortical dysplasias or extracranial anomalies are noted. Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, a dilated fourth ventricle, cystic enlargement of the posterior fossa, and moderate ventriculomegaly.

Brain MRI in this patient with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) demonstrates diffuse thickening and hyperintensity of the left optic nerve and optic chiasm. Mild enhancement of this segment is noted post-contrast, consistent with an optic pathway glioma. Multiple bilateral, hyperintense T2/FLAIR lesions (FASI - focal areas of signal intensity) are also visualized within the dentate nuclei, globus pallidus, and brainstem.

Impression: Left-sided optic pathway glioma, consistent with NF1 diagnosis. No mass effect on the optic chiasm or upstream ventriculomegaly is noted.

Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC/D). MRI shows dilation and focal thinning of the right ventricular free wall, with multiple localized microaneurysms at the RV outflow tract and apex. Quantitative analysis reveals a moderately reduced RVEF of 36% with regional dyskinesia. Late gadolinium enhancement demonstrates transmural fibrosis within the right ventricular free wall and RVOT region.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting major task force diagnostic criteria.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. Coronal and axial imaging demonstrates widely spaced, parallel lateral ventricles with dilation of the occipital horns (colpocephaly). The right atrium measures 12.8 mm and the left atrium measures 13.0 mm. Probst bundles are identified coursing longitudinally along the medial ventricular walls. Normal sulcation and myelination patterns are noted for 31 weeks.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild-to-moderate colpocephaly. No other intracranial abnormalities are identified.

Brain MRI demonstrates crescentic, bilateral extra-axial fluid collections in the frontoparietal regions, measuring up to 6 mm on the right and 5 mm on the left. The collections demonstrate mixed signal intensity, with T1 hyperintensity and T2 hypointensity suggestive of subacute subdural hematomas of varying ages. There is no significant mass effect on the underlying parenchyma.

Impression: Bilateral subacute subdural hematomas of varying ages. Clinical correlation is recommended to evaluate for potential non-accidental trauma.

Fetal brain MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a Dandy-Walker variant. There is mild hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis with a keyhole-like communication between the fourth ventricle and the cisterna magna. The posterior fossa is minimally enlarged. The lateral ventricles are completely normal in caliber, with both atria measuring 8.5 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 28 weeks, demonstrating clear cingulate and parieto-occipital sulci.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant characterized by mild inferior vermian hypoplasia, without ventriculomegaly, at 28 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI reveals normal biventricular volumes with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction of 58%. No wall motion abnormalities, regional hypokinesis, or late enhancement is noted. The aortic valve is morphologically trileaflet with normal systolic opening and no regurgitant jet.

Impression: Structurally normal pediatric heart with preserved biventricular systolic function. No signs of myocarditis, cardiomyopathy, or shunt pathologies.

Cardiac MRI shows Ebstein's anomaly characterized by severe downward displacement of the septal and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve (displacement index of 15 mm/m²). This creates a large, thinned, 'atrialized' portion of the right ventricle. The remaining functional right ventricle is small, with a depressed ejection fraction of 35%.

Severe tricuspid regurgitation is present. Left ventricular function remains intact with an ejection fraction of 58%. Impression: Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve with significant atrialization of the right ventricle, severe tricuspid regurgitation, and compromised right ventricular systolic function.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows advanced sulcation with well-defined secondary and tertiary sulci appropriate for 36 weeks. The lateral ventricular atria measure 5.0 mm. Posterior fossa and corpus callosum are normal.

Thoracic and abdominal anatomy is normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate brain maturation at 36 weeks gestation.

Neonatal cardiac MRI reveals normal segmental cardiac anatomy. The systemic and pulmonary venous connections are normal, and there is no evidence of intracardiac shunts, coarctation, or major vessel abnormalities. A patent foramen ovale is visualized with a physiologic left-to-right shunt, which is normal for a 12-day-old infant. Biventricular mass and volume are appropriate for the neonate.

Impression: Completely normal neonatal cardiac MRI showing preserved biventricular systolic function and no congenital heart defects.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation reveals severe skeletal anomalies. There is severe, symmetric shortening of all long bones (micromelia). The thorax is severely narrowed and bell-shaped, with associated pulmonary hypoplasia. The skull shows a subtle trilobed (cloverleaf) appearance, and there is prominent frontal bossing.

The brain parenchyma appears grossly normal, although the posterior fossa is relatively small. Impression: Features highly suggestive of a severe skeletal dysplasia, such as thanatophoric dysplasia. Pediatric genetics and neonatology consultation are recommended.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals a classic Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia and upward rotation of the cerebellar vermis, accompanied by cystic dilation of the posterior fossa communicating with the fourth ventricle. The torcular herophili is elevated. Mild bilateral ventriculomegaly is noted, with lateral ventricular atria measuring 10.4 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 26 weeks gestation.

Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation with associated mild bilateral ventriculomegaly. Recommend prenatal neurosurgical consultation and post-delivery imaging.

MR examination of the brain reveals a solid, hyperintense mass on T2/FLAIR centered in the cerebellar vermis, measuring approximately 3.8 x 3.5 x 3.2 cm. The lesion shows prominent, heterogeneous contrast enhancement and restricted diffusion. There is significant mass effect on the fourth ventricle, which is severely compressed, leading to severe obstructive hydrocephalus with transependymal flow of cerebrospinal fluid noted around the lateral ventricles.

Impression: Large posterior fossa mass arising from the cerebellar vermis, highly suggestive of medulloblastoma given the patient's age and imaging features. Marked obstructive hydrocephalus is present, necessitating urgent neurosurgical decompression.

MR imaging of the brain reveals bilateral fusiform enlargement and T2 hyperintensity of the optic nerves, extending back into the optic chiasm. Additionally, there are multiple ill-defined T2-hyperintense lesions without mass effect or enhancement in the brainstem, dentate nuclei of the cerebellum, and globus pallidus (FASI/UBOs).

Impression: Optic pathway glioma involving bilateral optic nerves and chiasm, accompanied by classic focal areas of signal intensity (FASI), highly characteristic of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1).

The study demonstrates normal anatomical relationships throughout the cerebral cortex, subcortical tracts, and brainstem. There are no signs of white matter signaling anomalies, cerebral ischemia, or structural lesions. The ventricular system, subdural spaces, and major arterial flow voids appear entirely normal.

Impression: Normal MR of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or neoplastic process identified to correlate with clinical presentation of atypical migraines.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 31 weeks gestation for maternal size limitations during routine ultrasound. The cerebral cortex demonstrates normal, age-appropriate sulcation and gyration patterns, specifically with well-defined parieto-occipital and calcarine sulci. Both lateral ventricular atria are within normal limits, measuring 5.8 mm on the left and 6.0 mm on the right. The corpus callosum is completely visualized and normal in thickness. The cerebellum, brainstem, and cisterna magna are structurally intact.

Fetal visceral anatomy, including the diaphragm, stomach, and kidneys, is normal. No structural anomalies of the spine are identified. Impression: Normal fetal brain and somatic anatomy at 31 weeks gestation, with normal ventricular atrial measurements and expected cortical development for gestational age.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a posterior fossa anomaly. There is partial agenesis of the lower cerebellar vermis and a prominent fluid-filled space in the cisterna magna, which communicates with the fourth ventricle. This creates a mild keyhole-shaped defect in the cerebellum. The cerebellar hemispheres are normal in size. The bilateral lateral ventricles measure 8.5 mm, which is within the upper limit of normal.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant (partial vermian hypoplasia with prominent cisterna magna). High-normal ventricular size; clinical follow-up is suggested.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates asymmetrical ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 12.1 mm, indicating moderate ventriculomegaly, whereas the right atrium measures 8.5 mm, which is normal. There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, and cortical migration patterns are intact, though slightly delayed locally on the left hemisphere.

All midline structures, including the corpus callosum and brainstem, appear fully intact. Impression: Isolated, moderate left-sided fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommend prenatal follow-up.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates standard structural development. The sulcation and gyration are appropriate for 30 weeks, demonstrating early secondary sulcus formation. The lateral ventricles are symmetrical and measure 5.8 mm. Posterior fossa structures, including the vermis and cerebellar hemispheres, are within normal parameters. Visualized fetal organs, spine, and placenta are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal fetal brain and body MRI at 30 weeks gestation. No anomalies detected.

Cardiac MRI shows a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 14 mm in maximal diameter. Significant left-to-right shunting is confirmed by phase-contrast imaging across the defect, demonstrating a Qp/Qs ratio of 1.75:1. There is moderate dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, with a right ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m2. Right ventricular systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 57%.

Impression: Moderately large secundum ASD with significant left-to-right shunt and secondary right-sided chamber dilation.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a severely enlarged posterior fossa with a high-riding torcular herophili. There is profound hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with rotation of the vermian remnant. A large, cystic CSF-space communication is noted between the fourth ventricle and the posterior fossa. The lateral ventricles show associated ventriculomegaly, with the right atrium measuring 12.5 mm and the left atrium measuring 13.0 mm.

The supratentorial sulcation pattern is appropriate for 28 weeks gestation, with no visible gray matter heterotopias. Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation with associated moderate bilateral ventriculomegaly. Prenatal neurosurgical consultation is advised.

Brain MRI demonstrates symmetric and age-appropriate myelination of the white matter tracts. The corpus callosum is intact and fully formed. The ventricular system, basal ganglia, and posterior fossa structures are entirely normal in morphology and signal characteristics.

Impression: Unremarkable pediatric brain MRI. No structural abnormalities, delayed myelination, or migration anomalies identified to explain developmental delay.

MRI of the brain was obtained following a sports-related concussion. There is no evidence of microhemorrhage on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) sequences. No abnormal signal intensities or focal parenchymal lesions are seen on T1, T2, or FLAIR imaging. Ventricles and extra-axial CSF spaces are within normal limits.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, hemorrhagic, or ischemic markers related to recent concussion.

Cardiac MRI evaluates status post repair of Tetralogy of Fallot. There is mild to moderate right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) dysfunction with trace residual infundibular stenosis. Right ventricular end-diastolic volume index (RVEDVI) is slightly elevated at 98 mL/m2, indicating mild RV dilatation, likely related to mild chronic pulmonary regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 15%. Left ventricular size and systolic function are preserved with an ejection fraction of 60%.

Impression: Post-operative Tetralogy of Fallot status with mild right ventricular dilatation and mild pulmonary regurgitation. No severe RVOT obstruction or significant branch pulmonary artery stenosis is seen.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates a normal singleton fetus. The intracranial structures are normal for early gestation. The lateral ventricles are completely normal and measure 5.4 mm bilaterally at the atria. The cerebral hemispheres are smooth with early, age-appropriate opercularization of the sylvian fissures, representing a normal early sulcation pattern. The posterior fossa structures are intact.

Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study at 20 weeks gestation with symmetric ventricles and expected early-stage sulcal development.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach, several loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left lobe of the liver are herniated into the left hemithorax. This causes a significant mediastinal shift to the right and marked compression of both lungs. The fetal brain is normal with age-appropriate sulcation and normal ventricles measuring 6.1 mm.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation (liver-up) and associated severe pulmonary hypoplasia. The observed-to-expected total fetal lung volume is calculated at 32%.

Cardiac MRI performed to rule out anomalous pulmonary venous connection in a 3-year-old child. Dynamic angiography and multiplanar reconstruction confirm that all four pulmonary veins drain normally into the left atrium. There is no evidence of sinus venosus, secundum, or primum atrial septal defects. Ventricular septal integrity is fully preserved.

Biventricular volumes, myocardial thickness, and systolic function are normal for age (LVEF 63%, RVEF 60%). No extra-cardiac anomalies are identified. Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI with normal pulmonary venous anatomy and no evidence of congenital cardiac shunts.

Cardiac MRI evaluated an 11-year-old boy with suspected rheumatic heart disease. There is thickening and restricted mobility of both the mitral and aortic valve leaflets. Moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation is observed on cine imaging with a regurgitant volume of 22 mL/beat, and mild aortic regurgitation is also present. Left atrial volume is moderately increased. Left ventricular size and systolic function are preserved with an ejection fraction of 62%. No late gadolinium enhancement is noted within the myocardium.

Impression: Chronic rheumatic valvular disease with moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation and mild aortic regurgitation. Left atrial enlargement is present; however, left ventricular systolic function remains stable.

Cardiac MRI performed on a 21-year-old male demonstrates normal cardiac structures and relationships. Left and right ventricular volumes, mass, and wall thickness are completely normal for age and body surface area. Systolic function is preserved with an LVEF of 65% and RVEF of 61%. No valvular regurgitation, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement is observed.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with excellent biventricular performance and no evidence of structural, congenital, or infiltrative cardiac disease.

Cardiac MRI reveals asymmetric septal hypertrophy, primarily involving the anterior interventricular septum. The maximal end-diastolic wall thickness is measured at 24 mm at the midventricular level, representing a Z-score > 6. The posterior wall thickness is 9 mm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve leading to mild dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and moderate mitral regurgitation. Left ventricular ejection fraction is elevated at 75%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) images demonstrate patchy, mid-myocardial enhancement at the RV insertion points and within the hypertrophied septal segments.

Impression: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with asymmetric septal hypertrophy, dynamic LVOT obstruction (SAM positive), and evidence of focal myocardial fibrosis. Suggestive of high risk for ventricular arrhythmias; clinical correlation recommended.

High-resolution epilepsy protocol MR imaging of the brain reveals localized thickening of the cortex in the posterior aspect of the left frontal lobe. There is blurring of the grey-white matter junction on T2 and FLAIR sequences, along with a subtle, hyperintense tapering tail of white matter extending toward the ventricle (transmantle sign). No other cortical abnormalities, vascular anomalies, or mass lesions are identified elsewhere in the cerebral hemispheres.

Impression: Focal area of cortical thickening and blurred grey-white junction in the left posterior frontal lobe, highly characteristic of focal cortical dysplasia (FCD Type II). This corresponds well with the patient's clinical seizure semiology.

Brain MRI was performed using standard pediatric multiplanar, multisequence protocols. The brain parenchyma is unremarkable with normal myelination and no areas of abnormal signal intensity or restricted diffusion. The ventricles, sulci, and extra-axial spaces are appropriate for age. Minimal mucosal thickening is noted in the maxillary sinuses, but the intracranial contents are completely normal.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or vascular intracranial lesions are identified.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 32 weeks gestation reveals complete absence of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly with prominent teardrop-shaped dilation of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles, with atrial measurements of 11.8 mm on the left and 11.5 mm on the right. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced. Evaluation of the cortical surface demonstrates a radial or "sunburst" pattern of the medial sulci converging toward the roof of the third ventricle, which is typical for callosal agenesis.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly and characteristic radial sulcation pattern at 32 weeks gestation.

Multiplanar, multisequence brain MRI reveals a well-circumscribed cyst with an enhancing mural nodule in the right cerebellar hemisphere. The cystic portion measures approximately 2.8 x 2.4 x 2.5 cm, with the solid mural nodule measuring 1.2 cm, demonstrating intense enhancement following gadolinium administration. There is moderate surrounding vasogenic edema with compression of the fourth ventricle and mild displacement of the brainstem anteriorly, although the cerebral aqueduct remains patent. No abnormal restricted diffusion or magnetic susceptibility is identified.

Impression: Well-circumscribed cystic and solid enhancing lesion within the right cerebellar hemisphere, highly suggestive of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. Mass effect on the fourth ventricle is present without evidence of acute obstructive hydrocephalus.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The right lobe of the liver and several loops of small bowel have herniated into the right hemithorax, resulting in a leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the heart. The left lung is compressed but visible; the right lung is severely hypoplastic. Cortical sulcation of the brain is normal for 36 weeks, with ventricles measuring 6.2 mm.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with herniation of liver and bowel loops, mediastinal shift, and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals multiple fractures in various stages of healing across the ribs and bilateral femora, which appear abnormally shortened and bowed. The skull is extremely thin and compressible under uterine pressure, yielding unusually high-resolution imaging of the brain due to lack of signal attenuation. The chest is narrow. The cerebral hemispheres show normal sulcation for 26 weeks, and the lateral ventricles are symmetric with atrial widths of 6.2 mm.

Impression: Skeletal abnormalities highly characteristic of Osteogenesis Imperfecta (Type II), with severe micromelia, rib fractures, and thin skull.

Magnetic resonance imaging reveals a large, well-circumscribed extra-axial fluid collection in the left temporal fossa measuring 4.5 x 3.2 x 2.8 cm. The signal intensity of the fluid is identical to cerebrospinal fluid on all sequences, including T1, T2, and FLAIR, and demonstrates no restriction on diffusion-weighted imaging. There is mild remodeling of the adjacent sphenoid wing and left temporal bone with minimal compression of the temporal lobe, but no midline shift or herniation.

Impression: Large, benign-appearing left temporal arachnoid cyst (Galassi Type II). There is mild local mass effect, but no signs of acute complication or hydrocephalus. Clinical correlation and follow-up imaging are suggested.

MRI of the brain was obtained for the evaluation of episodic vertigo and dizziness. There is normal gray-white matter differentiation. No intra- or extra-axial mass, acute ischemia, or hemorrhage is present. The ventricles, sulci, cisterns, and intracranial vascular flow voids are completely unremarkable for age.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No central structural cause identified for the patient's vestibular symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals significant bilateral renal anomalies. The fetal kidneys are markedly enlarged, showing severe bilateral hydronephrosis and dilated ureters down to the level of the bladder. The urinary bladder is severely dilated and thick-walled, highly suspicious for keyhole sign and posterior urethral valves (PUV). Oligohydramnios is present. The fetal brain shows appropriate sulcation and normal ventricles, with atria measuring 5.2 mm.

Impression: Severe bilateral hydroureteronephrosis, distended thick-walled bladder, and oligohydramnios, highly suggestive of posterior urethral valves. Fetal urology consultation and delivery planning are indicated.

MRI of the infant brain demonstrates normal, age-appropriate progression of myelination, with active myelination noted in the posterior limbs of the internal capsules and cerebellar peduncles. The corpus callosum is well-formed. No structural malformations, subdural collections, or abnormal parenchymal signals are observed.

Impression: Unremarkable pediatric brain MRI demonstrating age-appropriate myelination and structural development. No cause for global developmental delay is seen on structural imaging.

Cardiovascular MRI of a 5-month-old infant demonstrates a moderately sized perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 5.5 mm in diameter. Shunt flow is predominantly left-to-right with a Qp:Qs ratio of 1.5. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is mildly increased, reflecting left heart volume overload.

Left ventricular systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 62%. No significant right ventricular hypertrophy is noted. Impression: Moderately sized perimembranous ventricular septal defect with moderate left-to-right shunt and mild left ventricular volume overload, without pulmonary hypertension features on current imaging.

Cardiac MRI reveals severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal septal thickness measuring 22 mm at the mid-ventricular level. The posterior wall thickness is normal at 9 mm, giving a septal-to-posterior wall ratio of 2.4. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, resulting in a moderate eccentrically directed jet of mitral regurgitation and dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates focal, patchy enhancement within the hypertrophied septal segments, suggesting myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy, dynamic LVOT obstruction secondary to SAM, and focal septal myocardial fibrosis.

Brain MRI demonstrates multiple subependymal nodules projecting into the lateral ventricles, the largest situated near the left foramen of Monro measuring 6 mm. There are also several subcortical and cortical FLAIR hyperintense tubers dispersed within both frontal and temporal lobes. No associated midline shift or ventricular enlargement is present, and there is no evidence of interval progression of the subependymal nodules.

Impression: Multiple cortical tubers and subependymal nodules, typical for a patient with known tuberous sclerosis complex. The nodule near the left foramen of Monro must be monitored for conversion to a subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA).

Infant brain MRI shows severe, symmetric dilation of the lateral and third ventricles. The fourth ventricle is of normal caliber, localizing the obstruction to the cerebral aqueduct. There is significant thinning of the corpus callosum and stretching of the cerebral mantle, along with prominent transependymal CSF flow. No intracranial hemorrhage or extra-axial fluid collection is detected.

Impression: Severe obstructive hydrocephalus secondary to congenital aqueductal stenosis. Immediate neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Cardiac MRI reveals thickening and classic systolic displacement of both the anterior and posterior mitral valve leaflets into the left atrium, exceeding 3 mm beyond the annulus plane. There is associated moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation, with a regurgitant volume estimated at 32 mL per beat. This has resulted in moderate left atrial enlargement and mild left ventricular dilation. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 66%.

Impression: Bileaflet mitral valve prolapse with moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation and associated left heart chamber enlargement. Function is preserved.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The stomach, major portions of the small bowel, and a small portion of the left lobe of the liver are herniated into the left hemithorax. This herniation causes a severe rightward mediastinal shift and compression of the contralateral lung. The calculated total fetal lung volume is severely reduced.

The fetal brain appears normal with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 5.5 mm. Sulcation and operculization are age-appropriate. Impression: Large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver-up component and severe pulmonary hypoplasia. Maternal-fetal medicine and pediatric surgery consultations are indicated.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates an open neural tube defect in the lumbar spine. There is a defect in the posterior elements of the spine spanning from L4 through S2 with herniation of an open myelomeningocele sac containing neural placode. Secondary intracranial findings of Chiari II malformation are evident, including downward displacement of the hindbrain, a 'banana-shaped' cerebellum, and ventricular atrial measurements of 11.5 mm.

Impression: Open lumbar myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation and mild ventriculomegaly. Recommend counseling regarding prenatal vs. postnatal repair options.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal, healthy development. The fetal brain anatomy is symmetric, and the ventricular atrium measures 6.0 mm. Sulcal development and gyration are appropriate for 28 weeks. The corpus callosum and brainstem are fully formed and unremarkable.

Fetal organs, including lungs, stomach, and bladder, are structurally normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural development.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal parenchymal development with early primary sulcation appropriate for gestational age. The lateral ventricular system is normal in caliber, with the right and left atrial widths measuring 5.8 mm and 5.5 mm respectively. The corpus callosum, brainstem, and posterior fossa structures are well-visualized and anatomically intact.

Visualized fetal chest, abdomen, and spine demonstrate normal development for 22 weeks. No structural anomalies are identified. Impression: Normal fetal brain and systemic development for 22 weeks gestational age.

Thickening and diffuse, intense leptomeningeal enhancement is noted throughout the basal cisterns and cerebral sulci. There is mild, symmetric dilatation of the entire ventricular system without focal mass effect, suggesting a non-obstructive communicating process.

Impression: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement, highly suggestive of active meningitis (bacterial, tuberculous, or fungal) or an inflammatory process.

Cardiac MRI is performed on a 13-year-old female for evaluation of an innocent-sounding systolic heart murmur. Analysis of the biventricular chambers reveals normal volumes, wall thickness, and preserved contractility. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 62% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There are no signs of ventricular hypertrophy, regional wall motion deficits, or valvular regurgitation.

No late gadolinium enhancement or abnormal myocardial edema is visualized on specialized sequencing. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No congenital, structural, or functional heart disease identified.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a well-circumscribed fluid collection in the posterior fossa measuring 2.1 x 1.8 x 1.5 cm. This cyst is located within the right cerebellopontine angle/arachnoid space and is consistent with an arachnoid cyst. It causes very mild compression of the right cerebellar hemisphere, though the vermis is intact. Ventricular atria are normal at 7.2 mm.

Cortical sulcation matches age-appropriate developmental criteria. Impression: Benign-appearing posterior fossa arachnoid cyst with minimal mass effect.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates an open neural tube defect in the lumbar spine, with a myelomeningocele sac extending from L4 through S1. The hindbrain shows classic Chiari II features, including herniation of the cerebellar tonsils below the foramen magnum and a banana-shaped cerebellum. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, measuring 12.8 mm at the atrium.

Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 23 weeks. Bilateral clubfoot deformities are noted, but no other skeletal anomalies are seen. Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with Chiari II malformation and associated moderate ventriculomegaly.

Neonate cardiac MRI shows both the aorta and pulmonary artery arising almost entirely from the morphologic right ventricle, consistent with a double outlet right ventricle (DORV). A large subaortic ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring 9.5 mm is present. Left ventricular blood flow enters the right ventricle solely through this VSD. Additionally, there is severe infundibular and valvular pulmonary stenosis with significant narrowing of the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT).

Impression: Double outlet right ventricle (DORV) of the Fallot type, with a large subaortic VSD and severe pulmonic stenosis. Moderate right ventricular hypertrophy is noted.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. The posterior fossa CSF space is mildly enlarged and communicates with the fourth ventricle through a small defect in the lower vermis, though the vermis itself is only mildly hypoplastic and not significantly rotated. The lateral ventricles are normal, with atrial widths measuring 7.1 mm and 6.8 mm. Cortical sulcal pattern is normal for gestational age.

The fetal spine, abdomen, and thorax appear structurally intact. Impression: Fetal cerebellar vermian hypoplasia (Dandy-Walker variant). Prenatal counseling is recommended to discuss neurodevelopmental follow-up.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a giant aneurysm of the proximal to mid-left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery measuring 7.8 mm in diameter, as well as a moderate aneurysm of the proximal right coronary artery (RCA) measuring 5.2 mm. There is no evidence of thrombus within the aneurysms. The left ventricular volumes are normal, with a preserved ejection fraction of 61%, and late gadolinium enhancement is negative for myocardial infarction.

Impression: Follow-up of Kawasaki disease demonstrating a giant LAD coronary artery aneurysm and a moderate proximal RCA aneurysm without evidence of acute coronary thrombus or myocardial scar.

Cardiac MRI conducted for sports clearance following an episode of exertional syncope. The study demonstrates entirely normal biventricular dimensions, wall thickness, and systolic function (LVEF 63%, RVEF 59%). There is no evidence of right ventricular outflow tract dynamic obstruction, anomalous coronary artery origin, or late gadolinium enhancement. T1 and T2 relaxation times are well within normal limits.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No structural, ischemic, or inflammatory heart disease identified. No contraindications to athletic activity based on this examination.

Cardiac MRI of this 2-year-old child demonstrates apical displacement of the septal and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve by 18 mm. This results in significant 'atrialization' of the inlet portion of the right ventricle, which is thin-walled and functionally integrated with the right atrium. Severe tricuspid regurgitation is seen on cine imaging. The functional right ventricle is small but exhibits adequate systolic function. The left ventricle is normal in size but demonstrates compressed geometry due to septal shift.

Impression: Classical findings of Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve, characterized by significant apical displacement, a large atrialized right ventricle, and severe tricuspid regurgitation.

Brain MRI reveals profound enlargement of both lateral ventricles and the third ventricle. The fourth ventricle is of normal caliber, suggesting obstruction at the level of the aqueduct of Sylvius. There is a prominent ballooning of the posterior recess of the third ventricle and thinning of the corpus callosum. Mild transependymal CSF seepage is observed.

Impression: Severe obstructive hydrocephalus due to aqueductal stenosis. Neurosurgical evaluation for endoscopic third ventriculostomy (ETV) or shunt placement is indicated.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks gestation reveals normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate sulcation and cortical migration for 24 weeks. The ventricular system is normal in size, with atrial width measuring 5.9 mm bilaterally. The brainstem, corpus callosum, and posterior fossa are within normal limits. The spine is intact without any neural tube defects.

Impression: Completely unremarkable fetal MRI study at 24 weeks gestation showing normal central nervous system development.

Brain MRI shows a heterogeneous suprasellar mass measuring 2.4 x 2.1 x 1.9 cm, showing cystic and solid components with focal calcifications. The mass exerts significant upward pressure on the optic chiasm, which is superiorly displaced and flattened. Pituitary stalk displacement is also observed. Solid portions show avid, heterogeneous enhancement after gadolinium administration.

Impression: Suprasellar mass exerting mass effect on the optic chiasm, most consistent with a craniopharyngioma. Neurosurgical and endocrinological evaluations are required.

MR imaging of the brain in this infant demonstrates a large posterior fossa fluid-filled cyst that communicates widely with the fourth ventricle, associated with severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis. The posterior fossa is markedly enlarged, and there is elevation of the tentorium and torcula. The supratentorial ventricles are mildly dilated without acute transependymal edema.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by a large posterior fossa cyst, cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, and an enlarged posterior fossa. Mild ventriculomegaly is noted.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a large patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) demonstrating continuous left-to-right shunting. The Qp/Qs ratio is calculated at 1.8. There is moderate volume overload of the left atrium and left ventricle, with an indexed LV end-diastolic volume of 88 mL/m2. Left ventricular systolic function is hyperdynamic with an ejection fraction of 68%. The right-sided chambers and pulmonary artery pressures appear within normal limits.

Impression: Large, hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus with secondary left-sided chamber enlargement. Recommend clinical correlation for potential transcatheter or surgical closure.

Brain MRI was performed using multiplanar, multisequence protocols including DWI, FLAIR, and high-resolution T2-weighted sequences. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal signal intensity and symmetric myelination. The ventricular system, basal ganglia, and internal capsule appear completely unremarkable. There is no evidence of intracranial mass lesion, acute hemorrhage, cerebral ischemia, or structural malformation.

Impression: Normal magnetic resonance imaging of the brain for age. No structural etiology is identified to account for the patient's history of chronic tension-type headaches.

Cardiac MRI reveals a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 18 x 14 mm. There is significant volume overload of the right heart, with marked dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle (indexed RV end-diastolic volume of 128 ml/m²). Velocity-encoded phase-contrast imaging of the pulmonary trunk and ascending aorta demonstrates a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt, with a calculated Qp:Qs ratio of 1.9. Left-sided chambers are normal in size.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with significant right heart volume overload and a high-flow left-to-right shunt. Right ventricular systolic function is preserved (RVEF 55%).

Cardiac MRI evaluates an 8-year-old male with suspected coarctation of the aorta. Multiplanar imaging demonstrates a focal, severe narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, located immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The minimum internal diameter at the coarctation site measures 5.5 mm. High-velocity jetting is noted across the narrowing with an estimated peak gradient of 38 mmHg. Prominent collateral arteries, including dilated internal mammary and intercostal vessels, are visualized. Mild left ventricular concentric hypertrophy is present (LV mass index 72 g/m²), but systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 60%.

Impression: Discrete, hemodynamically significant coarctation of the thoracic aorta with moderate left ventricular concentric hypertrophy. Well-developed collateral circulation is noted.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates moderate, isolated left lateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 13.8 mm, with moderate rounding of the posterior horn. In contrast, the right lateral ventricular atrium is normal in caliber, measuring 6.4 mm. No intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular nodularity, or parenchymal destruction is identified. The corpus callosum is fully intact.

Cerebral sulcation is normal and age-appropriate. The posterior fossa structures are normal, and no extracranial anomalies are identified. Impression: Moderate isolated left-sided fetal ventriculomegaly without associated intracranial anomalies. Recommend serial ultrasound monitoring.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation reveals a severe malformation of the posterior fossa. There is marked hypoplasia and rotation of the cerebellar vermis, along with a massively dilated posterior fossa fluid space that freely communicates with an enlarged fourth ventricle. This cystic expansion has resulted in elevated positioning of the tentorium cerebelli. The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, with atrial measurements of 11.0 mm bilaterally, and the cerebral sulcation is appropriate for 28 weeks.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by cerebellar vermian hypoplasia and cystic dilation of the posterior fossa. Pediatric neurosurgery and genetics consultations are advised.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral fetal hydronephrosis. There is significant dilation of both renal pelvises (the left measuring 9.5 mm and the right measuring 8.8 mm in anteroposterior diameter) with mild calyceal blunting. Amniotic fluid volume is borderline low, but adequate. The fetal brain demonstrates normal architecture with lateral ventricular atria of 6.4 mm.

No cranial abnormalities or neural tube defects are observed. Impression: Bilateral moderate fetal hydronephrosis. Recommend monitoring of amniotic fluid volumes.

Postoperative cardiac MRI of an 8-month-old female with history of repaired Tetralogy of Fallot. Severe, free pulmonary regurgitation is noted with a calculated regurgitant fraction of 45%. The right ventricle is severely dilated with an end-diastolic volume index of 142 mL/m². The right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly depressed at 42%.

Impression: Postoperative Tetralogy of Fallot status post transannular patch repair, currently demonstrating severe pulmonary regurgitation with associated severe right ventricular dilation and mild right ventricular dysfunction.

Postoperative evaluation for anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (ALCAPA) status-post direct translocation. The reimplanted left coronary artery originates cleanly from the aortic root with good flow and no stenosis. The left ventricular volume is mildly enlarged, but shows significant improvement compared to pre-operative assessments. Global LV systolic function is mildly reduced (EF 52%) with residual focal hypokinesis of the anterolateral wall. Small subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement is present in the lateral papillary muscle and anterolateral wall, reflecting prior ischemic injury.

Impression: Status-post successful repair of ALCAPA. Patent reimplanted left coronary artery with improved left ventricular volumes and mild residual lateral wall dysfunction and localized subendocardial scar.

Post-operative evaluation of repaired Tetralogy of Fallot. MRI demonstrates severe pulmonary regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 44%. The right ventricle is severely dilated, with an end-diastolic volume index (RVEDVI) of 165 mL/m². The right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 46%. Mild-to-moderate pulmonary valve stenosis is present with a peak gradient across the RVOT of 35 mmHg. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 56%.

Impression: Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot demonstrating severe pulmonary valve regurgitation with associated severe right ventricular dilation and mild RV dysfunction. Evaluated for pulmonary valve replacement.

Brain MRI of this 4-week-old neonate demonstrates abnormal signal intensity and restricted diffusion within the posterior limbs of the internal capsules, bilateral thalami, and putamina. There is also patchy T2 hyperintensity and restricted diffusion in the subcortical white matter of the motor-sensory strip. Findings are indicative of a pattern of acute deep gray nucleus and cortical injury secondary to global ischemia.

Impression: MR findings consistent with moderate-to-severe hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) with involvement of the basal ganglia, thalami, and peri-rolandic cortex.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows mild, isolated ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 11.2 mm, while the right atrium is within normal limits at 8.9 mm. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal cortical sulcation and migration patterns for 24 weeks. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa are fully normal in appearance with no hemorrhage or extra-axial fluid collections.

Fetal spine, chest, and abdomen are unremarkable. Impression: Mild, isolated left-sided fetal ventriculomegaly. Continued ultrasound monitoring is recommended, but the remaining brain structures are normal.

Brain MRI of this 4-month-old infant demonstrates agenesis of the cerebellar vermis with a classic 'keyhole' deformity of the posterior fossa, characterized by free communication of the fourth ventricle with a massively dilated posterior fossa fluid space. The tentorium is elevated, and there is associated mild-to-moderate enlargement of the third and lateral ventricles. Supratentorial gray-white matter boundaries and corpus callosum development are normal for age.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with a Dandy-Walker malformation, accompanied by moderate obstructive ventriculomegaly. Close monitoring of head circumference and neurosurgical review is advised.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal fetal development. Visualized intracranial structures show age-appropriate smooth parenchymal margins with normal early sulcation. The ventricular atria are symmetric and measure 5.5 mm. The corpus callosum is present and visible for this early stage. Spine, heart, stomach, kidneys, and extremities are all within normal limits.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation showing appropriate early structural and cerebral development.

Neonatal brain MRI reveals symmetric abnormal signal intensity on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) with corresponding ADC map decrease within the bilateral ventrolateral thalami and posterior limbs of the internal capsules. Similar restricted diffusion patterns are faintly observed in the perirolandic cerebral cortex. The ventricles and extra-axial spaces are of normal size and configuration for a neonate.

Impression: MRI findings demonstrate pattern of hypoxic-ischemic injury involving the deep gray matter nuclei and perirolandic motor cortex, compatible with moderate hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) in the acute/subacute stage.

Cardiac MRI shows normal heart size and function. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% (LVEDVI 71 mL/m²). Right ventricular ejection fraction is 58% (RVEDVI 74 mL/m²). No late gadolinium enhancement, edema, or perfusion defects are visualized. The coronary origins are normal, with the left and right coronaries arising from their respective sinus of Valsalva.

Impression: Completely normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No evidence of myocardial dysfunction, structural abnormalities, or anomalous coronary origins.

MRI of the brain demonstrates multiple large, poorly demarcated, bilateral asymmetric areas of increased T2/FLAIR signal intensity involving the subcortical and deep white matter of both cerebral hemispheres. Several of these lesions demonstrate faint, incomplete ring-like enhancement on post-contrast imaging. The brainstem and corpus callosum are spared, and there is no evidence of mass effect or ventricular distortion.

Impression: Multifocal demyelinating lesions. Given the acute onset of neurological symptoms following a recent viral illness, this is highly suggestive of Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM).

Symmetric, age-appropriate left and right ventricular thickness and dimensions are observed. Normal origin and trajectory of the coronary artery ostia are noted. The atrial septum is intact. No perfusion defects are seen, and no late gadolinium enhancement is present. Ventricular contractility and ejection fraction are entirely normal.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal anatomy and biventricular function with no evidence of congenital or acquired cardiac disease.

Single ventricle anatomy status post-Fontan palliation. MRI demonstrates a well-functioning lateral tunnel Fontan conduit without evidence of thrombosis, stenosis, or obstruction. The systemic single ventricle (morphologic left ventricle) is moderately dilated, showing a mild reduction in systolic function with an ejection fraction of 47%. No significant atrioventricular valve regurgitation is identified.

Impression: Patent lateral tunnel Fontan pathway with no signs of stenosis. The systemic single ventricle shows mild systolic dysfunction and moderate dilatation.

High-resolution sagittal images demonstrate herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 7 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The fourth ventricle is normally positioned, but there is noticeable crowding of the craniocervical junction. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow analysis indicates restricted pulsatile flow dorsal to the tonsils.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 7 mm tonsillar ectopia and associated CSF flow restriction at the level of the foramen magnum. No evidence of cervical syrinx or ventriculomegaly on the current examination.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows normal, age-appropriate structural development. The cerebral cortex shows a smooth appearance with normal, early parieto-occipital and cingulate sulci development, typical of a 24-week gestation. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with the atrium measuring 6.2 mm. All midline structures, posterior fossa, and spine are intact.

Fetal viscera and amniotic fluid volume are completely normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 24 weeks gestation with normal cerebral, spinal, and visceral anatomy.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain reveals symmetric and normal brain parenchyma. There is no evidence of restriction on diffusion-weighted imaging, acute ischemia, or hemorrhage. The ventricles and cortical sulci are unremarkable. Orbits, paranasal sinuses, and mastoid air cells are grossly normal.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No structural pathology, space-occupying lesion, or demyelinating process is identified to explain the patient's atypical migraine symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation shows normal structural anatomy. The ventricular system is normal, with lateral ventricular atria measuring 6.1 mm bilaterally. Sulcation and gyration are appropriate for 29 weeks, demonstrating clear formation of the central sulcus and superior temporal sulcus. The corpus callosum is intact. Fetal visceral structures in the chest and abdomen are normal.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 29 weeks gestation showing appropriate structural development. No cranial or extracranial abnormalities identified.

MR venogram and conventional brain MRI demonstrate absence of the expected flow void in the superior sagittal sinus and left transverse sinus, compatible with dural venous sinus thrombosis. On T2-weighted and DWI sequences, there is a small area of cortical edema and petechial hemorrhage in the left parietal lobe, representing a localized venous congestion/infarct.

Impression: Extensive dural venous sinus thrombosis involving the superior sagittal and left transverse sinuses, with an associated small left parietal venous hemorrhagic infarct.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a well-demarcated cystic lesion with an eccentric, intensely enhancing mural nodule in the right cerebellar hemisphere. The cystic portion of the lesion measures approximately 2.8 x 2.5 cm, producing moderate mass effect on the fourth ventricle and leading to mild dilatation of the third and lateral ventricles. Surrounding vasogenic edema is minimal.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. There is mild obstructive hydrocephalus; correlation with neurosurgical assessment is recommended.

MR imaging reveals a well-circumscribed solid mass in the pineal region measuring 2.3 x 2.1 cm. The lesion shows homogeneous intermediate T1 and T2 signal intensity and demonstrates intense, uniform contrast enhancement. The mass exerts mass effect on the tectal plate, resulting in compression of the aqueduct of Sylvius and mild enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles.
