Impression: Pineal region mass with secondary aqueductal compression and mild ventriculomegaly. Given patient age and appearance, findings are highly suspicious for a pineal germinoma.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates asymmetric dilation of the cerebral ventricles. The right lateral ventricular atrium measures 13.5 mm, indicating moderate ventriculomegaly, while the left lateral ventricular atrium is within normal limits at 8.2 mm. There is no associated midline shift, subependymal heterotopia, or parenchymal destruction. The corpus callosum and cerebellar vermis appear normal for gestational age, and the sulcation pattern is appropriate.

Impression: Moderate isolated right-sided fetal ventriculomegaly. Close prenatal surveillance and repeat scanning are recommended to monitor for progression.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates a normal exam. Cortical development is advanced, showing deep, mature sulci and gyral patterns typical of a near-term fetus. The lateral ventricles measure 6.3 mm in the atrium. All midline intracranial structures are intact, and no thoracic, abdominal, or skeletal abnormalities are seen.

Impression: Normal, mature third-trimester fetal MRI. No intracranial, spinal, or visceral anomalies noted.

A lobulated mass is seen centered in the pineal region, measuring 2.4 x 2.2 cm, demonstrating vivid, heterogeneous enhancement and restricted diffusion. There is compression of the cerebral aqueduct resulting in mild-to-moderate enlargement of the third and lateral ventricles.

Impression: Pineal region mass with secondary ventriculomegaly, concerning for pineoblastoma or germ cell tumor. Close clinical correlation and neurosurgical evaluation are warranted.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced fetal development. Complex secondary and tertiary cerebral sulcation patterns are fully visible and completely appropriate for near-term gestational age. The ventricular atria measure 6.4 mm. The fetal brain, chest, abdomen, and spine show no structural abnormalities.

Impression: Normal near-term fetal MRI study at 35 weeks gestation showing expected anatomical maturation.

Cardiac MRI evaluates for cardiac source of chest pain. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 98 mL and ejection fraction is 63%. Right ventricular end-diastolic volume is 102 mL and ejection fraction is 59%. There is no evidence of myocardial edema, perfusion defects, or late gadolinium enhancement. The coronary artery origins are visualized and appear normal, with the left main and right coronary arteries arising from their respective coronary sinuses.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI study. There is preserved biventricular function, normal coronary artery anatomy, and no evidence of myocarditis or fibrosis.

Cardiac MRI was performed under general anesthesia to evaluate for structural anomalies. Cardiovascular structures show normal situs solitus, systemic and pulmonary venous connections. The atria, ventricles, and great vessels are of normal size and caliber. Left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 65%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 61%. No intracardiac shunts, valvular dysfunction, or regional wall motion abnormalities are identified. T1 and T2 mapping values are within age-specific normal ranges.

Impression: Structurally and functionally normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No congenital cardiovascular anomalies or myocardial tissue abnormalities.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates normal sulcation, consistent with late third-trimester developmental milestones. The primary and secondary sulci are extensively branched, and tertiary sulci are beginning to develop. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.0 mm and 6.2 mm. The corpus callosum and brainstem are entirely normal.

Fetal chest, abdomen, spine, and musculoskeletal systems are structurally normal. Amniotic fluid volume is physiologic. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing expected third-trimester brain development and normal cranial structures.

Cardiac MRI reveals marked asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal septal thickness measuring 24 mm in the basal-to-mid septum. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, resulting in severe left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction and an eccentric, posteriorly directed jet of moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows extensive focal fibrosis (hyperenhancement) at the anterior and posterior right ventricular insertion points.

Impression: Phenotypic expression of Hypertrophic Obstructive Cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with significant LVOT obstruction, secondary mitral regurgitation, and insertion point myocardial fibrosis.

The study demonstrates a moderate-sized global pericardial effusion measuring up to 12 mm in diastole posterior to the left ventricle. The pericardium is thickened (4 mm) and exhibits intense, diffuse hyperenhancement on post-contrast imaging, indicative of active pericardial inflammation. There is no evidence of diastolic collapse of the right atrium or right ventricle to suggest cardiac tamponade.

Biventricular volumes and systolic functions are normal (LVEF 61%, RVEF 55%). Impression: Acute pericarditis with a moderate, hemodynamically non-compromised pericardial effusion and prominent pericardial thickening and enhancement.

Brain MRI reveals a well-defined, solid, hypointense mass on T1-weighted imaging and hyperintense on T2-weighted sequences centered in the midline fourth ventricle, measuring approximately 3.1 x 2.8 x 3.2 cm. The lesion demonstrates restricted diffusion on DWI/ADC mapping and heterogeneous enhancement following gadolinium administration. It causes significant compression of the fourth ventricle and mass effect on the brainstem, leading to severe obstructive hydrocephalus with transependymal flow of CSF in the periventricular white matter.

Impression: Mass in the fourth ventricle causing obstructive hydrocephalus, most characteristic of a medulloblastoma. Urgent neurosurgical evaluation and intervention is recommended.

Brain MRI reveals a well-defined cystic lesion within the right cerebellar hemisphere, measuring 4.2 cm in its greatest dimension, containing a highly enhancing mural nodule measuring approximately 1.5 cm. There is mild surrounding vasogenic edema and mass effect on the fourth ventricle, although the ventricular system remains patent and symmetric without hydrocephalus.

Impression: Cystic cerebellar lesion with an enhancing mural nodule, highly characteristic of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. Differential diagnosis includes hemangioblastoma, though less likely in this demographic.

Neonatal cardiac MRI demonstrates completely normal cardiac situs. The systemic and pulmonary venous connections are normal. Left and right ventricular sizes, wall thicknesses, and systolic functions are normal for gestational and post-natal age. A tiny patent foramen ovale is suspected with a minimal, clinically insignificant left-to-right shunt.

Impression: Unremarkable neonatal cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular volume and function with no major congenital heart anomalies.

MRI of the brain demonstrates multiple, bilateral, asymmetric, poorly-demarcated hyperintense lesions on T2/FLAIR sequences. These lesions are scattered throughout the subcortical and deep cerebral white matter, brainstem, and cerebellar hemispheres, and show patchy, incomplete ring enhancement. No significant mass effect or mass-like shift is visualized.

Impression: Widespread demyelinating lesions of the white matter, consistent with acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) in this pediatric patient. Correlate with history of recent viral illness or vaccination.

Cardiac MRI reveals a bicuspid aortic valve (fusion of the left and right coronary cusps) with eccentric systolic dome opening. A moderate stenotic jet is identified with a peak velocity of 3.2 m/s, accompanied by mild aortic insufficiency (regurgitant fraction 12%). The ascending aorta is dilated, measuring 34 mm (Z-score +3.2), and mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is present.

Impression: Congenital bicuspid aortic valve with moderate aortic stenosis, mild aortic insufficiency, and ascending aortic dilation. Preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (60%).

Brain MR imaging performed for pediatric headache evaluation. The cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres demonstrate normal gray-white matter differentiation. No intracranial masses, abnormal focus areas of restricted diffusion, or pathologic contrast enhancement are observed. The ventricles and extra-axial CSF spaces are within normal limits for patient age.

Visualized paranasal sinuses are clear. Impression: Normal MRI of the brain with no structural or acute intracranial pathology identified to account for headaches.

MRI of the brain was requested following a sports-related concussion. Multiplanar, multisequence brain MRI shows no evidence of acute intraparenchymal, subdural, or epidural hemorrhage. There is no restricted diffusion to suggest acute ischemia, and no cortical contusions. Ventricles and extra-axial fluid spaces are normal in size and location.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain without signs of trauma, hemorrhage, or diffuse axonal injury.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a lumbosacral neural tube defect. There is a defect in the posterior elements of the lower lumbar and sacral spine with herniation of a meningeal sac containing neural elements, consistent with a myelomeningocele. Associated Chiari II malformation is visualized, with herniation of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum and a banana-shaped cerebellum. Bilateral ventriculomegaly is present; the lateral ventricular atria measure 11.2 mm on the left and 11.5 mm on the right.

Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with secondary Chiari II malformation and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly. Neurosurgical fetal intervention program evaluation is advised.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large atrial septal defect (ASD) of the secundum type, measuring approximately 13.5 mm in maximal diameter. There is a substantial left-to-right shunt with a calculated pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp:Qs) of 2.0. Mild-to-moderate dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle is visible, consistent with right-sided volume overload. The right ventricular free wall shows normal wall thickness.

Impression: Secundum atrial septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt and resulting right heart dilation. Right ventricular systolic function remains preserved with an ejection fraction of 57%.

Cardiac MRI evaluated an 18-year-old competitive athlete for screening purposes. The left and right ventricular volumes, wall mass, and wall thickness are within completely normal limits. Global systolic function is preserved with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 64% and right ventricular ejection fraction of 60%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormality, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement.

Heart valves are structurally normal with physiological flow velocities. Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI showing no structural or tissue-level cardiac pathology in this young athlete.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed utilizing pediatric multiplanar and multisequence protocols. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit normal cortical gyration and sulcal patterns for age. There is no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial mass, acute ischemia, hemorrhage, or demyelinating disease. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and subarachnoid spaces are symmetric and unremarkable. The major intracranial arterial flow voids are well-preserved.

Visualized orbital structures, paranasal sinuses, and mastoid air cells are clear. Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain, demonstrating no structural, vascular, or acute pathological changes to account for the patient's symptoms of chronic headaches.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a moderate circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 1.5 cm adjacent to the right ventricle and apex. There is no evidence of diastolic collapse of the right atrium or right ventricle, suggesting no immediate tamponade physiology. The myocardium demonstrates normal signal on T1 and T2 weighted sequences, without evidence of active myocarditis. Ventricular function is normal (EF 62%).

Impression: Moderate circumferential pericardial effusion without MRI evidence of tamponade. No associated myocardial signal abnormalities.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral cortex demonstrates appropriate sulcation for 28 weeks, with clear development of the callosal, cingulate, and calcarine sulci. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with atrial widths of 6.2 mm on the left and 6.1 mm on the right. The corpus callosum is fully formed and visible in its entirety.

The fetal intra-abdominal structures and limbs are normal. Impression: Normal fetal brain and visceral MRI demonstrating age-appropriate structural and neurological development.

MRI of the brain reveals a large, extra-axial CSF-signal intensity lesion in the left middle cranial fossa, measuring 4.2 x 3.0 x 2.8 cm. The lesion follows CSF signal on all sequences, including complete suppression on FLAIR and no restricted diffusion on DWI. There is remodeling of the adjacent sphenoid wing and mild mass effect on the left temporal lobe, without ventricular displacement.

Impression: Large left middle cranial fossa arachnoid cyst (Galassi Type II) with remodeling of the temporal bone and mild mass effect on the temporal lobe, but without midline shift or hydrocephalus.

Brain MRI was obtained to evaluate developmental delay. Symmetrical cortical development and normal gyral patterns are demonstrated. The corpus callosum is intact and fully formed. Myelination pattern is appropriate for a two-year-old child. There are no areas of restricted diffusion, focal masses, or abnormal extra-axial fluid collections.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, migrational, or myelination abnormalities identified to explain developmental delay.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 32 weeks gestation shows normal, age-appropriate intracranial development. The brain parenchymal signals are within normal limits. The ventricular atrial widths are symmetric, measuring 5.8 mm on the left and 6.0 mm on the right, well below the threshold for ventriculomegaly. Cerebral sulcation patterns, including the development of the parieto-occipital and calcarine sulci, are appropriate for 32 weeks.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation. Fetal brain anatomy, ventricular sizes, and sulcation patterns are entirely within normal limits for gestational age.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a Double Outlet Right Ventricle (DORV) of the Taussig-Bing variety. Both the aorta and the pulmonary trunk arise entirely from the morphologic right ventricle. A large, non-restrictive subpulmonary ventricular septal defect (VSD) is visualized, measuring approximately 11 mm. There is marked right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation, with preserved right ventricular systolic function (EF 54%). The left ventricle is hypoplastic but has normal intrinsic contractility.

Impression: Double outlet right ventricle with a large subpulmonary VSD (Taussig-Bing anomaly), resulting in right ventricular volume and pressure overload.

Brain MRI demonstrates a cluster of tightly packed vascular flow voids with a 'bag of worms' appearance in the right parietal lobe, measuring 2.4 x 2.2 cm. There is associated T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the surrounding brain parenchyma, but no evidence of acute or chronic hemorrhage on SWI. Post-contrast imaging shows a prominent feeding artery originating from the right middle cerebral artery and a dilated draining vein heading toward the superior sagittal sinus.

Impression: Unruptured right parietal arteriovenous malformation (AVM). Neurosurgery and interventional neurorology consultation is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The liver and portion of the ascending colon have herniated into the right thoracic cavity, displacing the heart leftward. The left lung is compressed but visible. Fetal lung-to-head ratio (LHR) and lung volumes are severely compromised. Intracranial structures are unremarkable, with normal ventricular size (atrial width 5.9 mm).

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation and severe compression of the right lung.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a skin-covered neural tube defect. There is a focal spina bifida defect at the mid-thoracic level, associated with a closed meningocele sac. Importantly, the cerebellar vermis and brainstem are normally positioned with a preserved cisterna magna, indicating the absence of an active Chiari II malformation. The lateral ventricles are normal in size, measuring 6.2 mm.

Impression: Closed thoracic meningocele (spina bifida) without signs of Chiari II malformation or hydrocephalus. Brain anatomy is otherwise normal for 21 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI reveals severe global dilation of the left ventricle with an indexed end-diastolic volume of 132 mL/m2. Left ventricular systolic function is severely depressed with a global ejection fraction of 28%. Diffuse thinning of the LV myocardium is noted. There is mild, non-specific mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement in the interventricular septum, typical of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy. Mild functional mitral regurgitation is present due to annular dilation.

Impression: Severe left ventricular dilation and systolic dysfunction, highly consistent with pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced development of the fetal brain. Well-defined secondary and tertiary sulci, including the parieto-occipital, calcarine, and central sulci, are visible and appropriate for 35 weeks. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with the atrium measuring 6.4 mm. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures show normal maturation and signaling.

The surrounding anatomical structures in the fetal neck, chest, and abdomen are completely normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 35 weeks gestation showing age-appropriate cortical sulcal maturation.

Cardiac MRI reveals a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 12 mm in diameter. There is moderate dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, reflecting a significant left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs ratio of approximately 1.8:1. Right ventricular systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 56%.

Impression: Secundum atrial septal defect with moderate right heart chamber enlargement secondary to a significant left-to-right shunt.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the pediatric heart was performed using multiplanar, ECG-gated cine balanced steady-state free precession sequences. Both left and right ventricles demonstrate normal cavity dimensions, normal myocardial thickness, and preserved systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 63%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. No structural abnormalities, septal defects, or anomalies of the great vessels are identified.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural heart disease, shunt, or ventricular dysfunction.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral dilatation of the lateral ventricles. The left ventricular atrium measures 13.8 mm, and the right ventricular atrium measures 14.2 mm, consistent with moderate bilateral ventriculomegaly. The third and fourth ventricles are normal in size. The cerebral cortex shows normal opercularization and sulcation patterns for 26 weeks gestation, without evidence of polymicrogyria or heterotopia.

Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are intact. Close follow-up is recommended to assess for progression.

Cardiac MRI shows a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 1.8 cm in diameter. There is significant volume overload of the right heart, with moderate dilation of both the right atrium and the right ventricle. Calculated shunt flow Qp:Qs is 1.9. Right ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 55%, and left ventricular ejection fraction is 61%.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with significant right-to-left/left-to-right shunting and secondary right heart dilation.

The patient underwent cardiac MRI for evaluation of a mild pericardial friction rub and chest pain following a viral illness. Left and right ventricular chambers are of normal caliber and demonstrate preserved, symmetrical wall motion. Calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. T2-weighted and native T1 mapping sequences reveal normal myocardial values, without any evidence of edema, active inflammation, or myocardial scar.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI with no objective findings of acute myocarditis, myocardial scar, or structural abnormality. No pericardial effusion or thickening is seen.

Brain MRI demonstrates complete absence of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles show a parallel configuration with prominent dilation of the occipital horns (colpocephaly) and a classic 'steer-horn' morphology on coronal views. Probst bundles are visualized running along the medial margins of the hemispheres. No other major focal abnormalities are seen.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with characteristic colpocephaly. No other associated midline or migration abnormalities identified.

Cardiac MRI shows localized dyskinesia and bulging of the right ventricular free wall, particularly in the region of the RV outflow tract. The right ventricle is dilated with an end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m2, and right ventricular ejection fraction is reduced at 38%. T1-weighted and late gadolinium enhancement sequences reveal focal areas of fatty infiltration and scarring within the RV free wall.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting multiple major Task Force criteria. Clinical correlation and electrophysiologic evaluation are recommended.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a large cystic space in the posterior fossa that communicates widely with the enlarged fourth ventricle, associated with severe cerebellar vermian hypoplasia. The cerebellar hemispheres are displaced anterolaterally. There is moderate supratentorial ventriculomegaly, with the right atrium measuring 12.0 mm and the left measuring 12.2 mm. Sulcation is otherwise within normal parameters.

Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation with severe vermian hypoplasia and moderate supratentorial ventriculomegaly at 26 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly with dilation of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles and parallel alignment of the lateral ventricles (steer-horn configuration). The third ventricle is superiorly displaced. The cerebral sulcation and gyration are otherwise appropriate for 32 weeks gestation, with no migratory anomalies noted.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly. No other intracranial abnormalities are identified on current imaging.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral renal agenesis. No renal parenchymal tissue or renal arteries are identified in either renal fossa or ectopic abdominal locations. There is complete absence of the urinary bladder. Severe anhydramnios (complete lack of amniotic fluid) is present, resulting in severe compression and crowding of the fetus, limiting clear visualization of the distal limbs.

The fetal lungs are hypoplastic and small for gestational age, and the brain appears compressed but anatomically gross intact. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis and severe anhydramnios, highly suspicious for lethal Potter sequence with secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

MRI of the brain was performed utilizing our standard pediatric epilepsy protocol, including high-resolution 3D T1-weighted and FLAIR sequences. Careful evaluation of the temporal lobes, hippocampal formations, and neocortex reveals normal structural architecture. There is no evidence of mesial temporal sclerosis, focal cortical dysplasia, cavernous malformation, or structural developmental delay. Ventricular anatomy and extra-axial spaces are within normal limits.

Impression: Unremarkable and structurally normal brain MRI. No epileptogenic lesion, cortical malformation, or pathologic intracranial signal anomaly detected.

MR brain imaging demonstrates a well-demarcated, non-enhancing CSF-like mass within the right cerebellopontine angle, measuring 2.8 x 2.2 x 2.0 cm. The lesion is hyperintense on T2-weighted imaging and fails to suppress completely on FLAIR sequences. It exhibits marked, homogeneous restricted diffusion on DWI sequences, causing mild displacement of the adjacent cerebellar hemisphere.

Impression: Right cerebellopontine angle mass showing characteristic restricted diffusion, indicative of an epidermoid cyst. No significant mass effect on the brainstem.

Brain MRI and MR angiography demonstrate a cluster of tightly packed vascular flow voids in the left temporoparietal region, measuring 2.4 x 2.1 cm. This vascular nidus is supplied by branches of the left middle cerebral artery and drains into the superior sagittal sinus via an enlarged cortical vein. No acute hemorrhage or adjacent parenchymal edema is seen.

Impression: Left temporoparietal arteriovenous malformation (AVM) without evidence of acute rupture. Recommend formal catheter angiographic correlation and neurosurgical consultation.

Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain demonstrates normal ventricular size and configuration. The cerebral cortex shows preserved gray-white matter differentiation with a normal sulcal pattern. There are no areas of abnormal signal intensity, restricted diffusion, or pathological contrast enhancement within the parenchymal structures. Visualized orbits and paranasal sinuses are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No structural abnormality, acute ischemic change, or intracranial mass is identified to explain the patient's headaches.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was completed using multiplanar sequences. The brain parenchyma is structurally normal for age, and myelination is complete and appropriate. There are no cortical malformations, focal signals of demyelination, or signs of elevated intracranial pressure. Auditory and optical pathways are intact.

Impression: Normal MR brain. No evidence of mass lesion, structural injury, or anomalous development to explain the patient's acute-onset sensorineural hearing loss.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a localized area of cortical thickening and blurring of the gray-white matter junction within the posterior aspect of the left superior frontal gyrus. There is hyperintense signal extending from the abnormal cortex toward the left lateral ventricle on T2 and FLAIR imaging (known as the 'transmantle sign'). There is no surrounding edema or associated mass effect.

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) in the left superior frontal gyrus, highly associated with the patient's refractory partial epilepsy. Neurosurgical epilepsy clinic referral is recommended.

Brain MRI was obtained to evaluate a first-time generalized tonic-clonic seizure. Multiplanar sequences demonstrate symmetric myelination and brain maturation patterns appropriate for a 2-year-old child. There are no signs of cortical dysplasia, hippocampal atrophy, or focal signal abnormalities on FLAIR or T2-weighted sequences. No mass lesions, vascular malformations, or areas of restricted diffusion are visualized.

Impression: Normal pediatric brain MRI. No structural abnormality, migration defect, or focus of ischemia identified to explain the new-onset seizure activity.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates marked bilateral lateral ventriculomegaly. The left atrium measures 14.2 mm, and the right atrium measures 13.8 mm, indicating severe symmetric dilation. There is associated thinning and stretching of the corpus callosum and mild dangling of the choroid plexus bilaterally. The cerebral cortex shows appropriate sulcation for gestational age, with no migration defects.

Remaining fetal anatomy, including the thoracic cavity and kidneys, is within normal limits. Impression: Moderate to severe bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly without associated intracranial anomalies. Close postnatal neurosurgical follow-up is recommended.

Cardiac MRI reveals normal pediatric cardiovascular anatomy. The ventricles demonstrate appropriate size, wall thickness, and function for a 3-year-old child. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 68 mL/m² and the right ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 71 mL/m². Left and right ventricular ejection fractions are calculated at 63% and 60%, respectively, without focal wall motion anomalies.

All four pulmonary veins drain normally into the left atrium, and systemic venous return is unremarkable. There is no evidence of intra-atrial or intra-ventricular shunt, and late gadolinium enhancement is negative. Impression: Entirely normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No congenital structural anomalies, shunts, or functional abnormalities.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates normal development. The brain exhibits cortical folding and primary sulcation patterns entirely appropriate for 27 weeks. The ventricular system is normal, with atrial width measuring 6.0 mm. The brainstem, cerebellum, and corpus callosum appear morphologically unremarkable. Fetal lungs, abdominal organs, and spine are intact with normal appearances.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural and neurodevelopmental parameters at 27 weeks gestation.

MR imaging of the brain in this infant demonstrates a markedly enlarged posterior fossa with severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle. There is upward displacement of the tentorium and transverse sinuses. Associated moderate lateral and third ventricular enlargement is noted, suggesting progressive ventriculomegaly.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation with severe vermian hypoplasia and hydrocephalus. Close monitoring of head circumference and neurosurgical review is warranted.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a normal singleton fetus. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.1 mm bilaterally, and the parenchymal signal is unremarkable. The Sylvian fissure opercularization is appropriate for gestational age, and the posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, are anatomically intact.

All fetal organs, including the stomach, lungs, heart, and urinary bladder, are well-positioned and normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate developmental morphology.

The examination reveals severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the interventricular septum measuring up to 24 mm in end-diastole, causing obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT). There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, associated with moderate eccentric mitral regurgitation. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows focal fibrosis at the anterior and posterior RV insertion points.

Impression: Asymmetric hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with severe septal hypertrophy, SAM of the mitral valve, and associated LVOT obstruction. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 75%.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a discrete narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The narrowest segment measures 6.5 mm in diameter, compared to the distal arch diameter of 14 mm. Collateral vascular channels, including enlarged internal mammary and intercostal arteries, are prominent. Left ventricular myocardium shows mild concentric hypertrophy with an ejection fraction of 58% and a stroke volume of 75 mL. No evidence of global hypokinesia is identified on short-axis cine imaging.

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the aorta with associated left ventricular concentric hypertrophy. Well-developed collateral circulation. Clinical correlation for blood pressure gradients across the upper and lower extremities is recommended.

Cardiac MR study reveals normal biventricular size and function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 74 mL/m² with an ejection fraction of 64%. The right ventricle is non-dilated with an ejection fraction of 60%. Myocardial perfusion is uniform throughout, and there is no evidence of late gadolinium enhancement to suggest focal myocardial fibrosis or scarring.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal ventricular volumes, intact systolic function, and no evidence of myocardial scar or active inflammation.

Brain MRI of a 2-month-old infant born prematurely demonstrates hyperintense material on T1 and hypointense on T2 along the ependymal linings of both lateral ventricles, consistent with resolving subependymal and intraventricular hemorrhage. There is mild asymmetric enlargement of the occipital horns of both lateral ventricles (colpocephaly), though the third and fourth ventricles are normal in size. No periventricular leukomalacia is seen.

Impression: Resolving bilateral Grade II intraventricular hemorrhage with mild post-hemorrhagic ventriculomegaly. Close monitoring with head ultrasound or follow-up MR is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced brain development. Extensive sulcation and gyral maturation are appropriate for 35 weeks. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with symmetric atria measuring 5.2 mm. Midline structures, including the corpus callosum and cavum septum pellucidum, are normal in morphology. The posterior fossa, including the vermis and cisterna magna, is completely unremarkable.

All extracranial structures, including the spine, chest, heart, gastrointestinal system, and kidneys, are normal. Impression: Normal third-trimester fetal MRI showing completely unremarkable anatomy and excellent structural brain development.

MR of the brain in this 9-month-old infant demonstrates moderate symmetrical dilatation of the lateral ventricles, with periventricular white matter thinning and a abnormal pattern of periventricular T2 hyperintensity. Susceptibility-weighted sequences show focal areas of periventricular calcification, particularly along the subependymal lining of the caudostriate notch.

Impression: Ventriculomegaly and characteristic periventricular calcification patterns, consistent with sequelae of congenital Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection. Clinical correlation with pediatric infectious disease and audiology is recommended.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed retrocerebellar fluid collection measuring 4.2 x 3.5 x 2.8 cm. The collection follows CSF signal intensity on all pulse sequences, including complete suppression on FLAIR and absence of restricted diffusion on DWI. There is mild scalloping of the inner table of the occipital bone and minimal mass effect on the cerebellar hemispheres.

Impression: Large, benign retrocerebellar arachnoid cyst. No hydrocephalus or significant compression of the brainstem or fourth ventricle is identified.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks and 3 days of gestation shows normal intracranial development. The bilateral lateral ventricles are symmetric and normal in caliber, with the left atrium measuring 5.4 mm and the right atrium measuring 5.6 mm. The cerebral cortex shows normal, age-appropriate smooth parenchymal configuration with early sylvian fissure development. The corpus callosum is visualized and appears intact. The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellum and brainstem, are within normal limits.

Impression: Normal fetal brain MRI for 22 weeks of gestation. No structural brain abnormalities or ventriculomegaly identified.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates features consistent with semilobar holoprosencephaly. The cerebral hemispheres are fused anteriorly, and there is a single monoventricle with partial development of the occipital horns. The thalami are partially fused. The corpus callosum is absent. Cortical sulcal formation is primitive, which is expected for 20 weeks but also limited by the structural malformation. Additionally, facial structures demonstrate hypotelorism.

The fetal spine, thoracic, and abdominal cavities are otherwise normal, and amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits. Impression: Semilobar holoprosencephaly with fused anterior cerebral hemispheres, monoventricle, and hypotelorism.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals a neural tube defect located in the lower lumbar spine. There is an open spinal dysraphism at the L4-S1 levels, characterized by herniation of the meninges and neural elements into an external sac, measuring 2.1 x 1.8 cm. Associated Chiari II malformation is present, with pointing of the frontal horns (lemon sign) and herniation of the cerebellar vermis below the foramen magnum.

The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with atrial measurements of 12.0 mm bilaterally. The remainder of the fetal organ systems are normally formed. Impression: Lumbar myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation and bilateral moderate ventriculomegaly.

MR imaging of the brain in this patient with known neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) demonstrates diffuse, fusiform enlargement of the optic chiasm and the pre-chiasmatic portion of both optic nerves. The involved structures show T2/FLAIR hyperintensity and moderate, patchy enhancement following gadolinium administration. Unidentified bright objects (UBOs) typical of NF1 are also noted in the bilateral globus pallidus.

Impression: Optic pathway glioma involving the optic chiasm and bilateral optic nerves, consistent with the patient's NF1 diagnosis. UBOs in the basal ganglia are also noted.

Cardiac MRI evaluates an infant with Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome (HLHS) status post-Stage II bidirectional Glenn shunt. The left ventricle is diminutive and non-functional, as expected. The right ventricle serves as the systemic pump and shows mild dilatation with an end-diastolic volume index of 110 mL/m², and a mildly reduced systemic ejection fraction of 46%. No regional wall motion abnormalities are present.

The bidirectional superior cavopulmonary (Glenn) anastomosis is widely patent with normal, laminar flow into both the left and right pulmonary arteries. There is no evidence of narrowing or obstruction at the anastomosis site, and the branch pulmonary arteries are well-developed. Impression: Status post-Stage II Glenn palliation for HLHS, demonstrating a patent Glenn shunt, mild systemic right ventricular dilatation, and mild systolic dysfunction.

Cardiac MRI shows severe, asymmetric hypertrophy of the left ventricle, primarily involving the anterior septum and anterior wall. The maximal wall thickness measures 24 mm in the mid-ventricular septum. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve leading to dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction, with a peak instantaneous gradient of 42 mmHg during systole. Focal, patchy mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement is present at the RV-LV insertion points.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with severe septal hypertrophy, SAM of the mitral valve, and classic LGE at the insertion points.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the heart was performed for evaluation of atypical chest pain and palpitations in a 16-year-old female athlete. Multiplanar, multisequence cardiac imaging demonstrates normal biventricular volumes, myocardial mass, and global systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 60%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormalities, myocardial edema on T2-weighted imaging, or late gadolinium enhancement to suggest myocardial scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI study. There is no structural heart disease, myocarditis, or objective markers of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy to explain the patient's symptoms.

The study demonstrates double outlet right ventricle (DORV), where both the aorta and the pulmonary trunk arise almost entirely from the right ventricle. A large, non-restrictive subaortic ventricular septal defect (VSD) is present, which allows systemic venous flow to enter the left-sided circulation. Severe right ventricular hypertrophy is noted secondary to systemic pressure exposure.

Impression: Double outlet right ventricle with a large subaortic ventricular septal defect and severe right ventricular hypertrophy. Surgical pathway evaluation is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal structural development. The fetal brain shows appropriate configuration with symmetric ventricles measuring 5.8 mm. Cortical plate development is unremarkable for this early gestational age. The brainstem, cerebellum, and corpus callosum are normal.

The fetal chest, cardiac position, abdominal organs, and kidneys are normal. The spine is completely intact. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 20 weeks gestation.

High-resolution coronary MRA was performed to monitor coronary artery aneurysms secondary to atypical Kawasaki disease. There is a giant saccular aneurysm of the proximal left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery, measuring 9.5 mm in maximum diameter, with sluggish internal blood flow but no thrombus. A smaller 4.2 mm fusiform aneurysm is also seen in the proximal right coronary artery (RCA). Myocardial perfusion and late-phase LGE imaging show no evidence of prior myocardial infarction.

Impression: Coronary artery aneurysms secondary to Kawasaki disease, including a giant proximal LAD aneurysm. Biventricular function remains completely normal (LVEF 64%) with no myocardial scarring.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging evaluates the thoracic aorta and ventricular volumes. The aortic arch is left-sided and shows normal branching. Both right and left ventricles demonstrate normal cavity sizes, normal wall thickness, and preserved systolic function (LVEF 65%, RVEF 62%). No regional wall motion abnormalities or delayed myocardial enhancement are identified. Valvular flow patterns are physiological.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI with unremarkable structural and functional parameters.

Cardiac MRI of this 3-month-old female infant reveals a large, perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 8 mm in diameter. There is a prominent left-to-right shunt with a calculated Qp:Qs ratio of 2.1, indicating significant pulmonary overcirculation. The left atrium and left ventricle are moderately dilated, reflecting chronic volume overload, though left ventricular systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 62%.

Impression: Large perimembranous ventricular septal defect with severe left-to-right shunt and left-sided cardiac chamber volume overload. No pulmonary arterial hypertension signs are noted on current imaging.

Cardiac MRI shows normal cardiac dimensions, intact atrial and ventricular septa, and unremarkable pericardium. Great vessels are normal in size and exhibit standard anatomic orientation. There is no evidence of myocardial edema, delayed enhancement, or perfusion defects. Valves are structurally thin and mobile with no hemodynamically significant regurgitation.

Impression: Completely normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No evidence of cardiomyopathy, congenital cardiac defect, or acute inflammatory processes.

MRI study of the brain was performed utilizing specialized epilepsy protocols including high-resolution 3D FLAIR and T1-weighted sequences. No focal areas of cortical dysplasia, hippocampal atrophy, or signal asymmetry in the temporal lobes are identified. The ventricles and extra-axial CSF spaces are unremarkable.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No structural abnormality, vascular lesion, or hippocampal sclerosis identified to explain the patient's new-onset seizure.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals a partially agenetic corpus callosum. The anterior callosal body and genu are present, but the posterior body and splenium are absent. There is a mild degree of colpocephaly with dilated occipital horns. The right atrium measures 9.8 mm and the left atrium measures 9.5 mm, representing borderline-to-mild ventriculomegaly.

Sulcul development is slightly asymmetric but overall age-appropriate. No associated migration defects or intracranial hemorrhage is identified. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated borderline bilateral ventriculomegaly and colpocephaly.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation shows a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The stomach and several loops of bowel, along with a portion of the left lobe of the liver, are displaced into the left chest. This results in significant compression of the mediastinal structures and a severe rightward shift of the heart. The right lung is compressed but visible. Fetal brain imaging shows normal sulcation and normal ventricles, with atria measuring 6.3 mm.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation, severe mediastinal shift, and high risk of pulmonary hypoplasia. Multi-disciplinary delivery planning at a tertiary center is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates advanced gyral and sulcal patterns, appropriate for late third-trimester development, with prominent tertiary sulci and tight opercularization. The ventricular atria measure 6.0 mm. Brain parenchyma, corpus callosum, and posterior fossa are unremarkable. Normal fetal thoracic, abdominal, and skeletal structures are observed. Amniotic fluid volume is normal.

Impression: Unremarkable and normal fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation, showing expected advanced central nervous system maturation and normal anatomy.

High-resolution epilepsy protocol MRI demonstrates focal cortical thickening and blurring of the gray-white matter junction in the right frontal lobe, with associated hyperintensity on T2/FLAIR sequences. A thin band of T2 hyperintensity extends from the abnormal cortex toward the right lateral ventricle, illustrating the transmantle sign.

Impression: Cortical dysplasia in the right frontal lobe, highly consistent with focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) Type II, explaining the focal epilepsy history.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 11 mm in maximal dimension. There is a prominent left-to-right shunt with a calculated Qp:Qs ratio of 1.8:1. Right ventricular dilation is present, with an end-diastolic volume index (RVEDVI) of 112 mL/m², indicating right-sided volume overload. The right ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 57%. The pulmonary veins drain normally into the left atrium.

Impression: Secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) with a significant left-to-right shunt and resulting moderate right ventricular dilation. Left ventricular size and function are normal.

Brain MRI demonstrates multifocal, poorly demarcated, bilateral asymmetric areas of high signal intensity on T2/FLAIR sequences involving both the subcortical white matter and deep gray matter nuclei. Some lesions show faint, incomplete ring-like enhancement on post-contrast imaging. No significant mass effect or midline shift is observed.

Impression: Findings are highly suggestive of Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis (ADEM), consistent with the clinical picture of post-infectious neurological decline.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a large perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD). The defect measures approximately 8.5 mm in diameter, demonstrating a significant left-to-right shunt with a calculated Qp:Qs ratio of 2.1:1. Moderate dilation of the left atrium and left ventricle is present, consistent with chronic volume overload. The right ventricular size and pressure indices remain within normal limits, and there is no evidence of pulmonary arterial hypertension.

Impression: Large perimembranous ventricular septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt (Qp:Qs 2.1) and secondary left-sided chamber dilation. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 60%.

Cardiac MRI is requested for a 16-year-old male with acute onset of crushing chest pain and elevated troponins following a viral illness. T2-weighted and T2-mapping sequences demonstrate diffuse myocardial edema within the subepicardium and mid-myocardium of the lateral and apical walls of the left ventricle. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging confirms patchy, non-ischemic subepicardial hyperenhancement in the identical regions. Left ventricular dimensions are normal, but the global ejection fraction is mildly depressed at 51%.

No significant pericardial effusion is visualized, and right ventricular size and function remain normal (RVEF 56%). Impression: Cardiac MRI findings satisfy the Lake Louise criteria for acute myocarditis, demonstrating myocardial edema and non-ischemic subepicardial fibrosis.

MRI of the heart demonstrates severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy, maximal at the mid-ventricular and basal septum, measuring up to 21 mm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve, resulting in moderate posteriorly-directed mitral regurgitation and dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 76%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals patchy mid-myocardial enhancement at the insertion points of the interventricular septum, indicating localized fibrosis.

Impression: Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) characterized by severe asymmetric septal hypertrophy, dynamic LVOT obstruction, and localized myocardial fibrosis. Cardiologist follow-up for sudden cardiac death risk stratification is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal anatomy. Cerebral sulcation is early and appropriate for 21 weeks, with a well-developed corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and within normal limits; the left atrium measures 5.2 mm and the right measures 5.1 mm. The chest, heart, diaphragm, liver, stomach, and kidneys are all normally situated without focal abnormalities.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestational age. No structural anomalies detected in the brain or fetal body.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate appropriate development and early sulcation patterns for this gestational age. The lateral ventricles are normal in size, with the atrial width measuring 5.8 mm. Posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis and brainstem, are unremarkable. Normal fluid signal is seen within the stomach and bladder, and the fetal spine is intact.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural development and intracranial anatomy at 22 weeks gestation. No structural defects or intracranial abnormalities identified.

Brain MRI demonstrates age-appropriate myelination patterns and cerebral volume. The corpus callosum is intact and normal in caliber. There are no migration anomalies, heterotopias, or white matter signal abnormalities. The ventricles, sulci, and posterior fossa structures are entirely unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, migratory, or myelination disorders identified to explain developmental delay.

MRI of the brain was performed to evaluate global developmental delay. Brain structure is completely normal for developmental age. The myelination pattern is symmetric and appropriate for an 18-month-old. The corpus callosum is intact, the ventricular system is normal in caliber, and the subarachnoid spaces show no pathologic widening. No focal signal abnormalities or structural anomalies of the cortex are seen.

Impression: Normal brain MRI with age-appropriate myelination. No structural or myelination abnormalities identified to account for global developmental delay.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates massive distension of the fetal urinary bladder with associated bilateral hydroureteronephrosis. The renal parenchyma is thinned, particularly on the left, which shows increased T2 signaling concerning for dysplastic changes. The proximal urethra is dilated, creating a keyhole appearance characteristic of posterior urethral valves. There is moderate oligohydramnios. Fetal brain anatomy, ventricular atrial width (5.2 mm), and spine are unremarkable.

Impression: Posterior urethral valves with severe bilateral hydroureteronephrosis, thinned dysplastic-appearing renal parenchyma, and moderate oligohydramnios. Urgent fetal urology and maternal-fetal medicine evaluation are indicated.

Cardiac MRI performed to evaluate atypical chest pain in an 11-year-old female. Cine imaging demonstrates normal global and regional biventricular wall motion, with an LV ejection fraction of 62% and an RV ejection fraction of 58%. All cardiac chambers are normal in size and volume, with no evidence of hypertrophy, dilation, or valvular disease.

Myocardial perfusion sequences during first-pass gadolinium transit are normal, and there is no evidence of late gadolinium enhancement or edema on T2-weighted sequences. Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI with normal ventricular volumes, preserved systolic function, and no evidence of myocardial inflammation, scar, or perfusion defects.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate palpitations in an 18-year-old male. Multiplanar, multisequence cine imaging demonstrates normal left and right ventricular volumes and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities are identified. T2-weighted and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences demonstrate no myocardial edema or focal myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No structural, functional, or infiltrative abnormalities are visualized to explain the patient's symptoms of palpitations.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 8.5 mm in diameter. There is a prominent left-to-right shunt with a calculated Qp:Qs ratio of 2.1:1. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is elevated at 98 mL/m², consistent with moderate left-sided volume overload. Left ventricular ejection fraction remains preserved at 64%. Right ventricular pressure is estimated to be mildly elevated with trace tricuspid regurgitation.

Impression: Large perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) causing moderate left-sided volume overload and a significant left-to-right shunt. Close clinical correlation and surgical consultation are recommended.

MRI of the brain demonstrates multiple subependymal nodules along the walls of the lateral ventricles, some of which exhibit calcification. There are also several cortical tubers, appearing as areas of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the subcortical white matter of both cerebral hemispheres. A 1.1 cm subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) is noted near the left foramen of Monro without obstruction.

Impression: Findings highly characteristic of tuberous sclerosis complex, including cortical tubers, subependymal nodules, and a stable subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA).

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniation of the stomach, spleen, and small bowel loops into the left chest is observed, causing a severe rightward shift of the heart and mediastinum. The left lung is severely compressed and hypoplastic. The total fetal lung volume is significantly reduced below normal values for 24 weeks gestation.

The brain anatomy is unremarkable; the lateral ventricular atria are normal and measure 6.5 mm on both sides. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with significant lung compression and mediastinal shift. Suggest immediate multidisciplinary neonatology and pediatric surgery referral.

Sports screening due to family history of cardiomyopathy. The cardiac MRI reveals normal cardiac anatomy and normal chamber sizes. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 65% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%. Wall thickness is normal throughout the left ventricle, and no late gadolinium enhancement is observed.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, arrhythmogenic substrate, or other structural pathology.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals a large left-sided diaphragmatic defect. There is herniation of the stomach, multiple small bowel loops, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe into the left hemithorax. This mass effect results in a severe contralateral mediastinal shift to the right and compression of the developing fetal lungs. The total lung volume is significantly reduced, indicating high risk for pulmonary hypoplasia.

Evaluation of the fetal brain demonstrates normal intracranial structures with symmetric ventricular atria measuring 5.4 mm. Sulcation and gyration are normal for 25 weeks. Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) containing stomach, bowel, and liver, with marked mediastinal shift. Brain development remains structurally normal.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 2-month-old infant presenting with mild stridor and a suspected vascular ring. High-resolution anatomical sequences demonstrate a normal left-sided aortic arch with normal branching pattern. There is no evidence of a double aortic arch, right-sided arch with aberrant left subclavian, or ligamentum arteriosum compressing the trachea or esophagus. The trachea is patent without significant extrinsic narrowing. Intracardiac anatomy is completely normal with intact septa and normal ventricular function.

Impression: Completely normal aortic arch and cardiac anatomy. No evidence of a vascular ring, sling, or airway compression.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal left ventricular end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVI) of 72 mL/m2 and right ventricular end-diastolic volume index (RVEDVI) of 75 mL/m2. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is calculated at 62%, and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 58%. No abnormal late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is observed to suggest myocardial scar or focal fibrosis. Native T1 and T2 mapping parameters are within normal physiological limits for the patient's age.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of congenital cardiac anomaly, ventricular dysfunction, or myocardial inflammation.

Brain MRI demonstrates multiple subependymal nodules lining the lateral ventricles, measuring up to 6 mm. High T2/FLAIR signal cortical tubers are observed within the bifrontal and right parietal lobes. There is no evidence of giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) development at the foramina of Monro. No mass effect or hydrocephalus is identified.

Impression: Features are classic for Tuberous Sclerosis Complex, including subependymal nodules and cortical tubers. No obstructive lesions are identified at this time.

Fetal MRI performed at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates expected anatomical development. The cerebral hemispheres are smooth, showing primary fissure formation appropriate for this early stage. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with the atrium measuring 5.2 mm. Midline structures and the posterior fossa are intact.

The spine, thoracic organs, and abdominal viscera show no gross abnormalities. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation showing normal development of the fetal brain, spine, and major organ systems.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with absence of the posterior body and splenium. The anterior body and genu are present but thin. There is mild bilateral ventriculomegaly with the atria measuring 10.8 mm on the left and 10.5 mm on the right, presenting a mild teardrop appearance. Sulcal patterns are appropriate for 27 weeks.

Impression: Partial corpus callosum agenesis with mild ventriculomegaly. Prenatal counseling and postnatal neurodevelopmental evaluation are advised.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a devastating intracranial abnormality. There is near-complete absence of the cerebral hemispheres, which are replaced by a large, fluid-filled cavity. The thalami and brainstem are preserved, and a thin rim of occipital cortex is noted. The skull vault is intact. The lateral ventricular structures cannot be normally defined due to the destruction of the parenchyma. The posterior fossa structures are relatively spared.

Impression: Fetal hydranencephaly. There is near-complete loss of the cerebral hemispheres, with preservation of the brainstem and thalami. Maternal and pediatric neurology consultations are recommended.

Pediatric cardiac MRI shows normal intracardiac anatomy, chamber sizes, and ventricular function. No atrial or ventricular septal defects are visualized. The origins and pathways of the coronary arteries are normal. Flow velocity profiles across the systemic and pulmonary systems are normal without evidence of stenosis, regurgitation, or shunt. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 65%.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI for age. No structural congenital heart disease or cardiomyopathy detected.

Brain MR performed for workup of macrocephaly. The cerebral ventricles are prominent, particularly the lateral ventricles, but are symmetric without transependymal edema or midline shift. The subarachnoid spaces along the frontal and temporal convexities are mildly widened. Cortical folding, grey-white differentiation, and myelination progression are normal and age-appropriate.

Impression: Prominent ventricles and subarachnoid spaces, consistent with benign enlargement of the subarachnoid spaces of infancy (BESSI). No findings suggestive of obstructive hydrocephalus or mass lesion.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The liver and portions of the bowel are herniated into the right hemithorax, resulting in leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the heart and left lung. The O/E LHR is calculated at 45%, suggesting moderate pulmonary hypoplasia.

Intracranial structures are normal with symmetric ventricles (5.9 mm). Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic liver herniation and moderate pulmonary hypoplasia.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals a severe abnormality of the posterior fossa, characterized by significant hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis and massive cystic dilatation of the posterior fossa CSF space. This cyst communicates widely with the fourth ventricle. There is marked elevation of the tentorium and torcula. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with the atria measuring 12.4 mm. The cortical sulcation pattern is appropriate for 25 weeks gestation.

The thoracic, abdominal, and musculoskeletal structures of the fetus are normal. Amniotic fluid volume is within expected limits. Impression: Anatomic features are diagnostic of a classic Dandy-Walker malformation with associated mild to moderate ventriculomegaly.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior callosal body and genu are visualized, but there is complete absence of the posterior body and splenium. There is mild colpocephaly with lateral ventricular atria measuring 9.0 mm on the left and 8.8 mm on the right. Radial sulcation is mildly apparent along the medial cerebral walls. The posterior fossa structures are within normal limits.

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with mild colpocephaly and early radial sulcation at 23 weeks gestation.

Cine MRI sequences reveal a large, perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 8.5 mm. Velocity-encoded phase-contrast imaging demonstrates a significant left-to-right shunt with a calculated pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp/Qs) of 1.9. There is moderate enlargement of both the left atrium and left ventricle, consistent with pulmonary-to-systemic volume overload. Right ventricular systolic pressure is estimated to be mildly elevated, but biventricular function remains preserved (LVEF 62%, RVEF 55%).

Impression: Large perimembranous ventricular septal defect with a significant left-to-right shunt (Qp/Qs = 1.9), resulting in left-sided chamber dilatation and volume overload.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a large sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT). The mass is predominantly external, arising from the sacrococcygeal region and measuring approximately 7.5 x 6.8 x 6.2 cm. It has mixed cystic and solid components with mild intrapelvic extension. No evidence of urinary obstruction or spinal dysraphism is present. The fetal brain shows appropriate sulcation; ventricular atrial width is 6.1 mm.

Impression: Large, predominantly external (Type I) sacrococcygeal teratoma with mixed solid and cystic components at 28 weeks gestation. Brain development is normal.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal structural development. The fetal brain shows appropriate sulcation for 28 weeks gestation, including the presence of the central and cingulate sulci. The lateral ventricles are normal in size, measuring 5.9 mm at the atrium. The posterior fossa, cerebellum, and corpus callosum are normal in size and appearance.

Chest, abdomen, spine, and extremity anatomy are normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing normal intracranial anatomy and age-appropriate sulcation at 28 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI of a 6-year-old female reveals normal biventricular dimensions, myocardial mass, and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There is no evidence of atrial or ventricular septal defect, and great vessel alignment is fully anatomical.

No abnormal late gadolinium enhancement is identified. Myocardial T1 and T2 mapping parameters are within normal limits. Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI with no structural or functional abnormalities.

Cardiac MRI and MR angiography of the chest demonstrate a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) measuring 3.5 mm at its narrowest point. There is significant left-to-right shunting, yielding a Qp:Qs ratio of 1.7:1. The left atrium and left ventricle are mildly dilated, reflecting volume overload (LVEDVI 92 mL/m²). Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 62%. No significant pulmonary arterial hypertension is detected.

Impression: Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) with moderate left-to-right shunt and resulting mild left-sided cardiac volume overload.

Multiplanar, multisequence pediatric cardiac MRI shows normal cardiac architecture. Both the right and left ventricular outflow tracts are wide and patent without subvalvular, valvular, or supravalvular stenosis. No anomalous pulmonary venous connections are present. Myocardial tissue characteristics are normal on all sequences.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No congenital, functional, or myocardial tissue abnormalities are identified. Normal biventricular systolic function (LVEF 64%).

Cardiac MRI of a 10-year-old female demonstrates asymmetric septal hypertrophy, primarily involving the basal and mid-ventricular interventricular septum. The maximal septal wall thickness is measured at 18 mm (z-score > 6). The left ventricular cavity is small, and there is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet, resulting in mild mitral regurgitation and dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction with a peak gradient of 25 mmHg. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 75%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows focal mid-myocardial enhancement at the anterior and posterior RV insertion points, representing myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Phenotypic features of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with asymmetric septal hypertrophy, hyperdynamic systolic function, dynamic LVOT obstruction, and localized myocardial fibrosis.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal intracranial structures. Sulcation and cortical plate organization are completely appropriate for 27 weeks gestation. The ventricular system is normal, with symmetric lateral ventricular atria measuring 5.8 mm. Brainstem, cerebellum, and corpus callosum are fully intact and show normal signal characteristics.

The chest, abdomen, spine, kidneys, and extremities are structurally normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study with no structural or intracranial abnormalities.

MRI of the brain was completed for evaluation of atypical, non-focal syncope episodes. Brain parenchyma shows no signal abnormalities, mass lesions, or acute infarction on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). The corpus callosum and brainstem are structurally intact and unremarkable. Intracranial vascular flow voids at the base of the skull appear patent and symmetric.

Impression: Normal MR study of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or vascular abnormalities are identified.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a large, solid, contrast-enhancing mass centered within the fourth ventricle, measuring 3.8 x 3.5 x 3.2 cm. The lesion is causing severe compression of the brainstem and cerebellar hemispheres, resulting in upstream ventricular dilation involving the third and lateral ventricles, consistent with acute obstructive hydrocephalus. Faint restricted diffusion is noted on DWI, indicating high cellularity.

Impression: Posterior fossa mass centered in the fourth ventricle with obstructive hydrocephalus, most consistent with medulloblastoma in this age group. Urgent neurosurgical intervention is recommended.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac chambers and great vessels. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is normal for the patient's body surface area, and the global ejection fraction is 62%. The right ventricular size and function are also within normal parameters, with an ejection fraction of 58%. There is no evidence of valvular stenosis, regurgitation, or intracardiac shunting. Myocardial perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrate no abnormalities.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI with preserved biventricular function and no structural or myocardial tissue pathology.

Multiplanar brain MRI demonstrates a well-demarcated cystic lesion with a highly enhancing mural nodule located within the right cerebellar hemisphere. The lesion measures approximately 2.8 x 2.6 x 2.4 cm and exerts mass effect upon the fourth ventricle, causing mild upstream lateral ventricular dilatation. No significant surrounding vasogenic edema or restrictive diffusion is noted.

Impression: Enhancing cystic posterior fossa mass, highly characteristic of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. Close evaluation by pediatric neurosurgery is recommended given the regional mass effect.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The right hepatic lobe and gallbladder, along with loops of small bowel, are herniated into the right hemithorax. This has resulted in a leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the left lung. Fetal lung-to-head ratio and total lung volume are reduced, consistent with moderate pulmonary hypoplasia. The fetal brain is normal with symmetric ventricles measuring 6.0 mm.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with herniation of liver and bowel, leading to mediastinal shift and moderate fetal lung hypoplasia.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was completed for evaluation of persistent post-concussive syndrome following a sports injury. Multiplanar sequences demonstrate no intracranial hemorrhage, acute territorial ischemia, or extra-axial fluid collections. Diffuse axonal injury (DAI) is evaluated on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) and reveals no microhemorrhages at the gray-white junctions or corpus callosum. Ventricles and sulci are unremarkable.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No structural, vascular, or traumatic microhemorrhagic sequelae of head injury identified to account for ongoing post-concussive headaches.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed cystic lesion measuring 3.8 x 3.5 x 3.2 cm centered in the right cerebellar hemisphere, showing a prominent enhancing mural nodule along its posterior margin. Significant local mass effect is observed, causing partial compression of the fourth ventricle and mild deviation of the brainstem, with minimal surrounding vasogenic edema.

Impression: Cystic cerebellar mass with an enhancing mural nodule, highly suggestive of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. Close neurosurgical monitoring and operative planning are recommended.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates an unremarkable scan. The cerebral hemispheres show advanced third-trimester sulcation and myelination patterns consistent with 35 weeks. The lateral ventricles are narrow and symmetric, with the atrium measuring 5.5 mm. The spine is intact, and abdominal viscera, including the kidneys and bladder, appear completely normal.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation. No structural, cranial, spinal, or abdominal anomalies identified.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 20 weeks gestation shows completely normal structural anatomy. Given the early gestational age, the cerebral hemispheres show smooth cortical surfaces with early forming Sylvian fissures, which is entirely normal for 20 weeks. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, with the atria measuring 5.5 mm. The corpus callosum and brainstem are developing normally.

The chest, abdomen, spine, and extremities demonstrate no morphological abnormalities. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI study demonstrating normal structural development and age-appropriate early brain sulcation at 20 weeks gestation.

Cardiovascular MRI evaluates the status of a patient post-repair of Tetralogy of Fallot. The study demonstrates severe pulmonary valve regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 44%. The right ventricle is severely dilated (RVEDVI 165 ml/m²) with mild global RV systolic dysfunction (RVEF 42%). Cine imaging also shows mild residual right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) dyskinesis at the patch site, with patchy LGE in the RVOT patch and septal insertion regions.

Impression: Status post Tetralogy of Fallot repair showing severe pulmonary regurgitation with significant, progressive right ventricular dilation and mild RV systolic dysfunction. These findings warrant consideration for pulmonary valve replacement.

Cardiac MRI was requested due to atypical chest pain in an adolescent female athlete. The exam demonstrates normal left and right ventricular cavity dimensions, wall thicknesses, and overall biventricular global and regional systolic functions. The left ventricular ejection fraction is estimated at 60%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. There is no evidence of myocardial edema, perfusion abnormality, or focal late gadolinium enhancement (LGE).

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal chamber dimensions, excellent biventricular function, and no evidence of myocarditis, fibrosis, or congenital anomalies.

Cardiovascular MR imaging shows normal cardiac anatomy and spatial relationships. The left ventricular ejection fraction is normal at 63%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is normal at 58%. No chamber dilation, hypertrophy, or regional wall motion abnormalities are identified. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences demonstrate no myocardial scarring or replacement fibrosis. Pulmonary and systemic venous connections are normal.

Impression: normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural, functional, or tissue abnormalities.

Cardiac MRI was acquired to investigate a systolic murmur detected during a routine physical exam. Assessment of cardiac anatomy demonstrates completely normal chamber dimensions, wall thickness, and valvular morphology. Right and left ventricular stroke volumes are balanced, and there is no evidence of intra- or extracardiac shunts, anomalous pulmonary venous drainage, or focal myocardial abnormalities.

Impression: Completely normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No structural, functional, or myocardial abnormalities identified to explain the murmur, which is consistent with a benign physiological murmur.

Cardiac MRI in a 17-year-old male with a family history of sudden cardiac death. Multiplanar imaging demonstrates marked, asymmetric hypertrophy of the interventricular septum, with a maximum septal wall thickness of 22 mm. Systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve anterior leaflet is observed, producing a dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction. The left ventricle is hyperdynamic with an ejection fraction of 78%. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals patchy mid-myocardial hyperenhancement involving the hypertrophied septal segments, suggesting myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Asymmetric hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with dynamic LVOT obstruction secondary to systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. Fibrosis is present within the hypertrophied septum.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 23 weeks gestation shows severe oligohydramnios, limiting resolution of some structures. There is complete bilateral absence of the fetal kidneys and renal arteries, and the urinary bladder is not visualized. The fetal lungs are small and hypoplastic, consistent with the severe oligohydramnios. Intracranial sulcation and ventricular width (atrium 6.4 mm) are within normal limits for 23 weeks.

Severe overcrowding of fetal limbs is noted, but no primary skeletal anomalies are identified. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe oligohydramnios and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia, characteristic of Potter sequence.

Diagnostic MR imaging of the brain was conducted to rule out a central cause for cyclic vomiting syndrome. Multisequence, contrast-enhanced images reveal unremarkable cerebral, cerebellar, and brainstem structures. There is no tumor or mass localized within the fourth ventricle or area postrema. Ventricular architecture and CSF pathways are fully patent without evidence of restriction or pressure changes.

Impression: Structurally normal brain MRI. No central mass lesion, obstructive pathology, or intracranial abnormality found to explain the patient's recurrent episodes of cyclic vomiting.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates highly satisfactory fetal development. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit well-developed sulcation patterns, including secondary gyral patterns in the frontal and temporal lobes, highly appropriate for 34 weeks. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with symmetric atrial measurements of 6.4 mm on the left and 6.3 mm on the right. The corpus callosum is well-formed, and the brainstem and posterior fossa appear intact.

Impression: Normal fetal brain MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrating advanced, age-appropriate sulcation and normal ventricular calibers.
