Multiplanar MR imaging of the brain reveals a complex, solid and cystic suprasellar mass measuring 3.2 x 2.5 cm. The cyst wall demonstrates peripheral enhancement, and the solid components show dense enhancement with T1 hyperintensity suggestive of proteinaceous fluid. The lesion compresses the optic chiasm and extends superiorly into the floor of the third ventricle.

Impression: Suprasellar solid and cystic mass, characteristic of an adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma. Significant mass effect on the optic chiasm and third ventricle is observed.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates multi-segmental subepicardial and mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the basal to mid-lateral and inferior left ventricular walls. T2-weighted imaging and T2 mapping show corresponding elevated signal, indicating acute myocardial edema. Mild global left ventricular systolic dysfunction is present with an ejection fraction of 49%.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of acute myocarditis. There is associated mild left ventricular dysfunction and localized myocardial edema.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation reveals entirely normal anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows expected opercularization of the sylvian fissures, and the parieto-occipital sulcus is well developed. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with both the left and right atria measuring 5.9 mm. Midline structures and the posterior fossa are intact.

No anomalies are visualized in the thoracic or abdominal organs. Impression: Symmetrical, age-appropriate fetal brain development with no structural defects.

Cardiac MR imaging is performed on a 3-month-old male who is status-post arterial switch operation for d-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA). The neo-aorta arises from the left ventricle and the neo-pulmonary artery arises from the right ventricle. There is mild, bilateral narrowing at the surgical anastomosis sites of the pulmonary artery branches, worse on the left side where the diameter is 3.5 mm. Left and right ventricular systolic functions are normal with EFs of 64% and 55% respectively.

Impression: Status post arterial switch operation for d-TGA. Mild bilateral branch pulmonary artery stenosis, with stable biventricular size and function.

Fetal MRI performed at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal early fetal development. Cortical sulcation is normal and smooth, corresponding correctly to 20 weeks gestation. The ventricular atria are symmetric, measuring 5.2 mm. Posterior fossa structure, corpus callosum, and abdominal organs are within normal limits.

Impression: Normal early-gestation fetal MRI study. No evidence of structural brain, spinal, or systemic abnormalities.

The study demonstrates normal positioning of the heart within the mediastinum. Both left and right ventricles are normal in size without hypertrophy, showing ejection fractions of 65% and 61% respectively. No abnormal late enhancement of the myocardium is detected, and there is no evidence of intracardiac shunts or structural abnormalities.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. Normal ventricular volumes and normal global and regional contractility without evidence of myocardial fibrosis.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates unilateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium is significantly dilated, measuring 13.5 mm, whereas the right ventricular atrium is normal at 7.2 mm. No intraventricular masses, hemorrhage, or periventricular nodularity is detected. The sulcation and gyral patterns are appropriate for 31 weeks, showing expected progression of frontal and temporal operculization.

The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal. Impression: Isolated left-sided moderate fetal ventriculomegaly. Suggest follow-up fetal ultrasound or MRI in 3-4 weeks to assess progression.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates complete, bilateral absence of the kidneys. No renal tissue is identified within either renal fossa or ectopic pelvic locations. There is severe anhydramnios (complete absence of amniotic fluid), leading to significant compression of the fetal body. The urinary bladder is not visualized, indicating a lack of fetal urine production. Fetal chest volume is severely reduced.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios and severe pulmonary hypoplasia (Potter sequence). This is a lethal fetal condition.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates localized subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) along the lateral and inferior walls of the left ventricle. Associated focal T2 prolongation in these same regions is consistent with myocardial edema, representing acute-on-chronic myocardial inflammation. Left ventricular systolic function is mildly impaired with an ejection fraction of 49%. No pericardial effusion is seen.

Impression: Findings consistent with acute myocarditis with mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction. No signs of pericardial involvement.

MRI of the brain reveals a large, solid, hypercellular mass in the midline posterior fossa, measuring approximately 4.1 x 3.8 x 3.5 cm. The lesion is primarily centered in the fourth ventricle, which is entirely effaced, resulting in severe supratentorial obstructive hydrocephalus. The lesion demonstrates restricted diffusion and heterogeneous contrast enhancement.

Impression: Large posterior fossa mass arising from the cerebellar vermis, highly characteristic of medulloblastoma. Staging spine MRI is recommended to rule out drop metastasis.

MR imaging of the brain is performed using a standard neuroimaging protocol. Brain parenchyma shows normal signal characteristics with intact gray-white matter differentiation. No intracranial mass, abnormal extra-axial fluid collections, or acute ischemic processes are visualized. Cranial nerves demonstrate normal trajectories, and the orbits are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No structural abnormality, chronic microvascular changes, or sinus pathology is identified to account for chronic headache symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. There is herniation of the stomach, multiple loops of small bowel, and a portion of the left hepatic lobe into the left hemithorax. This causes a significant mediastinal shift to the right and marked compression of both lungs; the total fetal lung volume is severely reduced. Intracranial structures are normal with a ventricular atrial width of 5.5 mm and normal sulcation for 25 weeks.

No spinal or skeletal anomalies are seen. Impression: Large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic herniation of stomach, bowel, and liver, causing severe mass effect and lung hypoplasia.

Cardiovascular MR imaging of the heart demonstrates normal biventricular volumes and mass indexed to body surface area. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 65% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%. There is no evidence of myocardial edema on T2-weighted sequences, and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging is completely negative for myocardial fibrosis. Normal coronary artery origins are visualized.

Impression: normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No congenital abnormalities, cardiomyopathy, or evidence of myocarditis detected.

Brain MRI performed following an episode of unexplained syncope. All sequences show normal cerebral anatomy. Gray-white matter differentiation is preserved. Ventricles, sulci, and basal ganglia are normal for age. No abnormal mass enhancement or signal abnormalities.

Impression: Unremarkable and normal brain MRI. There are no signs of intracranial pathology, mass lesions, or stroke to account for the syncopal symptoms.

Cardiac MRI of a 5-year-old male scheduled for follow-up evaluation after a previous episode of viral myocarditis six months ago. Multisequence MR imaging shows normal bi-ventricular volumes and contractility, with a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 63%. Native T1 and T2 mapping times have fully normalized. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows complete resolution of the previously described epicardial and midwall hyperenhancement, indicating healing of the inflamed myocardium without permanent scar formation.

Impression: Completely normal follow-up cardiac MRI demonstrating resolved myocarditis. No residual edema, fibrosis, or ventricular dysfunction is present.

Dedicated pediatric epilepsy protocol MR reveals localized thickening of the cortex in the posterior aspect of the right frontal lobe. Blurring of the gray-white matter junction is noted, with a subtle wedge-shaped FLAIR hyperintensity extending from the cortex down to the subependymal surface of the lateral ventricle, representing a transmantle sign. Hippocampi appear symmetric and normal in volume.

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia in the posterior right frontal lobe with a classic transmantle sign. This corresponds to the clinical focal seizure focus.

Evaluation for persistent cardiac murmur. The cardiac MRI shows completely normal cardiac anatomy. The atria, ventricles, and great vessels are normal in size and relation. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 62% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There is no evidence of atrial or ventricular septal defects.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal anatomy and biventricular function with no congenital heart defects detected.

Brain MRI demonstrates normal parenchymal volume and signal intensity. There is no evidence of intracranial hematoma, extra-axial fluid collections, or acute parenchymal injury. No microhemorrhages are detected on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). The ventricles and basilar cisterns are symmetric and of normal volume, and the major arterial flow voids are present and intact.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural correlates for post-concussive syndrome or traumatic axonal injury identified.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates normal cardiac chamber dimensions and wall thickness. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 74 mL/m2, and the right ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 76 mL/m2, both well within normal pediatric limits. Left and right ventricular systolic function is excellent, with calculated ejection fractions of 64% and 62% respectively. There is no evidence of focal myocardial thinning, regional wall motion abnormalities, or pathological late gadolinium enhancement (LGE).

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal biventricular size and systolic function. No structural congenital heart disease or myocardial fibrosis identified.

Cardiovascular MR imaging demonstrates normal pediatric cardiac structure. Normal origin and course of the coronary arteries. The aortic arch is left-sided without coarctation. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is appropriate for body surface area, with an ejection fraction of 64%. Right ventricular volume and function are normal (RVEF 62%). No abnormal myocardial enhancement or edema is identified.

Impression: Completely normal pediatric cardiovascular MRI. No evidence of congenital cardiac anomalies, myocardial dysfunction, or scar.

Brain MR evaluation shows normal cortical thickness, normal ventricular morphology, and absence of intra- or extra-axial mass lesions. The deep white matter is free of demyelinating or gliotic changes. No vascular abnormalities, aneurysms, or flow restrictions are visualized. Visualized paranasal sinuses are clear.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No organic etiology identified for the patient's complaints of episodic migraines with aura.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate for possible myocarditis following a history of atypical chest pain. There is no evidence of regional or global ventricular dysfunction, and ventricular volumes are within normal limits (LVEF 62%, RVEF 58%). T2-weighted and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences demonstrate no myocardial edema or pathologically enhanced scars.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI. No objective findings of myocarditis, myocardial scar, or structural heart disease.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate clinical suspicion of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC). The right ventricle is markedly dilated (indexed RVEDV 128 mL/m2) with focal areas of dyskinesia and microaneurysms along the RV free wall and apex. Delayed enhancement imaging demonstrates extensive hyperenhancement (fibrofatty replacement) involving the RV free wall and RV outflow tract.

Impression: Morphological and tissue characterization features are highly indicative of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) based on Task Force Criteria. The right ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 31%.

Cardiac MRI under sedation shows normal cardiac chamber sizes and symmetrical wall thicknesses for a 7-month-old infant. Left ventricular ejection fraction is estimated at 64% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. The systemic and pulmonary venous connections are normal. No intracardiac shunts are noted, and the aortic arch is left-sided and patent with no evidence of coarctation.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No congenital structural heart disease or ventricular dysfunction identified.

Brain MRI reveals asymmetric cortical atrophy in the left cerebral hemisphere, associated with prominent, thickened leptomeningeal enhancement over the left parieto-occipital region. The left lateral ventricle is compensatory enlarged. The left choroid plexus is also significantly enlarged and hyperenhancing.

Impression: Imaging findings are typical for Sturge-Weber syndrome (encephalotrigeminal angiomatosis) with unilateral leptomeningeal angioma, cortical atrophy, and ipsilateral choroid plexus hypertrophy.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal development. The fetal brain shows appropriate sulcation patterns for 28 weeks, with expected definition of the central and cingulate sulci. The lateral ventricles are symmetrical and measure 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal.

Fetal lungs are normal in volume for gestational age, and the abdominal organs are unremarkable. The fetal spine is intact. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation showing normal intracranial anatomy and normal general development.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal intracranial architecture. The ventricles are symmetric, with the lateral ventricular atrial width measuring 7.1 mm. Opercularization of the Sylvian fissure is proceeding normally, and cortical sulcation is appropriate for 28 weeks. The corpus callosum is fully formed, and the cerebellum and brainstem appear intact.

Fetal viscera, including the lungs, heart, stomach, kidneys, and bladder, show normal positioning and morphology. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI with age-appropriate structural development and normal posterior fossa.

Brain MRI demonstrates focal, fusiform thickening of the left optic nerve and optic chiasm, showing prominent T2-hyperintensity and moderate post-contrast enhancement. Additionally, multiple focal areas of signal intensity (FASI) are identified in the bilateral globus pallidus and cerebellar white matter.

Impression: Left optic pathway glioma and characteristic FASI, highly consistent with Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1).

Cardiovascular MRI of this 9-month-old infant demonstrates a double outlet right ventricle (DORV). Both the aorta and the pulmonary trunk arise almost entirely from the morphologic right ventricle. There is a large, non-restrictive subpulmonary ventricular septal defect (consistent with a Taussig-Bing anomaly). The pulmonary valve is anterior and slightly leftward relative to the aorta, with mild infundibular stenosis noted. The left ventricular cavity is well-developed but functions primarily to pump blood across the VSD.

Impression: Double outlet right ventricle with subpulmonary VSD (Taussig-Bing anomaly) and mild pulmonary outflow tract stenosis. Surgical planning visualization is provided.

MR imaging of the brain reveals moderate-to-severe symmetric enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles, with relative sparing of the fourth ventricle. Prominent transependymal flow of CSF is visualized as periventricular T2/FLAIR hyperintensity, indicating acute ventriculomegaly. A ventricular shunt catheter is visualized in the right lateral ventricle, with its tip appropriately positioned, but there is interval enlargement of the ventricles compared to prior studies.

Impression: Moderate-to-severe hydrocephalus with signs of active transependymal cerebrospinal fluid migration. Findings are concerning for ventriculoperitoneal shunt malfunction/obstruction.

Congenital cardiac MRI evaluates a patient with hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) post-Stage II bidirectional Glenn shunt. The superior vena cava is successfully anastomosed to the right pulmonary artery, with normal, patent flow demonstrated on phase-contrast sequences. There is severe hypoplasia of the left ventricle and mitral/aortic valves. The systemic right ventricle is moderately dilated with mild systolic dysfunction (RVEF 43%) and mild tricuspid regurgitation.

Impression: Status post bidirectional Glenn shunt for HLHS. Stable systemic right ventricle anatomy with mild systolic dysfunction, and normal bilateral pulmonary artery flows.

Brain MRI and MRA demonstrate severe, bilateral narrowing of the distal internal carotid arteries (ICA) at the terminus, along with occlusion of the proximal segments of the middle and anterior cerebral arteries. Extensive fine collateral networks at the skull base are visualized, creating a 'puff of smoke' appearance on MRA. Multiple small, chronic watershed infarcts are noted.

Impression: Bilateral distal ICA steno-occlusive disease with extensive lenticulostriate collateralization, consistent with Moyamoya disease. Multiple small chronic ischemic changes.

MR of the brain shows multiple non-enhancing focal areas of signal intensity (FASIs or UBOs) that are hyperintense on T2/FLAIR sequences, localized to the bilateral globus pallidus and brainstem. There is no evidence of associated mass effect. The optic nerves and chiasm are unremarkable.

Impression: Brain abnormalities consistent with known Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1), showing typical T2 hyperintensities (FASIs). No optic pathway glioma is identified on current sequences.

MR of the brain shows a well-defined area of restricted diffusion with matching T2/FLAIR hyperintensity involving the right MCA territory, specifically the frontoparietal cortex and caudate nucleus. Associated local mass effect is characterized by effacement of the adjacent cortical sulci, without midline shift or herniation. Magnetic resonance angiography shows a cutoff of flow in the M2 segment of the right middle cerebral artery.

Impression: Acute ischemic infarction of the right middle cerebral artery territory with associated mild mass effect. Acute M2 branch occlusion identified on MRA.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate suspected aortic coarctation. There is a discrete shelf-like narrowing in the proximal descending thoracic aorta, located immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The minimum lumen diameter at the coarctation site measures 5.2 mm, with a post-stenotic dilation of the descending aorta measuring 14.5 mm. Collateral vessels arising from the internal mammary and intercostal arteries are prominent.

Impression: Significant discrete coarctation of the thoracic aorta with post-stenotic dilation and collateralization. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 63% with mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy.

Multiplanar MRI of the brain reveals no structural or focal parenchymal abnormalities. The cerebral hemispheres, brainstem, and cerebellum show appropriate signal intensity. There is no restricted diffusion, acute hemorrhage, or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci are normal, and the optic nerves and orbits are unremarkable.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No evidence of mass lesion, ischemia, or demyelinating process to explain the atypical migraine symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates a left multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The left kidney is enlarged and contains multiple thin-walled, non-communicating cysts of varying sizes up to 2.2 cm, with no visible normal renal parenchyma remaining. The right kidney is normal in size and appearance with good corticomedullary differentiation. Amniotic fluid volume is completely normal, and the fetal urinary bladder is well-visualized.

Impression: Left-sided multicystic dysplastic kidney. The contralateral kidney is completely normal and functioning, as evidenced by normal amniotic fluid levels and bladder filling.

High-resolution epilepsy protocol MRI demonstrates focal cortical thickening and blurring of the gray-white matter junction along the posterior bank of the left central sulcus. Increased signal intensity on T2/FLAIR sequences is observed extending from the subcortical white matter down toward the ventricle wall, creating a faint 'transmedullary stripe' sign. The adjacent hippocampus is normal.

Impression: Cortical thickening and signal abnormalities in the left parietal lobe, characteristic of a focal cortical dysplasia (FCD Type II). This corresponds to the patient's clinical seizure focus.

Brain MRI of the neonate reveals diffuse, symmetrical T1 hyperintensity and T2 hypointensity within the bilateral thalami, posterior limbs of the internal capsules, and basal ganglia. Diffusion-weighted imaging demonstrates restricted diffusion within these central structures and the peri-rolandic cortex, indicating acute cytotoxic edema.

Impression: Brain MRI findings consistent with acute profound hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) involving the deep gray nuclei and peri-rolandic cortex.

Multiplanar multisequence brain MRI was performed. No acute focal infarct, hemorrhage, or mass lesion is seen. Ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal limits for age. Brainstem and cerebellar structures are unremarkable. Minimal mucosal thickening is noted in the maxillary sinuses, but intracranial structures are entirely normal.

Impression: Unremarkable MR imaging of the brain. No structural etiology identified for migraine symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation shows normal, symmetrical brain development. Primary and secondary cortical sulcation, including the precentral and postcentral sulci, are well delineated and typical for 33 weeks. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atria measuring 6.1 mm. The corpus callosum and cerebellar hemispheres appear completely intact.

Thoracic and abdominal anatomy are normal with no mass effects. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI demonstrating expected cerebral and structural progression for age.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit appropriate sulcation and operculization for 31 weeks, showing clear development of the central sulcus and lateral fissures. The ventricular system is normal in size, with symmetric lateral ventricular atria measuring 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum is fully formed, and the brainstem and posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellar vermis, are morphologically normal.

Visualized fetal chest, abdomen, and spine are intact, with no evidence of diaphragmatic hernia or spinal dysraphism. No extra-axial fluid collections are identified. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI demonstrating normal fetal structural development appropriate for a 31-week gestation.

A complex cystic-solid suprasellar mass is identified measuring 2.8 x 2.4 cm, containing prominent peripheral calcifications and hyperintense cystic fluid on T1-weighted images. The lesion compresses the optic chiasm and displaces the floor of the third ventricle superiorly, resulting in mild hydrocephalus.

Impression: Suprasellar adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma with significant mass effect on the optic pathways and pituitary stalk. Early upstream obstructive hydrocephalus is present.

Brain MRI and MRA were performed to screen for cerebral aneurysms due to a significant family history. The parenchyma is normal with no focal lesions, mass effect, or structural abnormalities. The high-resolution TOF MRA of the circle of Willis shows normal vascular anatomy with symmetric flow and no evidence of aneurysm or arteriovenous malformation.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI and MRA of the brain. No intracranial vascular malformations or aneurysms are visualized.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomical development. The cerebral hemispheres show early, appropriate sulcation, and the lateral ventricles are small and symmetric, measuring 5.5 mm. The brainstem, cerebellum, and corpus callosum are fully visualized and appear structurally intact. The chest and abdomen demonstrate normal lung signal, normal renal anatomy, and appropriate amniotic fluid volume.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 23 weeks gestation. No structural, CNS, or visceral anomalies identified.

Cardiac MR imaging demonstrates a focal discrete narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, situated immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The minimum luminal diameter at the coarctation site measures 6.2 mm, with a post-stenotic dilation of the descending aorta to 18.5 mm. Left ventricular mass index is elevated at 95 g/m2, representing mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 58%.

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the thoracic aorta with associated mild left ventricular hypertrophy. Collateral vascular channels are visualized along the internal mammary and intercostal arteries.

Anatomical and functional evaluation of the heart shows normal cardiac chambers and spatial relationships. The left and right ventricular volumes, wall thickness, and mass are well within the normal pediatric reference ranges. There is no evidence of intra-cardiac shunts, valvular dysfunction, or myocardial scarring on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI. Excellent biventricular systolic function with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 64% and right ventricular ejection fraction of 61%.

3D cardiac MR angiography evaluated for coronary sequelae of Kawasaki disease. There is a prominent saccular aneurysm involving the proximal left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery measuring 6.2 mm in diameter. A separate, fusiform dilation of the proximal right coronary artery (RCA) is also noted, measuring 4.1 mm. Myocardial perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement images are normal, with no evidence of inducible ischemia or prior myocardial infarction. Ventricular function is normal (LVEF 62%).

Impression: Coronary artery aneurysms involving the proximal LAD and proximal RCA, consistent with history of Kawasaki disease. No associated myocardial ischemia or fibrosis.

MR imaging of the brain reveals a large, extra-axial, fluid-filled space within the left middle cranial fossa, measuring approximately 4.5 x 3.2 x 3.0 cm. The fluid signal completely suppresses on FLAIR and tracks with CSF on all sequences. There is mild remodeling of the adjacent temporal bone and minor displacement of the adjacent left temporal lobe parenchyma without internal signal change.

Impression: Large left middle cranial fossa arachnoid cyst (Galassi Type II). There is mild mass effect but no midline shift, acute hemorrhage, or signs of parenchymal edema.

Brain MRI demonstrates a solid, homogeneously enhancing mass centered within the pineal gland, measuring 2.5 x 2.2 cm. The tumor causes compression of the tectal plate and narrowing of the cerebral aqueduct, resulting in moderate lateral and third ventricular dilation. Susceptibility-weighted sequences show no evidence of intratumoral hemorrhage or calcification.

Impression: Pineal region mass with compression of the tectal plate and associated obstructive hydrocephalus, highly suspicious for a pineal germinoma.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates progressive, moderate bilateral ventriculomegaly. The lateral ventricles are symmetrically dilated, with the left atrium measuring 13.5 mm and the right atrium measuring 13.1 mm. The third ventricle is mildly prominent but within normal limits. The corpus callosum is intact, and no periventricular nodular heterotopia or white matter signal abnormalities are seen.

The cerebral sulcation pattern is appropriate for 30 weeks gestation. The cerebellum and spine are unremarkable. Impression: Symmetrical, moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly without associated CNS anomalies. Recommend postnatal follow-up.

Cardiovascular MRI demonstrates a moderate circumferential pericardial effusion, measuring up to 14 mm in width along the posterior and lateral margins of the left ventricle and 10 mm anteriorly. There is no evidence of diastolic collapse of the right atrium or right ventricle to suggest cardiac tamponade. The cardiac chambers are normal in size, and biventricular global and regional systolic functions are preserved (LVEF 65%, RVEF 60%). No abnormal myocardial enhancement is identified.

Impression: Moderate circumferential pericardial effusion without MR findings of hemodynamically significant cardiac tamponade. The underlying myocardium appears normal.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic parallel alignment of the lateral ventricles (colpocephaly) with teardrop configuration, where the posterior horns are dilated relative to the anterior horns; the left atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right measures 11.5 mm. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and dilated. Sulcation is otherwise normal for gestational age.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly. Fetal neurology consultation is recommended.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked, asymmetric hypertrophy of the left ventricle, predominantly involving the basal anterior and anteroseptal walls, with a maximal wall thickness of 21 mm. There is systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve, resulting in brief contact with the interventricular septum and a moderate, eccentrically directed mitral regurgitation jet. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals patchy mid-myocardial enhancement within the hypertrophied septal segments, indicative of myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Findings are consistent with classic hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) involving severe septal hypertrophy and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. Left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 74%.

MRI demonstrates severe dilation of the left ventricle with a left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV) of 210 ml and severe global systolic dysfunction, represented by a left ventricular ejection fraction of 28%. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with an ejection fraction of 42%. There is diffuse, patchy mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement within the septum.

No primary valvular stenosis or regurgitation is seen, although moderate functional mitral regurgitation is noted secondary to annular dilation. Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular dilation and systolic impairment, accompanied by diffuse mid-wall myocardial fibrosis.

MRI of the brain was performed to investigate localized persistent headaches. Imaging reveals normal brain architecture with no focal parenchymal lesions, hemorrhage, or mass effect. Ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are entirely within normal limits. The optic nerves, optic chiasm, and pituitary gland are unremarkable. The major intracranial dural venous sinuses are patent.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural or vascular pathology identified to explain the headache symptoms.

Brain MRI performed with and without contrast shows diffuse, thick, leptomeningeal enhancement lining the cerebral hemispheres, basal cisterns, and within the sulci of the cerebellar hemispheres. There is mild, bilateral ventricular enlargement. No parenchymal mass lesion, focal collection, or ischemic stroke is seen.

Impression: Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement in a clinical context of high fever and neck stiffness, highly indicative of acute infectious meningitis. Correlate with cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis.

Cardiac MRI shows severe dilation and regional dysfunction of the right ventricle. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume index is severely elevated at 135 mL/m2. Prominent dyskinesia and microaneurysmal outpouchings are noted in the right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) and inferior wall. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows transmural enhancement of the right ventricular free wall, consistent with fibrofatty replacement.

Impression: Phenotypic features strongly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC). Left ventricular function and volumes are within normal limits (LVEF 58%).

Brain MRI reveals a well-defined, cystic cerebellar lesion measuring 3.1 x 2.8 x 2.9 cm in the right cerebellar hemisphere, with an intensely enhancing mural nodule. Moderate surrounding vasogenic edema is present within the hemisphere, compressing the fourth ventricle. There is no evidence of tonsillar herniation or supratentorial ventricular dilation.

Impression: Cystic cerebellar lesion with an enhancing mural nodule, highly characteristic of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. Neurosurgical evaluation is recommended.

MR imaging of the brain was performed for the evaluation of atypical migraines. The study demonstrates normal cortical architecture and myelination. No demyelinating lesions, vascular malformations, or mass lesions are present. The sinuses and mastoid cells are clear.

Impression: Unremarkable pediatric brain MRI. No structural abnormalities or pathologic enhancement to account for migraine symptoms.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal intra-axial and extra-axial structures. No evidence of space-occupying lesions, subacute infarction, or parenchymal hemorrhage is detected. Ventricular anatomy is normal, and venous sinuses demonstrate normal flow dynamics.

Impression: Negative and normal brain MRI. No intracranial mass or abnormality to explain chronic headache pattern in this patient.

Brain MRI shows multiple subependymal nodules lining the lateral ventricles, some of which demonstrate calcification. Additionally, multiple cortical and subcortical FLAIR hyperintense tubers are visualized, particularly within the bilateral parietal and frontal lobes. No evidence of a subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) is identified near the foramen of Monro.

Impression: Classic intracranial findings of Tuberous Sclerosis, including subependymal nodules and cortical tubers. No obstructive hydrocephalus or SEGA transformation is seen on the current exam.

Brain MRI demonstrates marked hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with a rotated remnant vermis, accompanied by severe cystic dilation of the posterior fossa that communicates directly with the fourth ventricle. The tentorium cerebelli and transverse sinuses are elevated. Moderate enlargement of the third and lateral ventricles is present.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by cerebellar vermis hypoplasia, large posterior fossa cyst, and associated ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI shows a mildly dilated left ventricle with a depressed global ejection fraction of 46%. T2-weighted triple IR imaging demonstrates patchy, diffuse high signal intensity in the lateral and subepicardial regions of the left ventricle, indicating myocardial edema. Early gadolinium enhancement images show hyperemia. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging reveals significant patchy, non-ischemic subepicardial and mid-wall enhancement in the basal-to-mid lateral wall, fulfilling Lake Louise criteria.

Impression: Acute myocarditis involving the lateral wall of the left ventricle with associated mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction. Recommend activity restriction and close clinical follow-up.

Fetal MRI performed at 31 weeks gestation for evaluation of skeletal dysplasia. There is severe, generalized shortening of all long bones, particularly the femora and humeri, which are bowed. The thoracic cavity is extremely narrow and bell-shaped, with short ribs, indicating severe pulmonary hypoplasia. The fetal calvarium is poorly mineralized, showing abnormal compressibility. Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable, with appropriate sulcation for 31 weeks.

Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia characterized by micromelia, bell-shaped thorax, and demineralized calvarium. Findings are highly suspicious for osteogenesis imperfecta type II or thanatophoric dysplasia.

Cardiac MRI evaluates status post arterial switch operation for d-transposition of the great arteries. The reconstructed neo-aorta arises from the left ventricle and is normal in caliber. The neo-pulmonary artery arises from the right ventricle; however, there is mild to moderate narrowing at the site of the surgical anastomosis, with the main pulmonary artery measuring 9 mm in diameter. Velocity-encoded imaging across the pulmonary anastomosis demonstrates a peak velocity of 2.4 m/s (estimated gradient of 23 mmHg). Biventricular size and function are normal (LVEF 60%, RVEF 55%).

Impression: Status post arterial switch operation for d-TGA. Mild to moderate stenosis at the neo-pulmonary artery anastomosis with preserved biventricular volumes and function.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates normal intra-axial and extra-axial structures. No mass lesion, abnormal enhancement, acute ischemia, or hemorrhage is observed. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and major vascular flow voids are unremarkable. The craniofacial structures are developmental normal.

Impression: Normal MR of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular pathology is demonstrated.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates completely unremarkable anatomy. The developing cerebral cortex is smooth, which is normal for this early gestational age. The ventricular system is small and symmetric, with the atrial widths measuring 5.2 mm. Visualized abdominal organs, including both kidneys, stomach, and urinary bladder, are normal in appearance and position. The spine is intact and without defects.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 20 weeks gestation with no intracranial, spinal, thoracic, or abdominal abnormalities identified.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a distinct focal narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta, immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. There is significant post-stenotic dilation of the descending aorta. Multiplanar reconstruction and flow-quantification sequences reveal a peak systolic pressure gradient of 38 mmHg across the obstruction, with prominent collateral vascular channels arising from the internal mammary and intercostal arteries.

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the thoracic aorta. Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved at 58% with mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, likely secondary to chronic pressure overload.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal structural development. The ventricular system is normal, with an atrial width of 5.5 mm. The brain stem, cerebellum, and corpus callosum are normal in morphology. Sulcation is appropriate for 25 weeks.

Fetal thoracic and abdominal viscera show normal signal and anatomy. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows partial agenesis/hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis. The keyhole-like CSF space in the posterior fossa is prominent, but the posterior fossa itself is not enlarged. The cerebellar hemispheres appear intact. Atrial measurements are 7.5 mm bilaterally, which is within normal limits.

No other cranial or extracranial abnormalities are seen. Impression: Inferior cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, representing a Dandy-Walker variant or vermian dysgenesis.

Brain MRI shows the cerebellar tonsils herniating approximately 7.5 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The third and fourth ventricles are normal in size and position. No evidence of ventriculomegaly or acute intracranial hemorrhage is identified. High-resolution cervical spine images obtained as a scout sequence demonstrate a small, fluid-filled syrinx extending from the C2 to C4 vertebral levels.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 7.5 mm tonsillar herniation and a small associated upper cervical syrinx. There is no evidence of hydrocephalus or intracranial mass effect.

MRI of the brain shows a large, well-circumscribed, extra-axial fluid collection in the left middle cranial fossa, measuring 4.2 x 3.0 x 2.8 cm. The fluid signal matches CSF on all sequences (T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI), showing no restricted diffusion. There is mild mass effect on the adjacent temporal lobe, but no midline shift or ventricular compression.

Impression: Left middle cranial fossa arachnoid cyst (Galassi Type II) with mild mass effect on the anterior temporal lobe. No acute complications or signs of hydrocephalus.

Brain MRI reveals a large, well-defined extra-axial fluid collection in the left middle cranial fossa measuring 4.5 x 3.2 x 3.6 cm, matching CSF signal on all sequences without internal enhancement or restricted diffusion. There is mild remodeling of the adjacent temporal bone and sphenoid wing, but no mass effect on the brainstem.

Impression: Large left temporal fossa arachnoid cyst (Galassi Type II), stable. There is no significant midline shift or acute mass effect.

Cardiac MRI shows severe dilation of the right ventricle with regional dyskinesia and micro-aneurysm formation within the right ventricular outflow tract and apex. Right ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 32%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates extensive hyperenhancement involving the right ventricular free wall.

Impression: Imaging features are diagnostic for Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) meeting multiple Task Force criteria. Left ventricular function remains preserved (EF 58%).

Brain MR imaging shows normal anatomical landmarks. Cerebral cortical volume, ventricles, and sulcal morphology are within normal limits. There are no intra- or extra-axial fluid collections, no acute ischemia, and no intracranial mass lesions. The pituitary gland and orbits are normal in appearance.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular anomalies identified to explain the episodes of syncope.

Brain MRI demonstrates normal cerebral parenchymal signals and volume. There are no acute ischemic changes, microhemorrhages, or extra-axial fluid collections. Cranial nerves, venous sinuses, and major arterial flow voids appear intact and unremarkable.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or vascular abnormality detected to account for recurrent episodes of syncope.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates mild bilateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right atrium measures 10.5 mm. The cerebral parenchyma is intact, and cortical sulcation is appropriate for 31 weeks gestation, with well-defined central and precentral sulci. The corpus callosum is present and normal in appearance. No intraventricular hemorrhage or structural anomalies are noted.

Impression: Mild bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. The brain structure, including cortical sulcation, is otherwise normal for gestational age.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation shows advanced cerebral maturation. The sulcation and gyration patterns are highly complex and appropriate for late third trimester. The lateral ventricles measure 7.1 mm at the atria. The thoracic and abdominal organs are structurally normal. The bowel demonstrates age-appropriate meconium signaling.

Impression: Structurally normal, term-equivalent fetal MRI. Normal fetal brain development and visceral anatomy.

Brain MRI in this 2-month-old infant shows symmetric, mild enlargement of the subarachnoid spaces over the frontal lobes and along the interhemispheric fissure. The ventricular system is normal in size and morphology. There is no evidence of subdural fluid collections or mass effect.

Impression: Findings are consistent with benign external hydrocephalus (benign macrocephaly of infancy), a self-limiting condition. No intracranial mass or pathological hydrocephalus is present.

MRI of the brain is performed using high-resolution 3D sequences. The cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres demonstrate normal signal intensity and morphology. No acute infarct, hemorrhage, or mass effect is identified. The ventricles, cisterns, and sulcal spaces are unremarkable for age, and major intracranial vascular flow voids are preserved.

Impression: Unremarkable pediatric brain MRI. No structural abnormality, mass, or restricted diffusion to account for the patient's headaches.

Cardiac MRI shows significant dilatation of the right ventricle with multiple focal aneurysms and dyskinesia along the RV free wall and RV outflow tract. The right ventricular ejection fraction is severely depressed at 34%. Multiplanar T1-weighted imaging demonstrates regional fatty infiltration within the RV myocardium, and post-contrast images reveal focal late gadolinium enhancement. The left ventricle is normal in size and function (LVEF 59%).

Impression: Structural and functional abnormalities highly indicative of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting major diagnostic task force criteria.

Pediatric cardiac MRI demonstrates normal chamber size, thickness, and ventricular function. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or focal myocardial scarring are detected on late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging. Valvular flow velocities and regurgitant fractions are well within physiological limits.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No evidence of cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, or congenital structural abnormalities.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac chamber sizes, wall thickness, and function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 61% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. No late gadolinium enhancement is present, and T1 mapping values are within the normal reference range, excluding diffuse fibrosis or active inflammation. Valvular structures are morphologically normal with no significant regurgitation or stenosis.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural heart disease, congenital abnormality, or cardiomyopathy.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a large septal defect. There is a secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring approximately 18 mm in maximum diameter with a significant left-to-right shunt (Qp:Qs ratio estimated at 2.1:1). Right ventricular dilation is present with an end-diastolic volume index of 110 mL/m2, representing right heart volume overload. Right ventricular systolic function is preserved (RVEF 59%).

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with a significant left-to-right shunt and consequent right ventricular volume overload.

Cardiac MRI of an 8-year-old female referred for evaluation of atypical chest pain during physical education. The multiplanar cine images demonstrate normal cardiac morphology. The ventricles exhibit normal end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes without evidence of wall motion abnormalities. Global left ventricular systolic function is excellent with an ejection fraction of 64% (RVEF is 60%). No myocardial edema is observed on T2 mapping sequences, and late gadolinium enhancement is completely absent, indicating no scar tissue.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI. No evidence of myocardial inflammation, ischemic scar, non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, or structural congenital heart defect.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation reveals a lumbosacral neural tube defect. There is a prominent osseous defect involving the posterior elements from L4 through S2, associated with an overlying fluid-filled sac containing neural elements, consistent with a myelomeningocele. Intracranial findings include a Chiari II malformation, characterized by a small posterior fossa, downward displacement of the cerebellar vermis and medulla through the foramen magnum (banana sign), and bifrontal narrowing of the cranium (lemon sign). The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with atrial measurements of 12.5 mm.

Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele (L4-S2) with associated Chiari II malformation and moderate ventriculomegaly. Recommend prenatal evaluation for potential in-utero repair.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates normal development of the fetal central nervous system and body. The cerebral gyration and sulcation patterns, including the developing precentral and postcentral sulci, are highly appropriate for gestational age. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with symmetric atrial widths of 5.8 mm. The brainstem, cerebellum, and posterior fossa are normal.

The thorax, heart, and abdominal viscera are normal in location and appearance. Normal amniotic fluid index is noted. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study at 30 weeks gestation with no structural or developmental anomalies.

Brain MRI of this infant shows focal areas of T1 hyperintensity and T2 hypointensity lining the left caudothalamic groove, indicative of a subacute germinal matrix hemorrhage. There is mild extension of hemorrhage into the left lateral ventricle, without ventricle dilatation or intraventricular clot formation. The cerebral parenchyma is otherwise normal.

Impression: Left subacute germinal matrix hemorrhage with trace intraventricular extension (Grade II). No hydrocephalus or parenchymal venous infarction is observed.

Cardiac MRI reveals regional right ventricular wall motion abnormalities, including dyskinesia of the RV free wall and bulging of the RV outflow tract. There is moderate right ventricular dilation (RVEDVI 115 mL/m2) with depressed right ventricular systolic function (RVEF 38%). Late gadolinium enhancement imaging shows focal areas of mid-myocardial fibrosis within the RV free wall.

Impression: Cardiac MRI findings are highly characteristic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC), meeting multiple task force diagnostic criteria.

Brain MR imaging demonstrates a lobulated suprasellar mass measuring 3.1 x 2.7 x 2.4 cm. The mass contains both cystic and solid enhancing components, causing substantial elevation and compression of the optic chiasm. The pituitary stalk is deviated laterally, and the normal pituitary gland is flattened within the sella.

Impression: Suprasellar mass with characteristics most consistent with a craniopharyngioma. Opthalmologic and endocrine evaluations are highly recommended.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates mild, isolated unilateral ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricular atrium measures 12.5 mm, whereas the left ventricular atrium measures 8.4 mm. No intraventricular hemorrhage, septal defects, or periventricular nodular heterotopia is identified. Cortical sulcation is highly advanced and symmetric, demonstrating extensive tertiary folding matching the 36-week gestational age.

Impression: Mild isolated unilateral ventriculomegaly (right side). Advanced, age-appropriate cortical development is noted with no associated cerebral parenchymal or spinal anomalies.

Brain MRI was obtained following a sports-related concussion to evaluate for traumatic injury. Multiplanar MR sequences demonstrate completely normal parenchymal signal intensity without evidence of extra-axial fluid collections, subacute subdural hematoma, or cortical contusion. Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) shows no evidence of diffuse axonal injury or microhemorrhage. The ventricles and basilar cisterns are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No imaging findings indicative of acute intracranial hemorrhage, contusion, or axonal shear injury.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 3-month-old infant with a significant heart murmur. There is a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 1.1 cm, with a significant left-to-right shunt. This has resulted in severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle. There is moderate right ventricular volume overload, though both ventricles maintain normal systolic function. Pulmonary venous return is normal.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with severe right-sided heart dilation and volume overload. No evidence of anomalous pulmonary venous connection.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 6-month-old infant with Tetralogy of Fallot. There is a large malalignment ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring 9.0 mm with overriding of the ascending aorta by approximately 45%. Marked concentric hypertrophy of the right ventricle is observed. There is severe subpulmonic infundibular and valvular stenosis, with the pulmonary valve annulus measuring 5.2 mm. Main and branch pulmonary arteries are hypoplastic. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 62%.

Impression: Classic anatomical findings of Tetralogy of Fallot with severe right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, hypoplastic pulmonary arteries, and marked right ventricular hypertrophy. Findings support surgical reconstruction planning.

Cardiac MRI reveals double outlet right ventricle (DORV) with a subaortic ventricular septal defect (VSD). Both the aorta and pulmonary artery arise entirely from the morphologic right ventricle. There is severe infundibular and valvular pulmonary stenosis resulting in marked right ventricular hypertrophy. The left ventricle is small but functionally intact, with blood exiting primarily through the VSD into the right ventricle.

Impression: Double outlet right ventricle with subaortic VSD and severe pulmonary stenosis (Fallot-type DORV). Marked right ventricular concentric hypertrophy is present.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows severe dilatation of the posterior fossa. There is complete agenesis of the lower cerebellar vermis and severe hypoplasia of the superior vermis, which is rotated superiorly. The fourth ventricle is continuous with a massively dilated cisterna magna, filling the posterior fossa and causing elevation of the tentorium and torcula. Mild bilateral ventriculomegaly is noted, with the atrial width measuring 10.5 mm.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation. Findings include cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, an enlarged posterior fossa cyst communicating with the fourth ventricle, and mild secondary ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 9-month-old infant with untreated cyanotic heart disease. There is a large, unrestrictive ventricular septal defect (VSD) with overriding of the aorta estimated at approximately 45%. Marked concentric hypertrophy of the right ventricular free wall is present. The right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) shows severe infundibular and valvular stenosis, with significantly reduced forward blood flow and post-stenotic dilation of the main pulmonary artery.

Impression: Classic anatomical features of Tetralogy of Fallot with severe right ventricular outflow tract obstruction and marked RV hypertrophy. Left ventricular function remains preserved with an ejection fraction of 61%.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 6-month-old female with complex congenital cyanotic heart disease. Both the aorta and pulmonary artery arise almost entirely from the right ventricle. There is a large subaortic ventricular septal defect (VSD). Additionally, there is severe infundibular and valvular pulmonary stenosis, with marked concentric hypertrophy of the right ventricular free wall. The left ventricle is relatively small but demonstrates normal systolic function (LV EF 63%).

Impression: Double outlet right ventricle (DORV) with a large subaortic VSD and severe subpulmonic stenosis (Fallot-type DORV). Marked right ventricular concentric hypertrophy.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe spherical dilation of the left ventricle with global hypokinesis. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is markedly increased to 128 mL/m2. Left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 28%. There is associated moderate-to-severe functional mitral regurgitation due to annulus dilation. No focal myocardial fibrosis or replacement scarring is seen on delayed enhancement imaging.

Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction and moderate functional mitral regurgitation. No evidence of myocardial scar.

Cardiac MRI of a 2-year-old female reveals that both the aorta and the pulmonary artery arise almost entirely from the right ventricle. There is a large subaortic ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring 10 mm, which is the primary outlet for the left ventricle. No pulmonary stenosis or subpulmonary stenosis is present, resulting in unrestricted pulmonary blood flow and moderate pulmonary trunk dilation (measuring 18 mm). Left and right ventricular chambers demonstrate moderate dilation, and biventricular systolic function is preserved with LVEF at 55% and RVEF at 52%.

Impression: Double outlet right ventricle (DORV) with a subaortic ventricular septal defect and no pulmonary stenosis. Findings demonstrate significant pulmonary overcirculation and bilateral ventricular enlargement.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a large lumbosacral neural tube defect with an open myelomeningocele sac extending from L3 through S2. This is associated with a Chiari II malformation, characterized by hindbrain herniation, cerebellar pegging (banana sign), and frontal bone flattening (lemon sign). The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, with the atrial width measuring 10.1 mm.

Sulcation is appropriate for 21 weeks, showing early Sylvian fissure formation. The upper extremities and remaining axial skeleton are unremarkable. Impression: Open lumbosacral myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation and mild ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI performed for evaluation of frequent premature ventricular contractions. All cardiac chambers demonstrate normal dimensions, volumes, and myocardial mass. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 56%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion anomalies. T1, T2 mapping, and late gadolinium enhancement sequences are completely normal, showing no myocardial fibrosis or edema.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No underlying structural heart disease, arrhythmogenic substrates, or focal fibrosis identified.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral renal agenesis. No renal tissue is identified within either renal fossa or within the pelvis. There is a complete absence of amniotic fluid (anhydramnios), which limits detailed resolution of the fetal extremities. The fetal urinary bladder is not visualized.

Fetal brain evaluation shows symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 6.0 mm with normal early cortical sulcation. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios, representing a lethal pulmonary hypoplasia risk sequence.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac structure, chamber sizes, and function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 74 mL/m² and the ejection fraction is 61%. Right ventricular end-diastolic volume is normal with an ejection fraction of 55%. No late gadolinium enhancement is present. The thoracic aorta and pulmonary trunk are normal in appearance.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. Normal biventricular size, function, and tissue characteristics without congenital or acquired pathology.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate frequent ventricular premature beats in a 16-year-old male athlete. Cine imaging demonstrates completely normal biventricular volumes and wall thicknesses. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 61%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or dyskinesias are identified.

Myocardial perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences demonstrate no focal areas of ischemia or myocardial scar. T1 and T2 mapping values are normal. Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study showing no structural heart disease, arrhythmogenic substrates, or myocardial scarring.

Cardiac MRI performed to evaluate a 6-year-old female with suspected atrial septal defect. Cine imaging reveals a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring approximately 18 mm in diameter, demonstrating rightward bulging of the interatrial septum and a left-to-right shunt. Phase-contrast flow analysis measures a pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp/Qs) of 1.9. There is marked dilation of both the right atrium and the right ventricle (RVEDVI 115 ml/m²), indicating substantial right-sided volume overload. Right ventricular ejection fraction is 54%.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt and consequent right heart chamber dilation. No evidence of pulmonary hypertension.

The patient's brain MRI is negative for mass lesions, midline shift, edema, or acute ischemia. All major cerebral arteries demonstrate intact vascular flow voids. Cortical sulcation and ventricular systems are appropriate for age.

Impression: Normal MR brain scan. No acute intracranial findings.

Brain MR evaluation demonstrates multiple subependymal nodules along the lateral ventricles, which are predominantly calcified and T2-hypointense. Additionally, several cortical tubers are identified as areas of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in the bilateral frontal and parietal lobes. A 1.2 cm enhancing subependymal nodule is seen near the left foramen of Monro, but there is no evidence of ventriculomegaly or obstruction.

Impression: Intracranial findings highly characteristic of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. The subependymal nodule near the left foramen of Monro should be monitored closely for potential progression to a subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA).

MRI brain was acquired under general anesthesia. Pediatric neuro-anatomy is fully preserved. The myelination pattern is mature and age-appropriate. There is no evidence of gray matter heterotopia, ventriculomegaly, or abnormal fluid collections. The brainstem, cerebellum, and pituitary gland demonstrate entirely normal size and morphology.

Impression: Structurally normal pediatric brain MRI. No anatomical, developmental, or metabolic-related white matter abnormalities identified.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation demonstrates moderate unilateral dilatation of the left lateral ventricle, measuring 12.5 mm at the atrium. The right lateral ventricle atrium is normal at 7.8 mm. There is thinning of the overlying posterior cerebral mantle on the left. Additionally, the sulcation pattern is delayed for 31 weeks, showing features more typical of a 28-week gestation, particularly in the frontal and temporal lobes.

Impression: Left unilateral ventriculomegaly associated with delayed cortical sulcation. Close neurodevelopmental monitoring and post-natal follow-up are recommended.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals moderate, symmetric bilateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 12.1 mm, and the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 11.8 mm. The third and fourth ventricles are normal in size, and there is no evidence of aqueductal stenosis or neural tube defects. The cortical sulcation pattern is appropriate for 31 weeks gestation, with well-demarcated parieto-occipital, cingulate, and central sulci.

Impression: Moderate, symmetric bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly at 31 weeks gestation with age-appropriate cortical sulcation. No associated anomalies identified.

Brain MR demonstrates a complex sellar and suprasellar mass measuring 3.1 x 2.7 x 2.5 cm. The mass contains prominent cystic areas with highly hyperintense T1 signal (suggestive of high protein/cholesterol content) and peripheral calcifications. The solid components of the mass show intense enhancement. The lesion compresses the optic chiasm and displaces the floor of the third ventricle upward, causing mild hydrocephalus.

Impression: Complex cystic and solid suprasellar mass, highly consistent with an adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma. Optic chiasm compression and mild ventriculomegaly are present.

Brain MRI shows marked hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with a significantly enlarged posterior fossa fluid space communicating directly with the fourth ventricle. The tentorium cerebelli and torcular herophili are abnormally elevated. Dilatation of the lateral and third ventricles is also noted, suggestive of associated non-communicating hydrocephalus.

Impression: Classic anatomical findings consistent with Dandy-Walker malformation. There is secondary ventricular expansion requiring close clinical monitoring and pediatric neurosurgery consultation.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation reveals bilateral, severe lateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 14.5 mm and the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 13.8 mm. There is thinning of the surrounding white matter parenchyma and the cerebral cortex, with mild delay in the progression of temporal and parietal sulcation patterns.

The third and fourth ventricles appear normal, and no aqueductal obstruction is definitively resolved. Impression: Severe bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly with associated delay in cortical maturation. Pediatric neurosurgery counseling is recommended.

Brain MR imaging was performed to rule out organic etiology for acute onset psychiatric symptoms. The cerebral cortex shows a normal gyral pattern with preserved volume. The ventricular system, basal ganglia, and thalamic structures are normal. No areas of restricted diffusion, demyelinating plaques, or pathological enhancement are visualized.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No structural, inflammatory, or demyelinating pathology is identified to account for the patient's psychiatric symptoms.

An infant brain MRI reveals a markedly enlarged posterior fossa with a cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle. There is severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis, with only a small residual superior tissue band. The torcula and transverse sinuses are abnormally elevated. Supratentorial ventricles show mild ventriculomegaly but no acute signs of progressive hydrocephalus.

Impression: Classic presentation of Dandy-Walker malformation. Clinical and neurosurgical correlation is advised to monitor ventricular caliber.

Cardiac MRI demonstrating a large secundum atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 1.8 cm. There is extensive right atrial and right ventricular dilation, indicating right-sided volume overload. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume index is elevated at 122 mL/m², with preserved RV ejection fraction at 57%. Flow quantification calculations reveal a significant left-to-right shunt with a Qp:Qs ratio of 1.95:1.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect causing moderate-to-severe right heart chamber dilatation. The shunt ratio supports closure intervention.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomy. Brain structures including the corpus callosum and cerebellum are intact and appropriate for 26 weeks. Ventricles are symmetric, with atrial measurements of 6.5 mm bilaterally. Fetal chest, abdominal viscera, and extremities show normal signal intensity and development. Amniotic fluid volume is normal.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate brain development and normal systemic anatomy at 26 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals a large right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The right lobe of the liver and multiple loops of small bowel are herniated into the right hemithorax, causing a severe leftward mediastinal shift. The left lung is compressed, and the calculated total fetal lung volume is severely reduced. The fetal brain is structurally intact; the ventricular atria measure 6.4 mm bilaterally, and the sulcation is appropriate for 26 weeks.

The remaining fetal organs are unremarkable, and amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits. Impression: Severe right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic liver herniation, leading to severe mediastinal shift and pulmonary hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI shows marked dilation of the left ventricle with an end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVI) of 135 ml/m2. Left ventricular systolic function is severely depressed, with an calculated ejection fraction of 28%. Diffuse, subtle mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) is identified along the septum. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with a borderline low ejection fraction of 42%. No intracardiac thrombus is visualized.

Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction, mild right ventricular dysfunction, and mid-wall fibrosis. No evidence of myocardial infarction or thrombi.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 22 weeks gestation reveals complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles exhibit a parallel orientation (colpocephaly) with dilation of the posterior horns; the left atrium measures 11.2 mm and the right atrium measures 11.5 mm. Third ventricle is high-riding and mildly dilated. Sulcation pattern is otherwise normal for gestational age.

No other intracranial or extracranial anomalies are identified. The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellum and brainstem, are within normal limits. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates a cranial vault defect. There is a small occipital midline skull defect with a herniating sac containing CSF and a minor amount of dysplastic cerebellar tissue, consistent with an occipital encephalocele. The ventricles are mildly dilated at 10.2 mm. Spine is completely intact.

No other major systemic anomalies are visualized. Impression: Occipital encephalocele with associated mild ventriculomegaly. Neurosurgical follow-up is recommended.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a moderate-sized perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 6.5 mm. Phase contrast flow analysis reveals a significant left-to-right shunt with a pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp/Qs) of 1.7. There is associated mild dilation of the left atrium and left ventricle, indicating volume overload, though left ventricular systolic function remains hyperdynamic.

Impression: Moderate perimembranous ventricular septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt. Normal left ventricular ejection fraction of 65% with early volume overload changes.

Fetal MRI performed at 32 weeks gestation demonstrates complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly with dilation of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles, giving them a tear-drop configuration; the atrial width of the lateral ventricles measures 11.2 mm on the right and 11.5 mm on the left. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and dilated. Gyration and sulcation correspond to the gestational age.

No other spinal or chest defects are visualized. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated colpocephaly and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly at 32 weeks gestation.

Brain MRI reveals a 1.2 cm hypointense lesion within the right lateral aspect of the pituitary gland, causing deviation of the infundibulum to the left. The optic chiasm is free from compression and there is no invasion into the bilateral cavernous sinuses.

Impression: Right-sided pituitary macroadenoma. No evidence of mass effect on the optic chiasm.

Evaluated for persistent post-concussive syndrome. The brain parenchyma is structurally intact without signal abnormalities. Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) shows no evidence of microhemorrhage or diffuse axonal injury. Ventricles and extra-axial spaces are within normal limits.

Impression: Normal pediatric brain MRI. No evidence of traumatic brain injury, acute hemorrhage, or structural pathology.

MR evaluation of the brain reveals normal brain parenchyma with no areas of signal abnormality, restricted diffusion, or abnormal enhancement. The extra-axial CSF spaces are within normal physiological limits. Orbits, paranasal sinuses, and mastoid air cells are unremarkable. The craniovertebral junction is intact.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No central nervous system etiology identified for the patient's symptoms.

MR of the brain shows bilateral tortuosity of the optic nerves with prominent cerebrospinal fluid sheaths and flattening of the posterior sclera. Slit-like lateral ventricles are noted, and there is partial empty sella. No mass lesions, vascular malformations, or dural venous sinus thromboses are identified on the accompanying MR venogram.

Impression: MRI findings consistent with idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri). Correlation with fundoscopy to assess for papilledema is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates severe bladder outlet obstruction. The fetal urinary bladder is extremely dilated, thick-walled, and exhibits a classic 'keyhole' sign, consistent with posterior urethral valves. There is marked bilateral hydroureteronephrosis and parenchymal thinning of both kidneys. Anhydramnios (complete absence of amniotic fluid) is present. Fetal brain demonstrates normal sulcation for 29 weeks and normal ventricular atrial width of 6.3 mm.

Impression: Posterior urethral valves with severe bilateral hydroureteronephrosis, megacystis, and anhydramnios.

High-resolution MRI of the brain demonstrates focal thickening of the cortex in the right frontal lobe, associated with blurring of the gray-white matter junction and a transmantle sign of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity extending toward the ventricle. The hippocampus, cerebellum, and remaining cerebral hemispheres appear normal.

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia in the right frontal lobe, highly consistent with the patient's history of medically refractory focal epilepsy. Neurology follow-up is indicated.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiovascular structures and function. Left and right ventricular chamber volumes are within the normal ranges for age and sex. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormality, myocardial edema, or hypertrophy.

No late gadolinium enhancement is visualized to suggest myocardial fibrosis, and the cardiac valves are fully competent. Pulmonary and systemic venous connections are normal. Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal biventricular function and no structural or congenital heart disease.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation shows unremarkable intracranial development. The brain parenchymal signal is normal, and early opercularization is underway. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and within normal limits, with the atrium measuring 6.1 mm on both sides. The posterior fossa structures and spinal cord are unremarkable.

Fetal thorax and abdomen are completely normal. Fetal biometry matches the gestational age. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study at 24 weeks gestation with no fetal anomalies identified.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation reveals a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The right lobe of the liver and several small bowel loops have herniated into the right hemithorax, displacing the heart and mediastinum significantly to the left. The left lung is compressed but visible. Fetal brain MRI shows normal ventricular size (atrial width 5.2 mm) and age-appropriate third-trimester cortical sulcal patterns.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver-up anatomy. Marked mediastinal shift and secondary lung compression are noted.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals features highly suggestive of a severe skeletal dysplasia, such as Thanatophoric dysplasia. There is marked, rhizomelic shortening of the long bones, with the femurs exhibiting a curved 'telephone receiver' appearance. The thoracic cage is extremely narrow and bell-shaped, with significant secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. Polyhydramnios is noted.

The brain shows relative macrocephaly with normal sulcation for 25 weeks, and normal ventricles measuring 7.2 mm. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia characterized by rhizomelic limb shortening, curved femurs, and a narrow thoracic cavity, most consistent with Thanatophoric dysplasia.

Multisequence brain MRI shows normal midline structures, a well-formed corpus callosum, and a normal pituitary gland. Cranial nerves V, VII, and VIII are normal in course and appearance. There is no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, or intracranial tumor. Skull base and craniocervical junction are intact.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI. No focal parenchymal lesions, demyelinating plaques, or mass lesions are present to account for transient right-sided focal sensory symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates a Dandy-Walker variant. There is mild-to-moderate hypoplasia of the lower cerebellar vermis with a keyhole-like communication between the fourth ventricle and a prominent retrocerebellar fluid space. The posterior fossa size is within the upper limits of normal, and the tentorium is not significantly elevated. The supratentorial brain shows normal ventricles (atrial width 7.8 mm) and appropriate sulcation.

Impression: Dandy-Walker variant (cerebellar vermian hypoplasia with prominent retrocerebellar space). No supratentorial abnormalities or ventriculomegaly visualized.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates mild hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis with a keyhole-shaped connection between the fourth ventricle and the cisterna magna. The posterior fossa is not significantly enlarged, and the tentorium is only minimally elevated. Supratentorial brain anatomy is normal, with symmetric ventricles measuring 7.0 mm.

Impression: Findings are consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant or isolated inferior vermian hypoplasia. Postnatal prognosis is generally more favorable than classic Dandy-Walker malformation.

MRI of the brain shows a large, predominantly cystic mass in the left cerebellar hemisphere measuring 4.2 x 3.8 x 4.0 cm. Associated with the cyst is an intensely enhancing mural nodule measuring 1.4 cm along the posterior-lateral margin. There is significant compression of the adjacent cerebellar parenchyma and mild displacement of the fourth ventricle to the right, though the ventricular system remains patent and without frank hydrocephalus.

Impression: Left cerebellar hemisphere cystic mass with an enhancing mural nodule, highly indicative of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma (JPA). Neurosurgical consultation is indicated for planned resection.

Cardiac MRI was performed for dynamic surveillance of repaired Tetralogy of Fallot. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume index (RVEDVI) is significantly elevated at 155 mL/m², indicating moderate right ventricular dilation. The right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is calculated at 45%, showing mild systolic dysfunction. Cine sequences demonstrate severe pulmonary regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 42%.
