Left ventricular size and systolic performance are preserved with an LVEF of 58% and no regional wall motion abnormalities.

Impression: Post-repair Tetralogy of Fallot presenting with moderate right ventricular dilation and severe pulmonary regurgitation, along with mild RV systolic dysfunction. No myocardial fibrosis is identified on late gadolinium enhancement imaging.

Cardiac MRI reveals Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve, characterized by severe downward displacement of the septal and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve (displacement index of 22 mm/m²). This results in a large "atrialized" portion of the right ventricle. The functional right ventricle is small with reduced contractility (RVEF 38%). There is severe tricuspid regurgitation with a regurgitant fraction of 55%. Left ventricular size and function are preserved.

Impression: Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve with severe tricuspid regurgitation, significant atrialization of the right ventricle, and reduced functional RV systolic function.

T2/FLAIR hyperintense cystic lesion with a strongly enhancing mural nodule is identified within the right cerebellar hemisphere. The solid mural nodule measures 1.8 cm and demonstrates minimal restricted diffusion. Marked surrounding vasogenic edema is noted, extending into the cerebellar peduncle and causing mild compression of the fourth ventricle without significant hydrocephalus.

Impression: Cystic and solid mass of the right cerebellar hemisphere, highly suggestive of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. Differential diagnosis includes ganglioglioma or medulloblastoma, though the cerebellar location and classic cystic/mural nodule appearance strongly favor JPA.

MRI of the brain demonstrates multiple, bilateral, asymmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions involving the cerebral subcortical white matter, brainstem, and deep gray matter structures. Some of these lesions demonstrate faint, patchy, non-circumscribed contrast enhancement on post-gadolinium sequences. No mass effect or midline shift is identified.

Impression: Multifocal white matter and deep gray matter lesions, characteristic of acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) given the patient's pediatric presentation and clinical course.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation shows completely normal intracranial structure. The lateral ventricular atria are symmetric and measure 6.3 mm. Cortical folding is progressing as expected, with visible sylvian, parieto-occipital, and cingulate sulci demonstrating normal depth. Brain parenchyma, myelination, and subarachnoid space are within physiological limits.

All other visualized organ systems appear intact and morphologically normal. Impression: Normal fetal brain and body development at 30 weeks gestational age.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates classic features of a Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia and upward rotation of the cerebellar vermis associated with cystic dilation of the posterior fossa fluid space, which freely communicates with the fourth ventricle. The torcula and tentorium are abnormally elevated. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits, with the atrial widths measuring 7.5 mm bilaterally. The cerebral sulcation is appropriate for gestational age.

Impression: Dandy-Walker malformation characterized by cerebellar vermian hypoplasia and posterior fossa expansion. Close monitoring for the development of ventriculomegaly is suggested.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a large, lobulated, avidly enhancing mass centered in the pineal region measuring 3.0 x 2.8 x 2.6 cm. The mass infiltrates the adjacent quadrigeminal plate and exerts significant mass effect on the cerebral aqueduct, resulting in secondary obstructive hydrocephalus with transependymal CSF migration. There is no evidence of spinal drop metastases on screening sequences.

Impression: Large pineal region mass with associated severe obstructive hydrocephalus, most suggestive of a pineoblastoma or germinoma. Neurosurgical evaluation and CSF seeding workup are urgently indicated.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates expected intracranial morphology for this early gestational stage. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits, with the left atrium measuring 5.8 mm and the right measuring 5.5 mm. Sulcation is early but appropriate, with smooth cortical surfaces and early sylvian fissure indentation. The fetal spine and extremities appear normal.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation showing normal development and anatomy.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates a large left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniated contents within the left hemithorax include the stomach and multiple small bowel loops, resulting in a marked mediastinal shift to the right and compression of the developing fetal lungs. The lung-to-head ratio (LHR) is estimated at 1.1, indicating moderate pulmonary hypoplasia. The fetal brain shows normal symmetric ventricles (left atrium 5.5 mm, right atrium 5.4 mm) and age-appropriate sulcal development with defined central and parieto-occipital sulci.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with moderate pulmonary hypoplasia and severe mediastinal shift. Fetal brain structures and sulcation are normal for 30 weeks gestation.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomy. The brain parenchyma shows appropriate sulcal and gyral development, including the appearance of the superior temporal and secondary frontal sulci. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with atrial measurements of 5.6 mm on the left and 5.8 mm on the right. The cerebellum, brainstem, and posterior fossa are within normal limits.

No abnormalities are noted within the fetal thorax, abdomen, or spine. Impression: Completely normal 30-week fetal MRI showing normal brain maturation and normal ventricular sizes.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates findings consistent with complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles are widely separated and run parallel to the sagittal midline. There is a classic 'steer-horn' configuration of the frontal horns on coronal imaging, and mild colpocephaly is noted. The left lateral ventricle atrium measures 11.2 mm, and the right lateral ventricular atrium measures 11.5 mm.

The third ventricle is slightly elevated and dilated. Cerebral sulcation is appropriate for 28 weeks. Visualized abdominal and chest organs are normal. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild bilateral ventriculomegaly and colpocephaly.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 24 weeks gestation reveals bilateral, moderate ventriculomegaly. The right lateral ventricle atrium measures 12.5 mm, and the left lateral ventricle atrium measures 11.8 mm. Cortical folding and sulcation patterns are preserved but slightly compressed. The corpus callosum is present but appears thin. The posterior fossa structures are intact, and the cerebellum is normal in size and morphology.

No other structural or extra-axial anomalies are identified in the fetal trunk. Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly at 24 weeks gestation. Follow-up imaging and postnatal neurosurgical evaluation are recommended.

MR evaluation of the brain reveals a solid, homogenously enhancing midline fourth ventricular mass measuring 3.0 x 2.8 x 2.6 cm, showing restricted diffusion on DWI sequences. The lesion completely effaces the fourth ventricle, resulting in moderate obstructive hydrocephalus with transependymal flow of cerebrospinal fluid surrounding the lateral ventricles.

Impression: Midline posterior fossa mass originating from the fourth ventricle, highly characteristic of medulloblastoma. Urgent neurosurgical intervention is indicated.

The study reveals a significantly dilated and hypokinetic right ventricle with localized dyskinesia and microaneurysm formation along the right ventricular free wall and outflow tract. Myocardial fatty infiltration and patchy subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) are identified within the right ventricular wall, matching the classic criteria for arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC).

Impression: Highly abnormal right ventricular morphology, wall motion, and tissue characterization diagnostic of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC). Right ventricular ejection fraction is significantly depressed at 38%.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation shows a distinct neural tube defect in the lumbosacral region. There is a prominent open myelomeningocele at the L4-S1 levels, accompanied by herniation of neural elements. Secondary intracranial signs of a Chiari II malformation are visualized, including a small posterior fossa, herniation of the cerebellar tonsils (banana sign), and bifrontal narrowing (lemon sign). The lateral ventricles are mildly enlarged, measuring 11.2 mm. Cortical sulcation is smooth, corresponding to 22 weeks.

Impression: Open lumbosacral myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly at 22 weeks gestation.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the heart was performed using multiplanar, ECG-gated steady-state free precession (SSFP) sequences. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 112 mL and end-systolic volume is 42 mL, yielding a calculated left ventricular ejection fraction of 62%. The right ventricle is normal in size and function with an ejection fraction of 58%. There is no evidence of regional wall motion abnormalities, myocardial edema, or late gadolinium enhancement. Both atria are normal in size, and the heart valves are thin and coapt normally.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI study. There is preserved biventricular size and systolic function with no evidence of myocardial scar, inflammation, or structural congenital heart disease.

Neonital brain MRI demonstrates symmetric areas of restricted diffusion on DWI/ADC mapping within the ventrolateral thalami, globus pallidi, and posterior limbs of the internal capsules. There is also mild restricted diffusion along the peri-rolandic cerebral cortex. The ventricles and extra-axial spaces are within normal pediatric limits.

Impression: Findings are highly consistent with acute-to-subacute profound Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) with deep gray matter injury. Clinical correlation with neonatal neurological status is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral renal agenesis. No renal parenchymal tissue or renal arteries are identified in either renal fossa, and there is an empty bladder. Severe, virtually complete oligohydramnios is present, which limits image resolution but allows for confirmation of empty renal fossae and crowded fetal limbs. Fetal lungs are severely hypoplastic, with volumes significantly below the 5th percentile.

The brain anatomy shows early but normal sulcation for 23 weeks, with normal ventricular atria measuring 5.4 mm. Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis (Potter sequence) with severe oligohydramnios and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia.

Brain MRI demonstrates descent of the cerebellar tonsils below the level of the foramen magnum by approximately 8.5 mm. The cerebellar tonsils appear pointed and peg-like. There is narrowing of the CSF spaces at the craniocervical junction. Cerebrospinal fluid flow study demonstrates compromised flow posteriorly. Visualized cervical spine shows no evidence of syrinx formation.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with significant tonsillar ectopia and posterior CSF flow restriction. No syrinx is identified at this time.

MR imaging of the brain was performed using multiplanar, multisequence protocols. There is no evidence of intracranial mass lesion, acute hemorrhage, or infarct. The ventricles and sulci are entirely normal in size and configuration for the patient's age. The major intracranial arterial flow voids are preserved, and the cranial-cervical junction is intact.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural abnormality, mass effect, or sign of acute intracranial disease is identified to explain chronic tension-type headaches.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks gestation. The fetal brain demonstrates normal parenchymal development with appropriate sulcation patterns for the stated gestational age, including early development of the parieto-occipital and calcarine fissures. The lateral ventricles are symmetric and normal in caliber, with the ventricular atrium measuring 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum, cerebellum, and brainstem are morphologically normal.

No chest or abdominal mass effects are identified. The fetal stomach and kidneys are normal in position and size. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation, showing expected intracranial anatomy and age-appropriate sulcation.

Multiplanar, multisequence MR brain imaging is performed. The cerebral parenchyma shows normal signal intensity, and gray-white matter differentiation is preserved. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and cerebral sulci are within normal limits for the patient's age. Symmetrical flow voids are seen in the major intracranial vessels.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural anomalies, ischemic lesions, or intracranial masses are identified to explain the episodes of syncope.

Brain MRI demonstrates severe, symmetric dilation of the lateral and third ventricles. There is abrupt narrowing at the level of the aqueduct of Sylvius with a completely normal-sized fourth ventricle, highly consistent with aqueductal stenosis. Mild thinning of the corpus callosum and transependymal CSF migration (interstitial edema) are noted.

Impression: Congenital aqueductal stenosis resulting in severe obstructive hydrocephalus. Urgent neurosurgical intervention for shunt placement or endoscopic third ventriculostomy is recommended.

MR imaging of the brain was performed utilizing multiplanar, multisequence protocols. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal signal intensity and age-appropriate myelination. No intra- or extra-axial mass lesions, restricted diffusion, or abnormal areas of enhancement are demonstrated. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and sulci are normal in size and configuration.

Impression: Normal MR brain scan. No structural pathology, ischemic injury, or developmental abnormalities found to explain the patient's complaints of recurring tension headaches.

Cardiac MRI evaluating a 1-year-old infant with a known murmur. There is a large perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 8.5 mm, demonstrating a left-to-right shunt. Phase-contrast flow quantification indicates a pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp/Qs) of 1.8, consistent with a moderate-to-large shunt. Consequently, there is mild-to-moderate dilation of the left atrium and left ventricle. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is elevated, and the ejection fraction is 58%.

Impression: Large perimembranous ventricular septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt and associated left heart volume overload. No pulmonary arterial hypertension or reversal of shunt direction is present.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 12-year-old male with a systolic heart murmur detected on routine physical examination. Standard multiplanar cine imaging demonstrates completely normal anatomy. Both ventricles are normal in size, thickness, and contractility. Calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. The cardiac valves are morphologically normal, and phase-contrast imaging confirms physiologic, laminar blood flow across all cardiac ports without valvular stenosis, regurgitation, or shunt.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No anatomical structural abnormalities, shunts, or valvular disease identified to explain the murmur, suggesting a physiologic/innocent etiology.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a structurally normal fetus. The cerebral hemispheres show early and appropriate sulcation for gestational age, featuring the early formation of the parieto-occipital and cingulate sulci. The lateral ventricles are normal in size, with symmetric atrial widths measuring 5.4 mm. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa are structurally intact.

The chest, diaphragm, stomach, bowel, and kidneys are within normal limits. Spine is fully intact. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating age-appropriate structural development and intact fetal anatomy at 22 weeks gestation.

Brain MRI reveals inferior herniation of the cerebellar tonsils below the level of the foramen magnum measuring approximately 9.5 mm. The cerebellar tonsils demonstrate a pointed, peg-like configuration. Assessment of the cervical spine included on the sagittal sequences shows a thin, longitudinally extensive syrinx cavity extending from C2 to C5, measuring up to 2.5 mm in maximum transverse caliber. The ventricular system is non-dilated.

Impression: Chiari I malformation associated with a moderately sized mid-cervical syrinx. Correlation with a dedicated spine MRI and neurosurgical consultation is recommended.

Cardiac MRI performed for evaluation of acute chest pain and elevated troponin. T2-weighted and T2-mapping sequences show patchy, subepicardial hyperintensity in the lateral and inferolateral free walls of the left ventricle, consistent with myocardial edema. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) images demonstrate corresponding patchy subepicardial enhancement in the mid-to-basal lateral wall of the left ventricle, sparing the subendocardium. Biventricular volumes and global systolic functions are within normal limits (LVEF 55%, RVEF 53%).

Impression: Imaging findings meet Lake Louise Criteria, highly indicative of acute active myocarditis in the left ventricular lateral wall. No pericardial effusion is visualized.

Cardiovascular MR imaging in a 13-year-old male with a history of d-Transposition of the Great Arteries, status post arterial switch operation. There is mild, hemodynamically insignificant narrowing at the supravalvular pulmonary stenosis site (diameter 11 mm) with a peak gradient estimated at 15 mmHg. Left and right ventricular volumes are within normal limits (LVEDVI 72 ml/m², RVEDVI 76 ml/m²).

Ventricular systolic function is normal (LVEF 59%, RVEF 57%). No late gadolinium enhancement or focal myocardial fibrosis is seen. Impression: Stable post-arterial switch state with normal biventricular function and only mild, non-obstructive supravalvular pulmonary narrowing.

Brain MRI reveals a well-defined, homogeneous mass in the pineal region measuring 1.8 x 1.6 cm. It is iso-to-hypointense on T1 and hyperintense on T2, demonstrating uniform post-contrast enhancement. The mass compresses the cerebral aqueduct, resulting in moderate dilation of the third and lateral ventricles, indicative of obstructive hydrocephalus.

Impression: Pineal region mass with secondary aqueductal stenosis and hydrocephalus, highly suspicious for a germinoma or pineoblastoma. Urgent neurosurgical and pediatric oncology consultation is advised.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates marked shortening of all long bones, most pronounced proximally. The ribs are severely shortened, resulting in a narrow, bell-shaped thorax and secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. Intracranial imaging reveals borderline ventriculomegaly with the atrial width measuring 10.5 mm, and macrocephaly with frontal bossing. Sulcation patterns are appropriate for 23 weeks, but the temporal lobes show a somewhat bulbous morphology.

Impression: Skeletal dysplasia, most compatible with Thanatophoric dysplasia, given the severe micromelia, narrow chest, and characteristic cranial features.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a well-demarcated cystic lesion with a strongly enhancing eccentric mural nodule located in the right cerebellar hemisphere. The cystic portion measures 2.9 x 2.7 cm, and the solid nodule measures 1.2 x 1.1 cm. There is mild mass effect on the right cerebellar peduncle and fourth ventricle without significant midline shift or ventricular dilatation. Myelination is otherwise appropriate for the patient's age.

Impression: Cystic cerebellar lesion with an enhancing mural nodule, highly characteristic of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. The fourth ventricle remains patent, but neurosurgical consultation is recommended for elective resection.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed using standard pediatric multiplanar sequences including T1, T2, FLAIR, and diffusion-weighted imaging. The cerebral parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity and morphology. There is no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, mass lesion, or demyelinating process. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are within normal limits for age. Visualized cranial nerves and vascular flow voids appear unremarkable.

Impression: Normal MR imaging of the brain. No structural or vascular abnormality is demonstrated to account for the patient's migraine-type headache symptoms.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a severe form of Ebstein's anomaly. There is marked apical displacement of the septal and posterior tricuspid valve leaflets, measuring 32 mm from the mitral valve annulus. This leads to severe atrialization of the right ventricle, with the functional right ventricle being severely restricted and hypokinetic. Severe, free tricuspid regurgitation is present, causing massive enlargement of the right atrium.

Left ventricular function is preserved but shows septal flattening due to right-sided volume overload. LVEF is 56%. Impression: Ebstein's anomaly with severe apical tricuspid valve displacement, significant tricuspid regurgitation, and massive right atrial enlargement.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 5-year-old child who is status-post surgical patch repair of Tetralogy of Fallot. There is severe, free pulmonary regurgitation with a calculated regurgitant fraction of 42% across the reconstructed right ventricular outflow tract. This has resulted in severe dilation of the right ventricle, with an indexed end-diastolic volume of 152 ml/m². The right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly depressed at 44%, while left ventricular size and function are preserved with an EF of 60%.

Impression: Post-repair Tetralogy of Fallot demonstrating severe pulmonary regurgitation and severe right ventricular dilation with mild systolic dysfunction. Close clinical surveillance of RV volumes is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of the corpus callosum. There is characteristic colpocephaly with dilation and tearing of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles, which measure 11.5 mm bilaterally, and parallel alignment of the lateral ventricles. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and moderately dilated. The cerebral sulcation and gyration pattern is normal elsewhere, and no heterotopias are identified.

The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellum and brainstem, are unremarkable. Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with secondary colpocephaly. Pre-natal pediatric neurology counseling is suggested.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates a prominent neural tube defect in the lumbosacral region. There is a defect in the posterior elements of the lower lumbar and sacral spine with an associated herniated sac containing CSF and neural elements, consistent with a myelomeningocele. Intracranial findings are indicative of an associated Arnold-Chiari II malformation, featuring a small posterior fossa, herniation of the cerebellar tonsils/vermis through the foramen magnum, and a characteristic banana-shaped cerebellum. Bilateral severe ventriculomegaly is present, with the lateral ventricular atria measuring 17.5 mm.

The third ventricle is also mildly dilated, and there is bifrontal narrowing of the cranium (lemon sign). Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with classic Arnold-Chiari II malformation findings, including crowding of the posterior fossa, cerebellar herniation, and severe bilateral ventriculomegaly.

MRI of the brain demonstrates a well-circumscribed cystic lesion in the right cerebellar hemisphere measuring approximately 2.8 x 2.5 x 2.4 cm. The lesion features a prominent, intensely enhancing mural nodule along its posterior border. There is mild surrounding vasogenic edema and regional mass effect, resulting in partial compression of the fourth ventricle without significant upstream ventriculomegaly or hydrocephalus.

Impression: Cystic cerebellar lesion with an enhancing mural nodule, highly characteristic of a juvenile pilocytic astrocytoma. Neurosurgical consultation is recommended for surgical planning.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation reveals complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. There is associated colpocephaly with dilated occipital horns of the lateral ventricles; the left atrium measures 12.1 mm and the right atrium measures 11.8 mm. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced and dilated. Sulcation patterns show radial orientation of the medial cerebral sulci, which is classic for this condition.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild bilateral ventriculomegaly/colpocephaly. No other midline or posterior fossa anomalies are identified.

MRI of the brain and orbits shows diffuse, fusiform enlargement of the left optic nerve and optic chiasm. The affected optic pathway structures exhibit T2 hyperintensity and mild, heterogeneous enhancement post-contrast. Multiple foci of abnormal signal intensity (FASIs) are noted in the bilateral globus pallidus, internal capsule, and cerebellar white matter.

Impression: Left optic pathway glioma and classic intracranial T2 hyperintensities (FASIs) in a patient with known Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1).

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal situs solitus and d-looping. The atrial and ventricular septa are intact. Left ventricular and right ventricular sizes and muscle mass are normal for age and body surface area. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%.

Myocardial perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement imaging are completely normal with no evidence of fibrosis or acute injury. Impression: Structurally and functionally normal cardiac MRI.

Cardiac MRI shows a large circumferential pericardial effusion. The fluid measures up to 2.2 cm in the posterior-lateral recess and 1.7 cm anterior to the right ventricle. Diastolic inversion of the right atrium is observed during early diastole, raising concern for hemodynamic significance.

Impression: Large circumferential pericardial effusion with signs of early right atrial diastolic collapse. No evidence of myocardial inflammatory changes or associated myocardial dysfunction.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates normal early fetal anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres are smooth with early insular opercularization, normal for 20 weeks. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits, with atrial widths of 6.5 mm on the left and 6.8 mm on the right. The corpus callosum is early in its development but visible. The posterior fossa, fetal spine, kidneys, bladder, and four-chamber view of the heart appear normal.

Impression: Completely normal early fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation, with age-appropriate structural and intracranial development.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). Herniation of the stomach, multiple loops of small bowel, and the left lobe of the liver into the left hemithorax is noted. This results in significant mass effect, with deviation of the heart and mediastinum into the right hemithorax. The right lung is compressed, and the left lung is severely hypoplastic. Brain development and ventricular size (atrium 6.0 mm) are normal.

Impression: Left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with intrathoracic herniation of stomach, bowel, and liver, causing severe mediastinal shift and pulmonary hypoplasia. Brain development is normal.

Fetal MRI performed at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 14.2 mm and the right lateral ventricular atrium measures 13.5 mm, both exceeding the upper limit of normal. There is mild thinning of the corpus callosum and colpocephalic configuration of the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles. No parenchymal abnormalities or intraventricular hemorrhage are seen.

Remaining fetal anatomy is otherwise normal. Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. Close monitoring with serial ultrasounds and postnatal neurodevelopmental evaluation is recommended.

Postoperative MRI of the brain demonstrates expected postsurgical changes following sagittal synostosis repair, with a stable cranial vault configuration. The cerebral hemispheres are symmetric, showing no signs of restricted diffusion or subdural fluid collections. Ventricles and extra-axial CSF spaces are within normal pediatric limits, and the major dural sinuses appear patent on flow-sensitive sequences.

Impression: Stable, normal postoperative brain MRI following craniosynostosis repair. No acute intracranial complications, mass effect, or abnormal fluid collections are identified.

Multiplanar, multisequence brain MRI was performed to evaluate recurrent, progressive headaches. The cerebral hemispheres, cerebellum, and brainstem demonstrate normal morphology, signal intensity, and myelination patterns appropriate for a 5-year-old child. The ventricular system, basal cisterns, and subarachnoid spaces are within normal limits. No abnormal contrast enhancement or restricted diffusion is visualized.

Impression: Unremarkable brain MRI with no structural or intracranial pathology identified to account for patient's headaches.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a normal intracranial configuration. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric and measure 5.2 mm in atrial width bilaterally. The cerebral cortex is smooth, corresponding to normal developmental milestones at 22 weeks. The corpus callosum is intact. The brainstem, cerebellum, and cisterna magna are within normal limits.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation. No intracranial anomalies or ventriculomegaly identified.

MR imaging of the brain was conducted to evaluate a new-onset behavioral change. The scan demonstrates symmetric gray-white matter differentiation and normal cortical sulcation. No localized signal abnormalities, white matter lesions, or ischemic updates are visible. The ventricular size is stable and matches age norms. The craniocervical junction and major flow voids are normal.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, inflammatory, or neoplastic etiologies identified to account for behavioral changes.

Fetal MRI performed at 31 weeks gestation reveals a Dandy-Walker variant (hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with a mild elevation). There is a keyhole-like communication between the fourth ventricle and the cisterna magna, which is mildly dilated at 12 mm. Intracranial sulcation is normal for 31 weeks. The lateral ventricles are slightly dilated, with both atria measuring 10.3 mm.

The corpus callosum is fully formed. Visualized fetal spine, thoracic, and abdominal organs are within normal limits. Impression: Dandy-Walker variant/cerebellar vermian hypoplasia with borderline ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular size and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. Myocardial wall thickness is within normal limits for body surface area, with no regional wall motion abnormalities or delayed gadolinium enhancement to suggest myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI study. Normal ventricular volumes, preserved systolic function, and no evidence of active inflammation or myocardial scarring.

Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates normal cardiac anatomy and biventricular function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% (LVEDVI 72 mL/m²), and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%, with no regional wall motion abnormalities or chamber dilation. Valve leaflets appear thin and mobile, without evidence of significant stenosis or regurgitation. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows no areas of myocardial scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI with preserved biventricular size and function, and no evidence of myocardial fibrosis.

Brain MRI obtained to evaluate developmental delay. The cortical gyral pattern and myelination progression are entirely normal and appropriate for a 7-year-old. No structural brain anomalies, destructive lesions, areas of abnormal signal intensity, or pathological contrast enhancement are identified.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No structural, myelination, or migrational delays identified as an organic etiology for the patient's developmental delay.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates a severely dilated posterior fossa. There is marked hypoplasia and rotation of the cerebellar vermis associated with cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle, which freely communicates with the enlarged posterior fossa. The lateral ventricles are mildly prominent, with the atria measuring 9.8 mm. The tentorium cerebelli is elevated.

No other structural abnormalities are seen in the fetal torso, chest, or spine. Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation. Pediatric neurosurgical consultation is recommended prenatally.

Cardiac MRI evaluates valvular structure and hemodynamics. There is prominent myxomatous degeneration and prolapse of the posterior leaflet (P2 segment) of the mitral valve into the left atrium during systole. This results in an eccentric, anteriorly directed jet of severe mitral regurgitation, with a regurgitant volume of 48 mL per beat. The left ventricle is mildly dilated (LVEDVI 98 mL/m2) with compensatory hyperdynamic systolic function (EF 68%).

Impression: Severe mitral valve prolapse with severe mitral regurgitation. Compensatory left ventricular dilation with preserved global systolic function.

Cardiac MRI and coronary MR angiography demonstrate focal aneurysmal dilation of the proximal left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery, measuring 5.2 mm in diameter, and a smaller aneurysm in the proximal right coronary artery (RCA) measuring 4.1 mm. Myocardial perfusion imaging is normal during rest, and late gadolinium enhancement sequence reveals no myocardial infarction or replacement fibrosis. Ventricular size and ejection fraction (61%) are normal.

Impression: Bilateral proximal coronary artery aneurysms, highly consistent with sequelae of Kawasaki disease. No evidence of myocardial ischemia or prior myocardial infarction.

High-resolution MRI of the brain reveals localized thickening of the cortex in the left superior frontal gyrus. There is associated blurring of the gray-white matter junction and a faint band of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity extending from the subcortical white matter toward the ventricle, consistent with a transmantle sign. No mass effect or surrounding edema is seen.

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia (likely Type II) of the left superior frontal gyrus, corresponding well to the patient's refractory epilepsy. Neurosurgical planning/functional mapping may be considered.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates normal and highly advanced fetal brain anatomy. There is a complex and age-appropriate sulcation pattern, including deep secondary and tertiary gyri across both cerebral hemispheres. The lateral ventricles are completely normal, with symmetric atrial widths of 6.0 mm. No intracranial masses, hemorrhage, or midline shifts are seen. The brainstem and cerebellum are completely normal in size and appearance.

Impression: Completely normal fetal brain MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrating excellent, age-appropriate gyral/sulcal development and normal ventricular calibers.

Brain MRI demonstrating normal ventricular system, unremarkable gray-white matter differentiation. No extra-axial fluid collections or structural lesions are identified. Normal development of myelination and corpus callosum for a 4-year-old.

Impression: Unremarkable and completely normal brain MRI. There is no structural or pathological abnormality seen within the intracranial vaults.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation evaluates suspected renal abnormality. The right kidney is enlarged and replaced by multiple, non-communicating cysts of varying sizes, consistent with a multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The contralateral left kidney is normal in size and appearance, showing mild compensatory hypertrophy. Amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits.

Fetal brain anatomy and development are normal. Impression: Unilateral right-sided multicystic dysplastic kidney with a normal, hypertrophied left kidney.

Cardiac MRI performed to rule out structural anomalies in a patient presenting with palpitations. All cardiac chambers are within normal volume limits for the patient's age and body surface area. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 64% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or delayed enhancement are seen.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of structural heart disease, focal fibrosis, or active inflammation.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The rostrum and anterior body of the corpus callosum are present, but the posterior body and splenium are absent. There is associated mild colpocephaly, with the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles measuring 10.5 mm.

Sulcation is otherwise age-appropriate. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with mild colpocephaly.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a dorsal neural tube defect. There is a lumbosacral myelomeningocele with herniation of the neural placode and meninges through a bony defect in the posterior elements of L4-S2. This is associated with an Arnold-Chiari II malformation, characterized by caudal descent of the cerebellar tonsils into the foramen magnum and a classic 'banana sign' shape of the cerebellum. The lateral ventricles are moderately dilated, with atrial measurements of 11.8 mm.

Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with Chiari II malformation and moderate ventriculomegaly. Prenatal evaluation for potential in-utero repair is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation reveals a left multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The left kidney is enlarged and filled with multiple, variable-sized, non-communicating cysts. The right kidney is normal in size and signal intensity. Amniotic fluid volume is completely normal. The fetal brain shows normal development, with ventricles measuring 6.4 mm and appropriate sulcation.

Impression: Left multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK). The contralateral kidney is completely normal, and normal amniotic fluid volume suggests preserved overall renal function.

The study demonstrates normal left and right ventricular morphology and function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 64%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%. Myocardial tissue characterization reveals normal native T1 and T2 relaxation times. No pathological late gadolinium enhancement is seen. Valvular function and great vessel anatomy are completely normal.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of myocardial inflammation, infiltration, scar, or structural heart disease.

MRI of the brain demonstrates diffuse fusiform enlargement and abnormal T2 hyperintensity of the intraorbital segment of the left optic nerve. The nerve demonstrates moderate contrast enhancement. Multiple foci of abnormal signal intensity (FASI) are noted in the bilateral globus pallidus and brainstem.

Impression: Left optic pathway glioma and characteristic cerebral foci of abnormal signal intensity in a patient with clinical neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1).

Cardiac MRI of an 11-year-old female presenting with symptoms of progressive dyspnea and exercise intolerance. There is marked dilation of the left ventricle with an end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVI) of 145 ml/m² and thinning of the ventricular myocardium. Global left ventricular systolic function is severely depressed with an ejection fraction of 28%, accompanied by diffuse hypokinesis. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with a depressed ejection fraction of 38%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates linear mid-wall fibrosis in the interventricular septum, characteristic of non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy.

Impression: Severe bi-ventricular dilated cardiomyopathy with mid-wall septal fibrosis. Markedly reduced left ventricular systolic function (LVEF 28%).

MR evaluation of the cervical junction and brain demonstrates downward herniation of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum by approximately 8.5 mm. The cerebellar tonsils appear pointed and peg-like. There is narrowing of the CSF spaces at the level of the craniocervical junction. The ventricular system is normal in size, and sagittal sequences through the upper spinal cord show no evidence of syrinx formation.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 8.5 mm tonsillar ectopia and effacement of the CSF spaces at the foramen magnum. No associated syringomyelia or hydrocephalus is identified at this time.

MR imaging of the infant brain demonstrates several small, non-enhancing subependymal nodules lining the lateral ventricles, which are hypointense on T2 and hyperintense on T1. Additionally, multiple wedge-shaped areas of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity are observed within the subcortical white matter of both cerebral hemispheres, consistent with cortical tubers. No subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA) is detected.

Impression: Brain MRI features highly consistent with Tuberous Sclerosis Complex, showing multiple cortical tubers and subependymal nodules. No hydrocephalus or signs of SEGA are observed.

Fetal MRI performed at 24 weeks gestation shows normal intracranial architecture. The fetal brain exhibits age-appropriate sulcal development, with the sylvian fissures showing normal configuration. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atrial diameter measuring 6.5 mm on both sides. The corpus callosum is intact, and the posterior fossa demonstrates a well-formed cerebellum and normal brainstem.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation. Intracranial structures, ventricular measurements, and sulcal patterns are within normal limits for this stage of development.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates a neural tube defect located in the lumbosacral region. There is a defect in the posterior spinal elements from L4 through S2 with a herniated myelomeningocele sac containing CSF and neural placode. Brain imaging shows characteristic secondary signs including a flattened, 'banana-shaped' cerebellum, obliteration of the cisterna magna, and bifrontal narrowing of the skull ('lemon sign').

The lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, with the atria measuring 10.8 mm. The cerebral sulcation is appropriate for 22 weeks. Impression: Open lumbosacral myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation and mild ventriculomegaly.

Brain MRI shows a tightly packed cluster of dilated, tortuous vascular channels (flow voids) in the right parietal lobe, measuring 2.1 x 1.8 cm. There is prominent signal void on T2-weighted sequences representing feeding arteries and draining veins. Mild peripheral gliosis is seen in the adjacent brain parenchyma, but no evidence of acute or chronic parenchymal hemorrhage is detected.

Impression: Unruptured arteriovenous malformation (AVM) in the right parietal lobe. No acute intracranial hemorrhage or mass effect is visualized.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral renal hydronephrosis. The right renal pelvis measures 11.2 mm and the left measures 12.5 mm in anteroposterior diameter. No significant cortical thinning or cystic dysplasia of the renal parenchymas is visualized. The urinary bladder is visualized and appears normal in size. Amniotic fluid volume is within the normal range, indicating adequate urine output.

Fetal brain anatomy, ventricles (6.2 mm), and sulcation are entirely unremarkable. Impression: Bilateral fetal hydronephrosis, likely due to bilateral ureteropelvic junction (UPJ) obstruction. Stable amniotic fluid is reassuring; suggest serial postnatal renal ultrasounds.

Multiplanar cardiac MRI demonstrates normal anatomy, chamber size, and wall thickness. Cine imaging shows excellent global and segmental biventricular systolic function with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 62% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 57%. No abnormal late gadolinium enhancement or edema is identified, ruling out occult cardiomyopathy or myocarditis. The aorta and pulmonary trunk are normal in caliber.

Impression: Unremarkable and completely normal cardiac MRI study. No evidence of structural or functional cardiovascular pathology.

Cardiac MRI shows normal heart anatomy with standard chamber sizes and excellent biventricular systolic function. Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction (RVEF) is 60%. No focal scarring, ventricular septal defects, or atrial shunts are identified. Myocardial T1 and T2 relaxation times are within expected physiological limits.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. No congenital anomalies or structural defects identified to account for patient's history of benign systolic murmur.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation reveals pronounced, symmetric dilation of the lateral ventricles. The right and left lateral ventricular atria measure 18.2 mm and 17.9 mm respectively, consistent with severe bilateral ventriculomegaly. There is thinning of the overlying cerebral cortex, and the sulcation pattern appears delayed, resembling a 28-week gestation. The aqueduct of Sylvius appears stenosed, and there is mild third ventricular dilation measuring 4.5 mm.

The corpus callosum is visible but stretched superiorly. The posterior fossa structures, including the cerebellum and brainstem, are within normal limits. Impression: Severe bilateral ventriculomegaly, likely secondary to aqueductal stenosis, with associated delay in cortical maturation.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation reveals a midline bony defect in the occipital bone with herniation of meninges and a small amount of dysplastic cerebellar tissue into a posterior sac, measuring 2.4 x 1.8 cm, consistent with an occipital encephalocele. The lateral ventricular atria measure 9.5 mm bilaterally, indicating mild ventriculomegaly. The brainstem is slightly distorted and pulled posteriorly.

Sulcation is early but appropriate for 21 weeks gestation. Spine and remainder of fetal anatomy appear intact. Impression: Midline occipital encephalocele containing herniated dural membranes and cerebellar tissue, associated with mild ventriculomegaly and brainstem distortion.

Sagittal T1-weighted images demonstrate peg-like herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 8 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. There is associated crowding of the craniocervical junction. Screening sagittal images of the cervical spine demonstrate no evidence of an associated syrinx. The supratentorial ventricles and cerebral hemispheres are normal in size and appearance.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 8 mm cerebellar tonsillar ectopia causing crowding of the posterior fossa at the craniovertebral junction. No syringomyelia is visualized on current sagittal spinal sequences.

Brain MRI was performed for atypical migraine workup. Visualized parenchyma of the cerebrum, brainstem, and cerebellum is structurally intact with no evidence of focal ischemia, parenchymal hemorrhage, demyelination, or mass lesion. The ventricles and extra-axial CSF spaces are within normal limits. Normal cranial vascular flow voids are present.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No intracranial mass, ischemia, hemorrhage, or malformation identified to account for atypical headaches.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal gray-white matter distribution. The ventricles and sulci are symmetric and completely normal in size. No acute infarcts, intracranial hemorrhages, or mass lesions are seen. Major vascular structures at the skull base show preserved flow voids, and the orbital structures and paranasal sinuses are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No structural, vascular, or inflammatory pathology identified to explain the patient's chronic migraines.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 26 weeks gestation shows complete agenesis of the corpus callosum. The lateral ventricles exhibit a teardrop configuration (colpocephaly) with dilation of the occipital horns; the left atrium measures 11.8 mm and the right measures 12.1 mm. The third ventricle is superiorly displaced. Sulcation is appropriate for 26 weeks, but the medial hemispheric sulci show a radial arrangement.

Impression: Complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly. No other midline brain anomalies or extracranial findings are demonstrated.

High-resolution brain MRI performed using a dedicated epilepsy protocol. There is normal cortical thickness and gyral pattern throughout both cerebral hemispheres. Symmetric hippocampal volumes and normal internal architecture are demonstrated, without T2 or FLAIR hyperintensity. No focal cortical dysplasia, vascular malformations, or mass lesions are identified.

Impression: Normal brain MRI with no epileptogenic focus detected. Specifically, there is no evidence of mesial temporal sclerosis or cortical malformation.

Cardiac MRI reveals normal cardiac anatomy and function. The left and right ventricular chambers are normal in size. Ventricular contractility is preserved, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 65% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 60%. Myocardial tissue characterization is normal with no abnormal late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No evidence of congenital heart anomalies or acquired cardiomyopathy.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates normal anatomy. The cerebral hemispheres exhibit well-developed sulcation and operculization appropriate for the gestational age. The ventricular system is symmetric and within normal limits; the left lateral ventricular atrium measures 5.6 mm and the right measures 5.4 mm. The corpus callosum, cerebellum, and brainstem are morphologically intact.

The lungs, diaphragm, heart, liver, kidneys, and musculoskeletal structures appear normal. Amniotic fluid volume is unremarkable. Impression: Completely normal fetal MRI study demonstrating normal structural development and age-appropriate brain maturation at 35 weeks gestation.

A well-defined, extra-axial fluid collection is demonstrated within the left middle cranial fossa, measuring approximately 4.5 x 3.0 x 2.8 cm. The signal intensity matches cerebrospinal fluid on all sequences, including complete suppression on FLAIR and absence of restricted diffusion on DWI. There is mild remodeling of the adjacent sphenoid wing and temporal bone, but no significant mass effect on the temporal lobe or midline shift.

Impression: Large, stable left temporal arachnoid cyst (Galassi classification Type II) with mild mass effect on the temporal tip, without midline shift or herniation.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals abnormal posterior fossa anatomy. There is mild fourth ventricular enlargement and a hypoplastic, elevated cerebellar vermis, consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits (7.2 mm). Sulcation and myelination patterns are appropriate for 26 weeks.

The rest of the fetus, including the heart, abdomen, and limbs, is normal. Impression: Dandy-Walker variant with cerebellar vermis hypoplasia. Prenatal genetics and pediatric neurosurgery counseling are recommended.

Postoperative cardiac MRI evaluates a patient status post arterial switch operation for D-transposition of the great arteries (D-TGA). The neo-aorta and neo-pulmonary trunk demonstrate normal spatial relationships. There is mild narrowing of the main pulmonary artery at the site of surgical reconstruction, with a localized peak flow velocity of 2.1 m/s, suggesting non-obstructive supravalvular stenosis. Left and right ventricular sizes and systolic function are preserved (LVEF 60%, RVEF 55%).

Impression: Stable postoperative appearances after arterial switch for D-TGA, with mild, non-obstructive supravalvular pulmonary stenosis. No myocardial perfusion deficits or scar identified on late-phase sequences.

Cardiac MRI reveals a large, circumferentially distributed pericardial effusion measuring up to 18 mm along the posterior wall and 14 mm adjacent to the right atrium. There is no evidence of diastolic collapse of the right atrium or right ventricle to suggest cardiac tamponade. The underlying myocardium shows normal thickness and signal intensity, and biventricular function is preserved (LVEF 61%).

Impression: Large pericardial effusion without current evidence of hemodynamic compromise or tamponade. No associated myocardial signal abnormalities or late gadolinium enhancement.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates severe dilation of the left ventricle with an end-diastolic volume index (LVEDVI) of 145 mL/m² and diffuse hypocontractility. The left ventricular ejection fraction is severely reduced at 28%. The right ventricle is also mildly dilated with a reduced ejection fraction of 42%. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging demonstrates mid-myocardial linear enhancement along the interventricular septum, typical for a non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy.

Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular enlargement and systolic dysfunction, accompanied by mid-myocardial fibrosis suggestive of a non-ischemic etiology.

Cardiac MRI evaluates status post tetralogy of Fallot surgical repair. The right ventricle is severely dilated, with an end-diastolic volume index of 158 mL/m2. Phase-contrast imaging of the main pulmonary artery demonstrates a severe regurgitant fraction of 42%, consistent with severe pulmonary insufficiency. The right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 44%, with dyskinesis noted at the RV outflow tract patch. The left ventricle demonstrates normal size and function with an ejection fraction of 55%.

Impression: Findings are consistent with status post Tetralogy of Fallot repair showing severe pulmonary valve regurgitation, marked right ventricular dilation, and mild right ventricular systolic dysfunction. No evidence of major branch pulmonary artery stenosis.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation demonstrates features consistent with skeletal dysplasia, suspicious for thanatophoric dysplasia. There is marked shortening of all long bones, particularly the femurs and humeri, which demonstrate curved morphology ('telephone receiver' sign). The fetal thorax is extremely narrow and bell-shaped, resulting in secondary compression of the lungs. The skull shows frontal bossing with cloverleaf skull deformity, and the cerebral ventricles are mildly prominent (atria measure 9.8 mm).

Impression: Severe micromelic skeletal dysplasia with a narrow, hypoplastic thorax and cloverleaf skull, highly suggestive of thanatophoric dysplasia.

Fetal MRI at 32 weeks gestation reveals generalized, severe demineralization of the fetal skeleton. Multiple fractures of the long bones are visualized, with associated severe shortening and angulation of the femora and humeri. The ribs show a beaded appearance due to multiple healing fractures, leading to a small, bell-shaped thorax. Extreme compressibility of the calvarium is noted during imaging.

Intracranial structures are intact, though there is mild ventriculomegaly with atrial widths of 10.1 mm bilaterally. Sulcation is appropriate for 32 weeks. Impression: Severe osteochondrodysplasia with findings highly characteristic of Osteogenesis Imperfecta Type II, including multiple fractures, severe micromelia, and a small chest cavity.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates a normal singleton pregnancy with normal intracranial development. The cerebral cortex shows expected opercularization of the sylvian fissures and early development of the parieto-occipital sulci, consistent with 27 weeks gestation. The ventricular system is normal, with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 5.9 mm at the atria. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal in morphology.

Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation with normal cerebral sulcation and ventricular measurements.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a Dandy-Walker variant (isolated inferior vermian hypoplasia). The cerebellar vermis is mildly hypoplastic inferiorly, accompanied by a modest upward rotation. There is a corresponding mild widening of the posterior fossa fluid space, which communicates with the fourth ventricle. No severe ventriculomegaly is noted; the lateral ventricular atria measure 7.1 mm. Cerebral sulcation is normal.

Impression: Inferior cerebellar vermian hypoplasia consistent with a Dandy-Walker variant. Mild posterior fossa widening without hydrocephalus.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates status post stage II single-ventricle palliation (bidirectional Glenn shunt) for hypoplastic left heart syndrome. The superior vena cava is anastomosed to the right pulmonary artery, with unobstructed, laminar forward blood flow demonstrated on velocity-encoded imaging. The single right ventricle is moderately dilated but exhibits preserved systolic function with an ejection fraction of 51%. The hypoplastic left ventricle is severely diminutive and non-functional. Mild-to-moderate neoaortic valve regurgitation is noted.

Impression: Patent, unobstructed bidirectional Glenn shunt in a patient with hypoplastic left heart syndrome. Single right ventricular systolic function is adequate, with mild-to-moderate neoaortic regurgitation.

MR examination of the brain demonstrates multiple discrete, ovoid T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several of these lesions demonstrate a perpendicular orientation to the lateral ventricles, consistent with Dawson's fingers. Post-contrast imaging shows active nodular enhancement in two of the periventricular lesions, indicating active demyelination.

Impression: Multiple demyelinating lesions demonstrating spatial and temporal dissemination, highly suggestive of pediatric multiple sclerosis or an acute demyelinating encephalomyelitis spectrum. Clinical correlation with cerebrospinal fluid analysis is recommended.

In a patient with neurofibromatosis type 1, MRI of the brain demonstrates diffuse, fusiform enlargement and T2/FLAIR hyperintensity of the left optic nerve and optic chiasm. The affected pathway shows moderate, uniform contrast enhancement. Multiple subcortical focal areas of signal intensity (FASIs) or 'unidentified bright objects' are noted in the bilateral basal ganglia and cerebellum, typical for this clinical condition.

Impression: Features of an optic pathway glioma involving the left optic nerve and optic chiasm, accompanied by classic basal ganglia and cerebellar FASIs, consistent with known neurofibromatosis type 1. Close ophthalmic and neuro-oncological surveillance is required.

Fetal MRI at 24 weeks gestation demonstrates severe bilateral hydroureteronephrosis and a massively distended urinary bladder (megacystis) with a thickened bladder wall. These findings are highly characteristic of bladder outlet obstruction, likely due to posterior urethral valves. Oligohydramnios is present.

Fetal lungs are mildly hypoplastic. Intracranial anatomy is unremarkable. Impression: Fetal bladder outlet obstruction with megacystis, bilateral hydronephrosis, and oligohydramnios.

MRI brain demonstrates a hypercellular midline posterior fossa mass centered in the cerebellar vermis, measuring 3.5 cm in its greatest dimension. The lesion is hypointense on T1-weighted imaging, hyperintense on T2/FLAIR, and shows restricted diffusion on DWI. Mild heterogeneous contrast enhancement is noted. Moderate compression of the fourth ventricle with resultant enlargement of the third and lateral ventricles indicates early obstructive hydrocephalus.

Impression: Midline posterior fossa mass originating from the cerebellar vermis, highly suspicious for medulloblastoma. Urgent neurosurgical and pediatric oncology consultations are recommended.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large, well-defined extra-axial fluid collection in the left middle cranial fossa, measuring 4.2 x 2.8 cm. The signal of the fluid matches cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) on all sequences, including complete suppression on FLAIR. There is mild mass effect on the left temporal lobe and mild remodeling of the overlying squamosal temporal bone, but no midline shift or ventricular compression.

Impression: Large left temporal arachnoid cyst (Galassi Type II) with mild local mass effect but no herniation or obstructive hydrocephalus.

The cardiac MRI examination shows completely normal cardiac morphology. All cardiac chambers are normal in size, and there is no evidence of regional or global ventricular dysfunction. Valvular structures are thin, mobile, and demonstrate normal excursion without stenosis or regurgitation. T1 and T2 mapping parameters of the myocardium are within normal limits, and there is no late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Structurally and functionally normal cardiovascular system. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 63% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%.

MRI demonstrates a lobulated, heterogeneous, soft-tissue mass filling the fourth ventricle, measuring approximately 3.2 x 2.6 cm. The tumor appears to protrude through the foramina of Luschka into the cerebellopontine angle. Moderate to severe upstream ventricular dilation involving the third and lateral ventricles is present, consistent with obstructive hydrocephalus, along with mild transependymal flow of CSF.

Impression: Fourth ventricular mass with extension into the lateral apertures, most consistent with a pediatric ependymoma. Secondary obstructive hydrocephalus is noted.

MRI of the brain and craniocervical junction demonstrates herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 8.5 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils appear pointed and peg-like. There is effacement of the CSF spaces at the level of the craniocervical junction, but no evidence of a syrinx in the visualized cervical spine. Brain parenchyma is otherwise structurally normal with appropriate gray-white matter differentiation.

Impression: Chiari I malformation without associated cervical syringomyelia. Clinical correlation is recommended for symptoms such as occipital headaches or cranial nerve dysfunction.

Brain MRI shows a heterogeneous, partially cystic and solid mass centered within the pineal region, measuring 2.4 x 2.2 x 2.0 cm. The mass compresses the tectal plate, resulting in partial obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct and moderate symmetrical dilatation of the third and lateral ventricles. Interspersed microcalcifications and nodular enhancement are present.

Impression: Pineal region mass with secondary aqueductal stenosis and hydrocephalus. Differential diagnosis includes pineoblastoma or germinoma; correlation with serum/CSF tumor markers is recommended.

Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging shows normal cardiac chamber dimensions and wall thickness. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 142 mL (indexed to 76 mL/m²), and right ventricular end-diastolic volume is 145 mL. No regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of ventricular dyskinesis are observed. Post-contrast late gadolinium enhancement imaging is completely negative for myocardial scar or fibrosis.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study. No arrhythmogenic substrate, structural disease, or fibrosis identified in this patient evaluated for frequent premature ventricular contractions.

Brain MRI demonstrates asymmetric thickening and enlargement of the left optic nerve, which displays diffuse T2-hyperintensity and moderate contrast enhancement. This lesion extends posteriorly to the optic chiasm. In addition, there are multiple foci of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity ('FASI' or vacuolation changes) in the bilateral globus pallidus and internal capsule, which do not show enhancement or mass effect.

Impression: Optic pathway glioma involving the left optic nerve and chiasm, together with characteristic focal areas of signal intensity (FASI) in the basal ganglia. These findings are diagnostic of Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1).

Cardiac MRI shows a large secundum-type atrial septal defect (ASD) measuring 14 mm in maximal diameter. This defect results in a significant left-to-right shunt with a calculated pulmonary-to-systemic flow ratio (Qp/Qs) of 2.1. The right atrium and right ventricle are severely dilated, with a right ventricular end-diastolic volume index (RVEDVI) of 135 mL/m2. Right ventricular systolic function remains preserved with an ejection fraction of 55%.

No significant ventricular septal defect or anomalous pulmonary venous return is identified. The main pulmonary artery is mildly dilated. Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect causing significant right-sided volume overload, indicating a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt appropriate for closure.

Fetal MRI performed at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis with upward rotation and a markedly enlarged posterior fossa cyst communicating with the fourth ventricle. This is accompanied by ventriculomegaly, with the lateral ventricular atria measuring 12.2 mm bilaterally. The cerebral sulcation is minimally delayed for 26 weeks, with shallow sylvian fissures.

There is no evidence of supratentorial parenchymal destruction. The chest and abdomen are unremarkable. Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation with cerebellar vermian hypoplasia, cystic dilatation of the posterior fossa, and secondary moderate ventriculomegaly.

Brain MRI demonstrates multiple large, poorly marginated, bilateral, and asymmetric areas of hyperintensity on T2-weighted and FLAIR sequences throughout the cerebral white matter, basal ganglia, and brainstem. There is minimal surrounding mass effect, and several of these lesions show open-ring or punctate enhancement following gadolinium administration. No restricted diffusion is observed.

Impression: Multifocal demyelinating lesions of the brain, highly indicative of acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) or pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis. Recommend clinical and CSF correlation.

Brain MRI shows multiple oval, well-demarcated hyperintense lesions on T2/FLAIR sequences distributed throughout the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several lesions exhibit orientation perpendicular to the lateral ventricles, consistent with 'Dawson's fingers.' Following administration of intravenous gadolinium, two of the periventricular lesions demonstrate active, nodular enhancement, indicating acute demyelinating activity. The optic chiasm and visualized spinal cord segment appear unaffected.

Impression: Multiple demyelinating plaques showing dissemination in space and time, strongly supportive of a diagnosis of pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS) or acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM).

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates mild, isolated bilateral ventriculomegaly. The lateral ventricular atria measure 11.2 mm on the left and 10.8 mm on the right. No other intracranial abnormalities are identified; the corpus callosum, posterior fossa structures, and sulcation patterns are appropriate for 23 weeks.

The rest of the fetal survey is completely normal. Impression: Mild isolated bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly. Follow-up imaging is recommended.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation shows an open neural tube defect. There is a low lumbar myelomeningocele characterized by a defect in the posterior elements of the L4-S1 vertebrae, with protrusion of a fluid-filled sac containing neural tissue. Features of an Arnold-Chiari II malformation are present, including herniation of the cerebellar tonsils/vermis through the foramen magnum and a banana-shaped cerebellum. Bilateral ventricular atria measure 10.5 mm, representing early ventriculomegaly.

Impression: Open lumbar myelomeningocele with Chiari II malformation and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly. Prenatal repair evaluation is recommended.

High-resolution T2 and FLAIR imaging demonstrates a focal area of cortical thickening and blurred gray-white matter junction in the right frontal lobe. There is a subtle band of hyperintensity extending from the dysplastic cortex toward the lateral ventricle, consistent with a transmantle sign. No mass effect, extra-axial collection, or abnormal enhancement is noted.

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia of the right frontal lobe with a transmantle sign, which represents a highly epileptogenic structural anomaly. Correlation with electroencephalogram (EEG) findings is advised.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation demonstrates severely enlarged, symmetric, highly echogenic kidneys filling the fetal abdomen, highly suspicious for autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD). Severe oligohydramnios is present. Fetal intracranial structures are normal; the lateral ventricles are symmetric and measure 5.8 mm. The sulcation pattern is well-developed, demonstrating deep central and cingulate sulci consistent with 33 weeks.

Impression: Fetal renal anomaly at 33 weeks gestation, highly consistent with infantile polycystic kidney disease (ARPKD) accompanied by severe oligohydramnios.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates severe bilateral ventriculomegaly with significant thinning of the surrounding cerebral cortex. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 18.5 mm, and the right lateral ventricular atrium measures 17.9 mm. While the 36-week sulcation pattern is present, there is noticeable compression of the cortical mantle. The corpus callosum is intact but thinned and stretched. The posterior fossa and brainstem are otherwise normal.

Impression: Severe bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly with cerebral parenchymal compression, requiring postnatal neurosurgical evaluation.

Brain MRI reveals marked leptomeningeal enhancement over the left parietal and occipital lobes, associated with severe ipsilateral volume loss (atrophy) of the cerebral cortex. Compensatory enlargement of the left lateral ventricle and left choroid plexus is seen. Serpentine prominent periventricular collateral veins are visualized.

Impression: Classical MR findings of encephalotrigeminal angiomatosis (Sturge-Weber syndrome) involving the left cerebral hemisphere with prominent leptomeningeal angioma and cortical atrophy.

Imaging demonstrates classic features of Ebstein's anomaly. There is marked apical displacement of the septal and posterior tricuspid valve leaflets (displacement index of 28 mm/m²). This displacement results in severe atrialization of the basal right ventricle. The functional right ventricle is small and demonstrates moderately reduced systolic function (EF 36%). The right atrium is severely dilated, and there is massive, severe tricuspid regurgitation.

Impression: Ebstein's anomaly with severe tricuspid valve leaflet displacement, massive right atrial dilation, and moderate functional right ventricular impairment.

MRI of the brain demonstrates normal anatomical structure. The cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres are symmetric, with normal gyral patterns and preserved gray-white matter boundaries. There are no space-occupying lesions, infarcts, or hemorrhages. The ventricles, sulci, and cisterns are of normal configuration and size. Cranial nerves are unremarkable and major vascular channels show normal flow voids.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No intracranial etiology identified to explain the episodes of syncope.

The study evaluates a patient with hypoplastic left heart syndrome (HLHS) post-Fontan completion. There is an extracardiac Fontan conduit with normal laminar flow and no evidence of focal thrombus, stenosis, or narrowing. Right ventricular end-diastolic volume is moderately increased, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 46%.

Impression: Status post-extracardiac Fontan completion for HLHS. There is a patent conduit without obstruction, and mild systemic (right) ventricular dilation and mild systolic dysfunction are observed, typical for this stage of palliation.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates bilateral renal agenesis. Both renal fossae are empty, and no normal renal tissue or renal arteries are identified. There is severe, near-complete oligohydramnios, which significantly limits fetal movement and image quality. The fetal bladder is not visualized, indicating a lack of fetal urine production. Fetal chest volume is reduced, consistent with secondary pulmonary hypoplasia. Intracranial sulcation is appropriate for gestational age.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with anhydramnios and signs of pulmonary hypoplasia. This is a lethal renal anomaly; maternal counseling is recommended.

Cardiac MRI shows thickening and restricted mobility of the anterior mitral valve leaflet with classic 'hockey-stick' deformity, highly indicative of chronic rheumatic heart disease. A high-velocity regurgitant jet is visualized entering the left atrium during systole, occupying >40% of the left atrial area, consistent with severe mitral regurgitation. The left atrium is significantly dilated (volume index 54 ml/m2), and the left ventricle is moderately dilated but retains a preserved ejection fraction of 60%.

Impression: Chronic rheumatic heart disease with severe mitral regurgitation and associated left atrial and left ventricular dilation.

Fetal MRI performed at 22 weeks gestation evaluates a single live fetus. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal symmetric development. The sulcation pattern is entirely appropriate for this gestational age, with early development of the Sylvian fissures. The bilateral ventricular atria measure within normal parameters, with the left atrium measuring 5.8 mm and the right atrium measuring 5.6 mm. The corpus callosum is fully visualized and structurally intact, and the brainstem and posterior fossa structures are normal.

Fetal body structures, including the diaphragm, abdominal viscera, and spine, appear normal. Amniotic fluid volume is subjectively within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate intracranial development and no structural anomalies at 22 weeks.

Seizure protocol MRI of the brain. High-resolution coronal FLAIR and T2 sequences demonstrate normal, symmetric morphology and signal intensity of both hippocampal formations. No focal cortical dysplasia, vascular malformations, or developmental anomalies are seen.

Impression: Completely normal brain MRI. No mesial temporal sclerosis or other structural epileptogenic foci identified.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation shows excellent development of the fetal brain. Deep, complex tertiary sulcation patterns are visualized across all lobes, reflecting advanced cortical maturation appropriate for late third trimester. The lateral ventricular atria measure 6.4 mm and are symmetric. The corpus callosum and brainstem are fully formed.

Fetal body structures, including the lungs and abdominal organs, are unremarkable. Impression: Normal fetal brain and body development with no structural anomalies.

Fetal MRI performed at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates appropriate brain maturation and normal fetal anatomy. Cortical sulcation and gyration are fully consistent with 34 weeks of development. The ventricular system is normal, with an atrial width of 6.0 mm. Brainstem and cerebellar structures are completely intact. Visualized fetal chest and abdomen reveal no anomalies.

Impression: Unremarkable and completely normal fetal MRI for 34 weeks gestation. Normal ventricular atrial diameter and excellent cortical maturation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates Ebstein's anomaly. There is severe apical displacement of the septal and posterior tricuspid valve leaflets (displacement index of 22 mm/m2). The right atrium and the 'atrialized' portion of the right ventricle are massive, causing significant compression and leftward displacement of the interventricular septum. Severe tricuspid regurgitation is observed on cine sequences.

Impression: Classic Ebstein's anomaly with severe tricuspid regurgitation, massive right atrial/atrialized RV enlargement, and impaired functional right ventricular systolic output (RVEF 35%).

Cardiac MRI evaluates cardiac structure and function. Multiplanar, multisequence images demonstrate normal cardiac segmental anatomy and normal systemic and pulmonary venous connections. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 72 mL/m², and the ejection fraction is normal at 63%. The right ventricular size is within normal pediatric limits with an ejection fraction of 58%. No late gadolinium enhancement is present to suggest focal myocardial fibrosis.

Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI. There is no evidence of structural heart disease, shunts, valvular dysfunction, or myocardial scar.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior body and genu are present, but the posterior body and splenium are absent. There is mild, asymmetric dilation of the posterior horns of the lateral ventricles (colpocephaly), with the left atrium measuring 10.5 mm and the right atrium measuring 9.8 mm. The posterior fossa structures and cerebellum are unremarkable.

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with mild posterior colpocephaly. Recommend postnatal clinical and imaging follow-up.

MRI of the brain demonstrates herniation of the cerebellar tonsils approximately 8 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils appear pointed and peg-like. There is effacement of the CSF spaces at the craniovertebral junction. The ventricular system is normal in size and configuration, and the visualized cervical cord shows no evidence of syrinx formation.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with 8 mm tonsillar herniation. No associated syringomyelia or hydrocephalus seen at this time.

Brain MRI shows multiple discrete T2/FLAIR hyperintense lesions distributed within the periventricular, juxtacortical, and infratentorial white matter. Several lesions are oriented perpendicularly to the lateral ventricles, consistent with Dawson's fingers. Following gadolinium administration, two of the periventricular lesions demonstrate active nodular enhancement.

Impression: Demyelinating disease of the central nervous system with lesions demonstrating spatial and temporal dissemination, highly suggestive of pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis, resulting in a mild keyhole-like communication between the fourth ventricle and the cisterna magna. The posterior fossa is not significantly enlarged, and the tentorium is normally positioned. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits, with the atrial widths measuring 7.1 mm on the left and 7.3 mm on the right. No other intracranial or extracranial anomalies are identified.
