Impression: Normal pediatric brain MRI. No structural or developmental abnormalities are identified to account for the patient's seizure activity.

The study demonstrates features of Chiari II malformation, including small posterior fossa, low-lying torcula, and tonsillar herniation through the foramen magnum. The ventricular system shows moderate ventriculomegaly, stable from previous exams, and the corpus callosum is dysgenetic. A small myelomeningocele repair site is observed in the lumbar spine on sagittal localizers.

Impression: Stable Chiari II malformation. Ventriculomegaly is unchanged from baseline, with no signs of acute decompensation, shunt malfunction, or progressive brainstem compression.

Cardiac MRI shows intact interatrial and interventricular septa with no evidence of intracardiac shunts. Ventricular dimensions and wall thicknesses are within normal limits for patient age and body surface area. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 64% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%. There is no evidence of myocardial edema, perfusion abnormality, or late gadolinium enhancement on tissue characterization sequences.

Impression: Completely normal pediatric cardiac MRI. Unremarkable cardiac anatomy and biventricular systolic function.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 32 weeks gestation reveals significant bilateral ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricular atrium measures 14.5 mm, and the right measures 13.8 mm, indicating moderate-to-severe dilation. There is mild thinning of the posterior corpus callosum secondary to ventricular distension. There is a noticeable delay in the expected tertiary sulcation and operculization patterns for 32 weeks, suggesting cortical developmental delay secondary to ventriculomegaly.

Impression: Moderate bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly with associated cortical sulcation delay. No clear evidence of aqueductal stenosis or neural tube defects visualized. Recommend postnatal neurosurgical follow-up.

Fetal MRI performed at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum, with the posterior body and splenium absent. There is mild colpocephaly with the posterior horn of the right lateral ventricle measuring 11.2 mm and the left measuring 10.8 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 29 weeks, showing normal opercularization and temporal gyrus formation.

The cerebellum and brainstem appear normal. The fetal chest, abdomen, and musculoskeletal systems are intact. Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly, otherwise normal fetal anatomy.

Cardiac MRI shows a structurally normal heart. Left ventricular volumes (LVEDVI 75 mL/m²) and systolic function (LVEF 63%) are within normal limits. Right ventricular volumes (RVEDVI 79 mL/m²) and function (RVEF 59%) are also normal. No valvular stenosis or regurgitation. T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) measurements are within normal physiological ranges without myocardial scarring.

Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No structural, functional, or tissue characterization abnormalities.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a classic cor triatriatum sinister. A fibromuscular diaphragm/membrane is visualized dividing the left atrium into a proximal accessory chamber (receiving the pulmonary veins) and a distal true left atrial chamber (containing the left atrial appendage and communicating with the mitral valve). There is a restrictive fenestration within the membrane causing turbulent flow and mild venous congestion.

Impression: Cor triatriatum sinister with a mildly restrictive intra-atrial membrane. Ventricular dimensions and global systolic function remain normal.

Fetal MRI performed at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates completely normal fetal intracranial anatomy. Cerebral sulcation is early but appropriate for 20 weeks, demonstrating normal opercularization of the sylvian fissure. The lateral ventricular atria are symmetric and measure 5.2 mm. The corpus callosum is visible and intact, and the posterior fossa structures are normal.

The fetal chest, abdomen, spine, and extremities are morphologically normal. Amniotic fluid volume is within normal limits. Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation showing expected structural development for gestational age.

MRI of the infant brain demonstrates normal myelin maturation pattern consistent with a 3-month-old infant. There is no evidence of subdural, epidural, or subarachnoid hemorrhage. No parenchymal restricted diffusion is identified to suggest acute ischemic injury, and the ventricular system and subarachnoid spaces are normal in caliber.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain for age. No intracranial pathology or evidence of acute or chronic trauma.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation reveals a neural tube defect in the lumbar region. There is a localized bony cleft in the posterior arches of L3 through L5, with an overlying skin defect and protrusion of a myelomeningocele sac. The brain demonstrates a Chiari II malformation, characterized by herniation of the cerebellar vermis into the upper cervical canal, a small posterior fossa, and moderate ventriculomegaly with atrial widths of 11.2 mm.

Impression: Lumbar myelomeningocele and Chiari II malformation at 20 weeks gestation. Refer to maternal-fetal medicine and pediatric neurosurgery for prenatal repair counseling.

Brain MRI was obtained utilizing pediatric multiplanar, multisequence protocols. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal signal intensity and gray-white matter differentiation. There is no evidence of acute infarction, hemorrhage, or mass effect. Ventricles, cisterns, and sulci are entirely normal in caliber and configuration for age, without signs of hydrocephalus. The cranial nerves, brainstem, and posterior fossa structures are normal, and myelination is age-appropriate.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural abnormalities, intracranial pathology, or signs of elevated intracranial pressure are identified to account for the patient's presenting symptoms of atypical pediatric headaches.

Fetal MRI at 21 weeks gestation demonstrates complete absence of tissue within both renal fossae. No ectopic renal structures are visualized within the fetal pelvis. There is a profound lack of amniotic fluid (severe oligohydramnios), resulting in crowding of the fetal parts. The fetal urinary bladder is non-visualized, consistent with anuria. The fetal chest shows moderate compression, raising concern for pulmonary hypoplasia.

Impression: Bilateral renal agenesis associated with severe oligohydramnios and early-stage pulmonary hypoplasia. This is a highly critical finding with poor neonatal prognosis.

Brain MRI demonstrates a large, well-circumscribed extra-axial fluid collection in the left middle cranial fossa, measuring 3.6 x 2.4 x 4.0 cm. The fluid completely follows cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) signal characteristics on all sequences, including complete suppression on FLAIR and absence of restricted diffusion on DWI. There is mild remodeling of the adjacent sphenoid wing and squamous temporal bone, and mild mass effect on the left temporal lobe.

Impression: Large Galassi Type II arachnoid cyst in the left temporal fossa. The lesion is stable without acute hemorrhage or significant midline shift.

Cardiac MRI reveals marked dilatation of the left ventricle with severely depressed global systolic function; the calculated left ventricular ejection fraction is 26%. There is mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the mid-to-apical ventricular septum. Moderate secondary mitral regurgitation is present due to mitral valve annular dilation.

Impression: Severe non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with mid-wall septal fibrosis and severe global left ventricular systolic dysfunction.

MR venogram and brain MRI obtained for constant headache evaluation. Findings show flattening of the posterior sclera bilaterally with mild intraocular protrusion of the optic discs, along with distension of the perioptic subarachnoid space. There is also moderate stenosis of both distal transverse dural sinuses. No intracranial masses, extra-axial collections, or acute parenchymal changes are observed.

Impression: Radiographic signs are strongly supportive of idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri), including bilateral optic nerve sheath distension, posterior scleral flattening, and transverse sinus stenosis.

Fetal MRI at 31 weeks gestation reveals multiple fractures and skeletal abnormalities. There are multiple bilateral healing rib fractures, resulting in a mildly narrow chest. The femurs and humeri are shortened, thickened, and demonstrate acute bowing, consistent with multiple intrauterine fractures. Fetal brain imaging demonstrates normal cerebral parenchyma and appropriate sulcation for 31 weeks. The ventricular atria measure 6.4 mm.

Impression: Skeletal abnormalities highly characteristic of Osteogenesis Imperfecta (likely Type II or III) with multiple rib fractures and long bone bowing. Mild thoracic narrowing is present.

Cardiac MRI evaluation for atypical chest tightness during exertion. Cine sequences demonstrate normal ventricular volumes, wall thickness, and contractility. The left ventricular ejection fraction is calculated at 62%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. No regional wall motion abnormalities, myocardial edema, or perfusion defects are noted. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging is entirely negative for fibrosis or scar.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI study. There is no evidence of structural heart disease, cardiomyopathy, or myocardial injury to explain the patient's clinical presentation.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large, hemodynamically significant Patent Ductus Arteriosus (PDA) measuring approximately 4.5 mm at its narrowest point. There is significant left-to-right shunting, resulting in moderate dilation of both the left atrium and the left ventricle. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is elevated at 112 ml/m2. The pulmonary-to-systemic shunt ratio (Qp:Qs) is calculated at 2.1.

Left ventricular systolic function is hyperdynamic with an ejection fraction of 68%. No signs of pulmonary hypertension are evident, and right ventricular size and function remain normal. Impression: Large patent ductus arteriosus with significant left-to-right shunt, resulting in moderate left heart volume overload.

Cardiac MRI reveals a moderately sized, perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 6 mm in diameter. There is a prominent left-to-right shunt visualized on velocity-encoded phase-contrast sequences, with a Qp:Qs ratio estimated at 1.8:1. Significant volume overload of the left atrium and left ventricle is noted, with mild left ventricular dilation (LVEDVI 92 mL/m2).

Impression: Moderate perimembranous ventricular septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt and associated left heart volume overload. Left ventricular systolic function remains preserved (EF 60%).

Cardiac MRI reveals a large perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 8 mm in diameter, with a significant left-to-right shunt. The Qp:Qs ratio is calculated at 2.1:1. There is mild dilation of both the left atrium and left ventricle, reflecting pulmonary overcirculation and volume overload. Right ventricular and pulmonary artery pressures are estimated to be moderately elevated.

Impression: Large perimembranous ventricular septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt and resulting left-sided chamber dilation.

MR examination of the brain was obtained following an episode of transient syncope. The brain parenchyma is structurally normal without signal abnormality, mass lesion, or abnormal enhancement. The ventricular system, extra-axial spaces, and vascular flow voids are well-preserved and appropriate for age.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No acute intracranial process, mass, or demyelinating pathology was found to explain the syncopal episode.

Fetal MRI at 20 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal intracranial structures. The cerebral cortex is smooth, which is expected and appropriate for this early stage of gestation. Symmetrical lateral ventricular atria measure 5.2 mm. The brainstem, cerebellum, and posterior fossa are normal in appearance, with the corpus callosum appropriately visualized on sagittal images.

Fetal chest, abdominal viscera, kidneys, and spine are normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate structural development at 20 weeks.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates severe bilateral renal hydronephrosis. The left renal pelvis measures 18 mm and the right measures 15 mm. There is thinning of the renal cortex bilaterally, more pronounced on the left. Dilated ureters are traced to the level of the bladder, and the fetal urinary bladder is noted to be markedly distended but lacks a keyhole appearance. Normal amniotic fluid volume is present.

Impression: Severe bilateral hydronephrosis and hydroureter, suggestive of bilateral ureterovesical junction obstruction or high-grade vesicoureteral reflux. Cortical thinning is present.

Dedicated sagittal and coronal thin-slice MRI of the sella turcica demonstrates a hypo-enhancing, well-defined lesion in the right lateral wing of the adenohypophysis measuring approximately 4 mm. The lesion causes subtle upward deviation of the pituitary stalk, but the optic chiasm is free and not compressed. The posterior pituitary bright spot is preserved in the sella.

Impression: Small, 4 mm hypo-enhancing lesion in the right adenohypophysis, consistent with a pituitary microadenoma. No evidence of mass effect on the optic chiasm or cavernous sinus invasion.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation reveals normal fetal development. Cerebral sulcation is advanced and completely normal for 34 weeks, with clear primary and secondary sulci. The lateral ventricles are normal in caliber, with the left atrium measuring 6.0 mm and the right measuring 6.2 mm. Brainstem and cerebellar hemisphere morphology are normal.

Fetal viscera, including the heart, lungs, liver, stomach, and kidneys, show normal MRI signal and morphology. No musculoskeletal anomalies are identified. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation, indicating normal anatomical progression.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates normal fetal development. Intracranial anatomy is normal with advanced sulcation and gyration patterns, including secondary and tertiary sulci appropriate for 36 weeks. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with the atria measuring 6.2 mm. The corpus callosum is fully formed and normal.

All extracranial organs, including lungs, bowel, liver, and kidneys, demonstrate normal development and signal characteristics. Impression: Unremarkable late-third-trimester fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation with normal development and no detectable anomalies.

MR imaging of the brain demonstrates a solid, lobulated mass filling the fourth ventricle, measuring 3.5 x 3.2 x 3.0 cm. The lesion shows marked diffusion restriction on DWI sequences and heterogeneous enhancement following contrast administration. Severe compression of the brainstem and cerebellar vermis is noted, leading to moderate obstructive supratentorial hydrocephalus with transependymal CSF migration.

Impression: Posterior fossa fourth ventricular mass showing features highly consistent with a medulloblastoma. Urgent neurosurgical intervention and staging cerebrospinal fluid analysis are indicated.

Fetal MR evaluation at 30 weeks gestation shows completely normal fetal development. Cortical folding, opercularization of the Sylvian fissures, and the primary and secondary sulcation patterns are entirely normal for 30 weeks. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, with the atrial diameter measuring 6.1 mm. The corpus callosum is well-visualized, and the cerebellum and brainstem appear normal.

All fetal viscera, the spine, and extremities are normal. Amniotic fluid volume is appropriate. Impression: Unremarkable fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation with no structural abnormalities and appropriate CNS development.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates a large defect in the central portion of the interatrial septum, consistent with a secundum-type atrial septal defect, measuring approximately 16 mm. A significant left-to-right shunt is present with a calculated Qp:Qs flow ratio of 1.8:1. This has resulted in moderate dilation of the right atrium and the right ventricle, with a right ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m2. Right ventricular systolic function is preserved with an ejection fraction of 56%.

Impression: Large secundum atrial septal defect with a hemodynamically significant left-to-right shunt, causing moderate right heart enlargement. Left-sided chambers are normal in size and function.

Fetal MRI at 27 weeks gestation demonstrates symmetrical ventricular atria measuring 5.9 mm. Cortical ribbon shows normal infolding and sulcation appropriate for 27 weeks gestation. The corpus callosum is intact and normal in configuration. The posterior fossa structures are well-developed.

Thorax, spine, and abdominal organs are unremarkable. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing completely healthy development.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 13-year-old male with D-transposition of the great arteries (D-TGA) status post neonatal arterial switch operation. Multiphase imaging shows normal origin and course of the surgically translocated coronary arteries. The systemic (left) ventricle is normal in size and function (LVEF 59%). There is mild narrowing at the site of the pulmonary anastomosis (supravalvular pulmonary stenosis) resulting in a localized velocity of 2.8 m/s, but without severe right ventricular pressure overload (RVEF is 51%). No late gadolinium enhancement is identified within either ventricle.

Impression: Post-arterial switch D-TGA with normal systemic LV function. Mild residual supravalvular pulmonary stenosis is noted without severe right ventricular compromise.

Brain MRI of this 3-month-old infant demonstrates a severely enlarged posterior fossa with a cystic malformation communicating with the fourth ventricle. There is severe hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis, which is rotated superiorly. The lateral and third ventricles are moderately dilated, consistent with ventriculomegaly. The corpus callosum is intact.

Impression: Classic Dandy-Walker malformation. Associated ventriculomegaly is present and requires clinical monitoring for intracranial pressure signs.

This examination evaluates a 6-year-old boy post-arterial switch operation for d-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA). The reconstructed vessels demonstrate mild, stable narrowing at the supravalvular pulmonary anastomosis with a peak velocity of 2.1 m/s, indicating mild stenosis. The neo-aortic root and ascending aorta show mild dilation but no signs of significant regurgitation. Biventricular volumes and systolic function are preserved (LV EF 58%, RV EF 54%).

Impression: Status post-arterial switch operation for d-TGA. Mild, hemodynamically stable supravalvular pulmonary stenosis with preserved biventricular size and function.

Magnetic resonance angiography and cardiac cine sequences reveal a discrete coarctation of the aorta located just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery. The narrowest segment measures 3.2 mm in diameter, with a significant post-stenotic dilation of the descending thoracic aorta. Mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is noted, with an indexed LV mass of 85 g/m² and preserved ejection fraction (63%).

Impression: Severe discrete aortic coarctation distal to the left subclavian artery with mild concentric left ventricular hypertrophy. Surgical or transcatheter intervention is indicated.

Fetal MRI at 33 weeks gestation demonstrates mild, asymmetric ventriculomegaly. The left lateral ventricle atrium is dilated, measuring 11.2 mm, while the right lateral ventricle atrium measures 7.1 mm. The cortical migration and sulcation pattern is appropriate for 33 weeks. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal in morphology and signal intensity. No extra-axial fluid collections are identified.

Impression: Mild, isolated, asymmetric left-sided fetal ventriculomegaly at 33 weeks gestation. No other structural central nervous system abnormalities are detected.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals severe micromelia involving all extremities, highly suggestive of skeletal dysplasia. The long bones are significantly shortened, thickened, and abnormally bowed. The thorax is narrow and bell-shaped with ribs that appear shortened, resulting in moderate pulmonary compression. The fetal skull is mildly enlarged with a prominent forehead. Fetal brain tissue displays appropriate sulcation for 26 weeks, and ventricular caliber is normal (atrial width 6.0 mm).

Impression: Skeletal dysplasia characterized by severe micromelia, narrow thorax, and long bone bowing. Thanatophoric dysplasia or severe Osteogenesis Imperfecta are high on the differential.

Brain MRI demonstrates a lobulated, cystic and solid suprasellar mass measuring 2.5 x 2.2 cm, demonstrating heterogeneous enhancement of its solid portions. The mass elevates the optic chiasm and compresses the infundibulum. Focal calcifications within the wall of the lesion are suspected on susceptibility-weighted imaging.

Impression: Suprasellar mixed cystic and solid mass compressing the optic chiasm, most consistent with a craniopharyngioma. Pediatric endocrinology and neurosurgery referrals are recommended.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates partial agenesis of the corpus callosum. The anterior genu and body of the corpus callosum are present, but the posterior body and splenium are absent. There is mild colpocephaly with dilation of the occipital horns of the lateral ventricles, where the atrium measures 10.8 mm. The cerebral sulcation and gyration are normal for 29 weeks.

Impression: Partial agenesis of the corpus callosum with associated mild colpocephaly. No other intracranial abnormalities detected.

ECG-gated multiplanar cardiac MRI shows normal cardiac situs. The systemic and pulmonary venous connections are normal. Left ventricular end-diastolic volume is 85 mL, with an ejection fraction of 61%. Right ventricular end-diastolic volume is 88 mL, with an ejection fraction of 57%. There are no septal defects or abnormal shunts. The myocardium shows normal signal intensity without evidence of edema or late gadolinium enhancement.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with normal chamber sizes, preserved biventricular systolic function, and no structural anomalies.

Brain MRI shows a complex, cystic and solid sellar/suprasellar mass measuring 3.5 x 2.9 x 3.1 cm. The lesion contains hyperintense fluid on T1-weighted images (suggestive of high protein/cholesterol content) and demonstrating calcification on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI). The solid component enhances intensely and heterogeneously following contrast. The optic chiasm is severely compressed and displaced superiorly. The third ventricle is compressed, causing mild upstream ventriculomegaly.

Impression: Sellar and suprasellar mass with characteristic imaging features of a pediatric craniopharyngioma. Significant compression of the optic chiasm.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation shows features consistent with a skeletal dysplasia, likely thanatophoric dysplasia. There is marked shortening of all long bones, with curved femurs (telephone receiver shape). The thoracic cavity is narrow and severely hypoplastic, with platyspondyly present throughout the spine. 

The brain shows normal temporal lobe gyration for 25 weeks, and the ventricular atrium measures 7.0 mm. No intracranial masses are identified. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia with marked narrow chest and rhizomelic limb shortening, characteristic of thanatophoric dysplasia. Pediatric genetics consultation is recommended.

Brain MRI demonstrates normal intracranial architecture. There is no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial pathology, mass lesion, or abnormal enhancement. The ventricles and cortical sulci are unremarkable. Evaluation of the skull and superficial tissues shows a small subcutaneous fluid-containing cyst of the posterior scalp without any intracranial communication.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. Benign subcutaneous scalp cyst without intracranial extension.

MRI of the brain demonstrates cerebellar tonsils herniating 7 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. There is crowding of the craniovertebral junction with effacement of the surrounding CSF spaces. A small, non-expanding syrinx is noted in the visualized upper cervical spine. No ventriculomegaly or supratentorial mass is visualized.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with associated small cervical syrinx. Correlation with patient symptomatology (e.g., occipital headaches) is recommended.

Cardiac MRI performed for evaluation of atypical chest pain and an ambiguous cardiac murmur. All cardiac chambers display normal internal dimensions, volume indexes, and wall thicknesses for age. Great vessel anatomy is unremarkable with normal relationships and flow dynamics. No myocardial perfusion abnormalities or myocardial scarring/late enhancement is identified.

Impression: Structurally and functionally normal cardiac MRI. There is no evidence of cardiomyopathy, congenital shunt, or valvular disease. LVEF is 62%.

Multiplanar, multisequence MR imaging of the brain was obtained following a history of sports-related concussion. There is no evidence of intra-axial or extra-axial hemorrhage, mass effect, or midline shift. Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) demonstrates no signal dropout to suggest microhemorrhages or diffuse axonal injury. The cerebral cortex, white matter, and deep grey structures are unremarkable, and ventricles are normal in caliber.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No objective evidence of traumatic brain injury, acute hemorrhage, or microbleeding to correlate with the patient's post-concussive symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation demonstrates an open neural tube defect in the lumbosacral region extending from L4 to S2, with exposure of the placode. Associated findings include a Chiari II malformation characterized by herniation of the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum and a small posterior fossa. Supratentorial ventriculomegaly is present, with the right atrium measuring 14.2 mm and the left measuring 13.9 mm.

Impression: Lumbosacral myelomeningocele with associated Chiari II malformation and ventriculomegaly at 28 weeks gestation.

Evaluation of a 17-year-old female athlete with abnormal electrocardiogram findings and syncope. There is marked, asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the maximal diastolic interventricular septal thickness measuring 22 mm. Systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior leaflet of the mitral valve is demonstrated, causing dynamic left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction with a calculated peak systolic gradient of 45 mmHg. The left ventricular cavity is small, and systolic function is hyperdynamic with an ejection fraction of 75%.

Mitral regurgitation is moderate, directed posteriorly. Late gadolinium enhancement imaging reveals patchy hyperenhancement at the RV-LV insertion points and within the hypertrophied anterior septum. Impression: Phenotypic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with dynamic LVOT obstruction, moderate mitral regurgitation, and focal myocardial fibrosis.

Cardiac MRI was performed to evaluate acute onset of chest pain and elevated troponins following a viral syndrome. T2-weighted and T2-mapping sequences demonstrate focal areas of myocardial edema within the epicardial and mid-myocardial regions of the lateral and inferior left ventricular walls. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging shows matching subepicardial and mid-wall hyperenhancement, which is non-ischemic in distribution.

Impression: Multi-segmental subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement and matching edema, meeting the updated Lake Louise Criteria for acute myocarditis. Left ventricular ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 49%.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates significant enlargement of the fetal urinary bladder with a dilated proximal urethra, demonstrating the classic keyhole sign. Bilateral hydroureteronephrosis is present, with pelvic dilatation measuring 14 mm on the right and 16 mm on the left, associated with cortical thinning. Oligohydramnios is noted. Fetal lung volumes are mildly decreased.

Impression: Posterior urethral valves (PUV) with severe megacystis, bilateral hydroureteronephrosis, and oligohydramnios at 29 weeks gestation.

Fetal brain MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals classic findings of a Dandy-Walker malformation. There is severe hypoplasia and upward rotation of the cerebellar vermis, accompanied by cystic dilation of the posterior fossa that communicates directly with the fourth ventricle. Elevated tentorium cerebelli and torcular inversion are noted. The bilateral lateral ventricles are mildly dilated, measuring 9.5 mm at the atria. Cortical sulcation is minimal, which is age-appropriate for 26 weeks.

Impression: Fetal Dandy-Walker malformation at 26 weeks gestation with vermian hypoplasia, enlarged posterior fossa, and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly.

Diffusion-weighted imaging reveals a wedge-shaped area of restricted diffusion with matching hypointensity on ADC mapping in the territory of the left middle cerebral artery (MCA), specifically the cortical branch. This is accompanied by local sulcal effacement and mild edema in the left frontoparietal cortex. Magnetic resonance angiography shows decreased flow in the corresponding M2 segment.

Impression: Acute ischemic cortical stroke in the left middle cerebral artery territory. Prompt pediatric stroke workup is advised to evaluate for hypercoagulable states or vascular dissection.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates a large, simple cyst in the left choroid plexus measuring 8.5 mm. There is associated mild ventriculomegaly of the left lateral ventricle, with an atrial measurement of 10.5 mm. The right lateral ventricle atrium is normal at 6.8 mm. The remaining brain parenchyma shows normal migration and sulcation patterns for 23 weeks. The fetal spine is intact, and no other structural anomalies are seen.

Impression: Left choroid plexus cyst with associated mild left-sided ventriculomegaly. Given the isolation of the finding, close monitoring is recommended to evaluate for resolution.

Multiplanar, multisequence MRI of the brain was performed. The brain parenchyma is normal in signal intensity across all sequences. There is no evidence of intracranial mass, acute hemorrhage, or ischemia. The ventricles and extra-axial fluid spaces are normal in caliber and configuration for age. Visualized orbits and sinus cavities are clear.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain. No structural, neoplastic, or vascular abnormalities are identified to explain the episodes of dizziness or syncope.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation reveals findings highly suggestive of skeletal dysplasia. There is severe, symmetric shortening of all long bones, along with platyspondyly and a narrow, bell-shaped thorax. The fetal skull is prominent with temporal bossing, though no classic trilobed (cloverleaf) deformity is fully expressed. Fetal lungs are severely hypoplastic due to thoracic constriction.

Intracranial anatomy shows normal sulcation for 25 weeks, with an atrial width of 7.2 mm. Impression: Severe skeletal dysplasia (such as Thanatophoric Dysplasia) with secondary thoracic constriction and lung hypoplasia.

Cardiac MRI is performed on an adolescent female presenting with acute chest pain and elevated troponins following a viral prodrome. Multiplanar T2-weighted triple IR imaging demonstrates patchy, focal areas of high signal intensity in the mid-myocardial and subepicardial regions of the lateral and inferolateral left ventricular free wall, indicative of myocardial edema. Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging confirms non-ischemic, subepicardial and mid-wall enhancement in these same regions, sparing the subendocardium.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of acute myocarditis based on the Lake Louise criteria. There is mild global hypokinesis of the left ventricle with a depressed ejection fraction of 47%. No pericardial effusion is visualized.

High-resolution epilepsy protocol MRI demonstrates focal thickening of the cortex in the posterior aspect of the right frontal lobe. There is mild blurring of the gray-white matter junction, and a linear band of T2/FLAIR hyperintensity extending from the dysplastic cortex to the lateral ventricle is visualized (transmantle sign).

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia of the right frontal lobe. This represents a highly probable epileptogenic focus.

MR study of the brain was acquired without and with intravenous gadolinium contrast. The cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres demonstrate normal morphology, sulcation, and myelination patterns for a 12-year-old child. There is no evidence of intracranial mass lesion, acute infarct, or hemorrhage. Ventricles and extra-axial CSF spaces are within normal limits for age, and the major intracranial arterial flow voids are intact.

Impression: Normal MRI of the brain. No structural brain abnormalities or enhancement patterns to account for pediatric headache symptoms.

This study was performed to evaluate a young competitive athlete with frequent, complex premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) on Holter monitoring. Quantitative assessment of the right and left ventricles shows normal chamber volumes, myocardial mass, and global systolic function (LVEF 63%, RVEF 57%). No late gadolinium enhancement is observed, and there are no regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of focal fatty replacement in the RV free wall.

Impression: Normal cardiac MRI with no identifiable structural, tissue, or functional substrates for ventricular ectopy. The heart is anatomically unremarkable.

MRI of the brain demonstrates completely normal gray and white matter signal. Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) shows no evidence of microhemorrhages, diffuse axonal injury, or hemosiderin deposition. The ventricles, cisterns, and major vascular flow voids are intact, with no signs of structural damage or tissue volume loss.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No evidence of traumatic brain injury, diffuse axonal injury, or other focal intracranial abnormalities to explain post-concussive symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation demonstrates an open neural tube defect in the lumbar spine. There is a defect in the posterior elements of the L4-S2 vertebrae with herniation of meninges and neural elements. Intracranial evaluation shows classic signs of an Arnold-Chiari II malformation, including effacement of the cisterna magna, cerebellar herniation (banana sign), and bifrontal narrowing (lemon sign). Moderate bilateral ventriculomegaly is noted with atrial widths measuring 12.0 mm.

Impression: L4-S2 open myelomeningocele with Chiari II malformation. Fetal surgery evaluation is recommended.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates apical displacement of the septal and posterior leaflets of the tricuspid valve, measuring 25 mm from the mitral valve annulus. This results in significant atrialization of the right ventricle. The functional right ventricle is small, and there is severe tricuspid regurgitation. The right atrium is massively dilated. Left ventricular volume is compressed by the shifted interventricular septum but maintains an EF of 55%.

Impression: Ebstein's anomaly of the tricuspid valve with severe tricuspid regurgitation and massive right atrial dilation.

Fetal MRI at 25 weeks gestation shows normal intracranial and extracranial structures. The ventricular atrium on the left measures 6.0 mm and on the right measures 6.2 mm, indicating normal fluid volume. The cerebral cortical ribbon shows symmetrical development with early-stage sulcation appropriate for 25 weeks.

The posterior fossa, brainstem, spinal cord, and chest cavities are clear of any mass or malformation. Impression: Completely normal 25-week fetal MRI, with excellent anatomical progression.

Fetal MRI at 29 weeks gestation demonstrates mild symmetric ventriculomegaly. The lateral ventricular atria measure 11.5 mm on the left and 11.8 mm on the right. There is also a mild enlargement of the extra-axial fluid spaces, but the cortex is well-developed with normal sulcation appropriate for 29 weeks. The corpus callosum and posterior fossa structures are normal.

No other structural abnormalities are detected within the chest, abdomen, or spine. Impression: Mild, isolated bilateral ventriculomegaly. Recommend serial ultrasound or follow-up MRI to monitor progression.

MR imaging of the brain was performed following complaints of persistent dizziness and migraine headaches. The cerebral hemispheres demonstrate normal signal intensity and morphology. There are no extra-axial fluid collections, areas of restricted diffusion, or abnormal enhancement. The paranasal sinuses are clear.

Impression: Unremarkable MRI of the brain with no structural or vascular abnormality to explain the patient's symptoms of dizziness and migraine.

Cardiac MRI of a 19-year-old athlete demonstrates entirely normal cardiac chamber sizes and geometry. The left ventricular mass index is 70 g/m², which is within the normal limits for a trained individual. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 61% and right ventricular ejection fraction is 59%. There are no regional wall motion abnormalities, and myocardial tagging sequences show normal myocardial strain and compliance.

Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) imaging is completely negative for focal enhancement, replacement fibrosis, or subepicardial scarring. Great vessels are normal in course and caliber, and the cardiac valves are fully competent. Impression: Unremarkable cardiac MRI. No findings of cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, or underlying structural heart disease.

Brain MRI obtained without intravenous contrast. There are no extra-axial fluid collections or intracranial masses identified. Brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity and morphology. Deep gray nuclei are intact, and brainstem structures are unremarkable. Arterial flow voids at the base of the skull are well-preserved.

Impression: Normal MR of the brain. No structural or vascular abnormality identified to account for adolescent headache symptoms.

Fetal MRI at 23 weeks gestation demonstrates features consistent with skeletal dysplasia. There is severe shortening and bowing of all long bones, particularly the humeri and femora. The thorax is significantly narrowed in the anteroposterior dimension, with a characteristic bell-shaped thoracic cavity. Intracranial structures are unremarkable, and brain sulcation is appropriate for 23 weeks.

No spinal anomalies are visualized, but there is mild polyhydramnios. Impression: Skeletal dysplasia, with features suspicious for thanatophoric dysplasia given the micromelia and narrow, bell-shaped thorax.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals a large right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The herniated organs include the entire right lobe of the liver and multiple small bowel loops, causing severe leftward mediastinal shift and compression of the left lung. The fetal brain appears normal, with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 6.2 mm at the atria. Sulcation patterns are appropriate for 26 weeks gestation, displaying early parieto-occipital and cingulate fissures.

Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia with liver herniation, severe mediastinal shift, and secondary pulmonary compression at 26 weeks gestation.

Brain MRI reveals a well-defined, solid mass in the pineal region measuring 2.4 x 2.1 x 1.9 cm. The mass is isointense to gray matter on T1 and T2, and demonstrates intense, homogeneous enhancement following contrast administration. It exerts mass effect on the tectal plate, compressing the aqueduct of Sylvius and resulting in moderate enlargement of the lateral and third ventricles.

Impression: Pineal region mass with obstructive hydrocephalus. Features are highly suggestive of a germinoma. Recommend neurosurgical and oncological evaluation.

Brain MRI demonstrates focal cortical thickening and blurring of the gray-white matter junction in the posterior superior aspect of the left frontal lobe. Dedicated 3D FLAIR imaging reveals a hyperintense signal extending from the abnormal cortex towards the lateral ventricle, representing a 'transmantle sign'. No extra-axial collection or midline shift is noted.

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) Type II in the left frontal lobe. This represents a highly epileptogenic structural lesion consistent with the clinical history of refractory focal seizures.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates marked spherical dilation of the left ventricle, with an end-diastolic volume index of 145 mL/m2. Global left ventricular systolic function is severely depressed, with an ejection fraction calculated at 28%. There is diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricular free wall. Left atrial dilation is also noted. Right ventricular size is mildly increased, with a borderline low ejection fraction of 45%. No late gadolinium enhancement is observed, indicating no focal myocardial scar.

Impression: Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe left ventricular enlargement and systolic dysfunction. No focal late gadolinium enhancement is present, which is typical of non-ischemic pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates normal development of the central nervous system. The cortical sulcation pattern is well-developed, with clearly defined parieto-occipital and calcarine sulci appropriate for 30 weeks. The lateral ventricles are within normal limits; the left atrium measures 6.0 mm and the right atrium measures 5.8 mm. The corpus callosum is well-visualized and anatomically intact. Visualized fetal chest, abdomen, and limbs are unremarkable.

Impression: Normal fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation. Brain development, ventricles, and sulcation are appropriate for age.

Postoperative evaluation following an arterial switch procedure for d-transposition of the great arteries (d-TGA). The neo-aorta arises from the left ventricle and the neo-pulmonary artery arises from the right ventricle, showing successful anatomic correction. The branching of the pulmonary arteries is intact with mild narrowing at the surgical anastomosis site of the left pulmonary artery (peak velocity 1.8 m/s). Biventricular systolic function is normal (LVEF 58%, RVEF 50%) without regional wall motion abnormalities.

Impression: Patent postoperative reconstruction following arterial switch for d-TGA. Mild, non-obstructive narrowing of the left pulmonary artery anastomosis, with preserved biventricular function.

Neonatal brain MRI demonstrates structural development within normal physiological limits for a 2-month-old infant. Myelination is appropriately localized to the posterior limb of the internal capsule and brainstem. Ventricles are symmetric and normal in caliber, and the subarachnoid spaces are within normal limits.

Impression: Normal neonatal brain MRI. No evidence of hypoxic-ischemic injury, structural malformation, or hemorrhage.

Cardiac MRI shows asymmetric septal hypertrophy, with the interventricular septum measuring up to 21 mm in end-diastole, causing dynamic obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract during systole. Systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the anterior mitral valve leaflet is observed, leading to a moderate, eccentric jet of mitral regurgitation. Foci of patchy, mid-wall late gadolinium enhancement are present within the hypertrophied segments.

Impression: Severe hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) with prominent SAM and associated myocardial fibrosis/scarring. The left ventricular ejection fraction is hyperdynamic at 72%.

Fetal MRI at 34 weeks gestation demonstrates unremarkable intracranial and extracranial anatomy. The cerebral cortex shows a highly developed and age-appropriate sulcation pattern, including deep central and parieto-occipital sulci. The lateral ventricles are completely symmetric, with atrial measurements of 6.1 mm. The brainstem, vermis, and cerebellar hemispheres are entirely normal in morphology and size.

The fetal chest, heart, diaphragm, liver, and kidneys are within normal limits. Normal volume of amniotic fluid is present. Impression: Normal, unremarkable fetal MRI study demonstrating appropriate structural development at 34 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI evaluates a 15-year-old male presenting with hypertension and lower extremity claudication. There is a discrete, focal narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta immediately distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, consistent with aortic coarctation. The luminal diameter at the narrowest segment measures 6.5 mm. Prominent collateral vessels, including dilated internal mammary and intercostal arteries, are visualized bilaterally bypassing the obstruction. Left ventricular mass is mildly elevated at 85 g/m², indicating early concentric hypertrophy.

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the descending thoracic aorta with significant collateralization. Left ventricular systolic function remains preserved with an ejection fraction of 64% and no evidence of myocardial scar or fibrosis on late gadolinium enhancement imaging.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal biventricular size and function. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 75 mL/m² with an ejection fraction of 62%. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 70 mL/m² with an ejection fraction of 57%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of late gadolinium enhancement are present to suggest pathology. The visualized great vessels are normal in caliber.

Impression: Unremarkable pediatric cardiac MRI. No congenital anomalies or acquired structural, functional, or tissue abnormalities are identified.

MRI brain reveals a focal region of abnormal cortical thickening and blurring of the gray-white matter junction within the right superior frontal gyrus. High-resolution T2 and FLAIR sequences demonstrate a subtle hyperintense signal extending from the abnormal cortex toward the ventricle (transmantle sign). No mass effect or abnormal contrast enhancement is observed.

Impression: Focal cortical dysplasia within the right superior frontal gyrus, providing a highly probable structural correlate for the patient's refractory epilepsy.

Cardiac MRI demonstrates normal cardiac structures with no congenital defects. The left and right ventricles are normal in size, mass, and configuration. Biventricular systolic function is normal, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 64% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 58%. The systemic and pulmonary arteries are normal in size and course.

No myocardial edema, perfusion defects, or late gadolinium enhancement are visualized. Impression: Normal pediatric cardiac MRI. No diagnostic features of cardiomyopathy, valvular disease, or congenital anomaly.

High-resolution MRI of the brain reveals focal thickening of the cortex in the left frontal lobe along the superior frontal gyrus. There is blurring of the gray-white matter junction on T1-weighted images and a hyperintense transmantle sign extending from the ventricle to the cortex on FLAIR images. No other structural anomalies or extra-axial fluid collections are noted.

Impression: Focal cortical thickening and signal abnormality in the left frontal lobe, highly consistent with focal cortical dysplasia (FCD), representing a potential epileptogenic focus.

MR of the brain reveals normal brain parenchyma with preserved gray-white matter differentiation. No intracranial mass, abnormal signal enhancement, restricted diffusion, or extra-axial fluid collections are detected. The cranial nerves and vascular flow voids of the circle of Willis are normal in appearance. Paranasal sinuses are clear.

Impression: Normal MR study of the brain. No structural, vascular, or acute ischemic cause for the patient's syncopal episodes is identified.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the heart demonstrates normal biventricular size, morphology, and systolic function. The left ventricular ejection fraction is 63%, and the right ventricular ejection fraction is 58%. No regional wall motion abnormalities or areas of ventricular dyskinesia are observed. The cardiac valves appear structurally normal with no evidence of stenosis or regurgitation.

No late gadolinium enhancement is present. Impression: Entirely normal cardiac MRI study, with no evidence of structural heart disease, cardiomyopathy, or focal scar.

Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrates a distinct discrete narrowing of the proximal descending thoracic aorta just distal to the origin of the left subclavian artery, characteristic of aortic coarctation. There is a prominent high-velocity jet across the stenotic region on phase-contrast sequences, with moderate collateral vascular flow through dilated intercostal arteries. The left ventricle shows mild concentric hypertrophy with preserved systolic function.

Impression: Severe focal coarctation of the aorta with associated collateral circulation and compensatory left ventricular concentric hypertrophy. No evidence of discrete left ventricular dysfunction; ejection fraction is calculated at 60%.

Multiplanar MR of the heart demonstrates patchy mid-wall to subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) involving the lateral and inferolateral walls of the left ventricle. T2-weighted imaging and T2 mapping show increased signal intensity in these same regions, consistent with localized myocardial edema. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume is at the upper limit of normal, and the ejection fraction is mildly reduced at 51%.

Impression: Dynamic MRI findings are highly characteristic of acute myocarditis. There is associated mild left ventricular systolic dysfunction without macroscopic evidence of myocardial necrosis or pericardial effusion.

Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain was performed following a recent concussion. Brain parenchyma demonstrates normal signal intensity and morphology. No acute intracranial hemorrhage, microhemorrhages, or focal areas of restricted diffusion are seen. The ventricular system, cisterns, and major vascular flow voids are completely unremarkable.

Impression: Normal brain MRI. No structural evidence of acute traumatic brain injury, parenchymal contusion, or diffuse axonal injury.

Cardiac MRI reveals a moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion measuring up to 16 mm in posterior and lateral aspects. There is diffuse thickening and hyperenhancement of the pericardial layers on late gadolinium enhancement imaging, indicating active pericardial inflammation. No diastolic collapse of the right atrium or right ventricle is noted to suggest tamponade physiology on current sequences. Biventricular size and function are preserved.

Impression: Moderate-to-large circumferential pericardial effusion with active pericarditis, showing pericardial thickening and enhancement. No current signs of cardiac tamponade.

Brain MRI and MR venography (MRV) demonstrate a lack of normal flow void in the superior sagittal sinus and the left transverse sinus. T2-weighted and FLAIR imaging show high signal intensity in these venous structures, confirming acute dural venous sinus thrombosis. Associated mild congestion is seen in the left temporoparietal cortex without definite parenchymal hemorrhage.

Impression: Extensive dural venous sinus thrombosis involving the superior sagittal sinus and left transverse sinus. No secondary hemorrhagic venous infarction is observed.

MR angiography of the brain reveals bilateral severe narrowing of the supraclinoid internal carotid arteries, with occlusion of the proximal middle cerebral and anterior cerebral arteries. There is a dense network of collateral vessels in the basal ganglia region bilaterally, giving the characteristic 'puff of smoke' appearance.

Impression: Classic vascular findings of Moyamoya disease. Visualized brain parenchyma shows no evidence of acute or chronic ischemic stroke.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a lumbar myelomeningocele. There is herniation of the neural placode and CSF-filled meninges through a posterior defect in the lower lumbar vertebrae. Associated Chiari II malformation is present, marked by a downward herniation of the cerebellar vermis, a banana-shaped cerebellum, and mild bilateral ventriculomegaly with the atrium measuring 13.5 mm. Sulcation pattern is normal for 26 weeks.

Impression: Open lumbar myelomeningocele with secondary Chiari II malformation and moderate ventriculomegaly.

Cardiac MRI shows global left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an EF of 48%. T2-weighted and T2 mapping sequences demonstrate diffuse, elevated signal intensity and T2 relaxation times in the subepicardial regions of the basal-to-mid lateral and inferior walls. Contrast-enhanced imaging demonstrates prominent subepicardial and mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) in these same distributions.

Impression: Findings are highly characteristic of acute myocarditis meeting the revised Lake Louise criteria. No gross pericardial effusion or ventricular thrombi are identified.

Fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation demonstrates a term-like appearance of the brain. There is highly advanced, age-appropriate sulcation and gyration, with deep sulci across all cerebral lobes. The ventricular system is normal, with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 6.5 mm. The cerebellar vermis, brainstem, and posterior fossa are unremarkable. Fully normal fetal thorax and abdominal organs are confirmed.

Impression: Completely normal late-third-trimester fetal MRI at 36 weeks gestation. No structural anomalies or maturation delays identified.

Unremarkable pediatric cardiac MRI. The systemic and pulmonary venous connections are normal. Atrial and ventricular septa are intact without evidence of defect. The left ventricular end-diastolic volume index is 68 ml/m² with a normal ejection fraction of 64%. The right ventricular ejection fraction is 60%.

No abnormal myocardial hyperenhancement is present on post-contrast imaging. The coronary artery origins are visualized and appear normal. Impression: Structurally and functionally normal cardiac MRI, showing no evidence of congenital cardiac defect or cardiomyopathy.

Fetal MRI at 30 weeks gestation demonstrates age-appropriate fetal brain maturation. Normal progression of sulcation is observed, with visible central, parieto-occipital, and cingulate sulci. The lateral ventricles are completely normal in size, with atrial measurements of 5.7 mm. Midline structures and the posterior fossa are normal.

Fetal chest, abdominal viscera, kidneys, and extremities are well-formed. Normal amniotic fluid is present. Impression: Normal 30-week gestational age fetal MRI with no central nervous system or visceral abnormalities.

Fetal MRI at 28 weeks gestation indicates normal growth and development. The cerebral cortex shows appropriate progression of sulcation and opercularization for a 28-week fetus, with clearly demarcated sylvian fissures. The ventricles are symmetric with an atrial measurement of 6.8 mm on the left and 6.5 mm on the right. The cavum septum pellucidum, corpus callosum, and brainstem are completely intact and morphologically normal.

The fetal chest, cardiac axis, abdominal viscera, and extremities are normal. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study showing age-appropriate brain development and normal anatomy.

Cardiac MRI shows normal heart anatomy with intact interatrial and interventricular septa. Left and right ventricular chamber sizes, wall thickness, and mass indices are normal. Biventricular systolic function is preserved, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 65% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 60%. Myocardial tissue characterization is unremarkable.

No late gadolinium enhancement is noted. Cardiac valves are thin, mobile, and normal in function. Impression: Structurally and functionally normal cardiac MRI.

Fetal MRI evaluated at 32 weeks gestation shows robust cerebral development. The major sulci, including the central, precentral, and postcentral sulci, are well-formed and demonstrate expected depth and operculization for 32 weeks. The ventricular system is normal in caliber, with the bilateral atrial widths measuring 5.8 mm. The brainstem, corpus callosum, and cerebellar vermis show normal, age-appropriate morphology.

No thoracic, abdominal, or spinal abnormalities are visualized. Amniotic fluid volume is normal. Impression: Normal fetal MRI study demonstrating appropriate brain maturation and structural integrity for 32 weeks gestation.

Cardiac MRI study displays completely normal cardiac chambers, structure, and pulmonary and systemic venous connections. The ventricular myocardium shows normal thickness and normal contractility. Left ventricular ejection fraction is 65%, and right ventricular ejection fraction is 61%. No late gadolinium enhancement is present. Flow curves within the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk are normal.

Impression: Completely normal cardiac MRI study. No congenital shunts, cardiomyopathy, or evidence of myocarditis identified.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation demonstrates a right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH). The defect in the right diaphragm has allowed herniation of the right hepatic lobe and gallbladder into the right thoracic cavity, resulting in significant leftward mediastinal shift and compression of both the left and right lungs.

The fetal brain displays a normal appearance for 26 weeks, with symmetric lateral ventricles measuring 6.2 mm at the atria. Sulcation pattern is appropriate, and no intracranial anomalies are identified. Impression: Right-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia containing the liver and gallbladder, with secondary mediastinal shift. Normal brain development.

Cardiac MRI evaluates congenital aortic stenosis. There is a bicuspid aortic valve with a fusion pattern of the right and left coronary cusps, showing restricted leaflet excursion during systole. Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy is present with a maximum diastolic wall thickness of 13 mm and an indexed LV mass of 94 g/m2. No areas of focal late gadolinium enhancement are visualized.

Impression: Severe congenital aortic stenosis of a bicuspid aortic valve with secondary left ventricular hypertrophy. Left ventricular systolic function remains well-preserved with an ejection fraction of 60%.

Cardiac MRI shows a large perimembranous ventricular septal defect (VSD) measuring approximately 9 mm in diameter. Cine imaging reveals a substantial left-to-right shunt. The left atrium and left ventricle are moderately dilated, indicative of volume overload (left ventricular end-diastolic volume index of 115 mL/m²). The biventricular systolic function is preserved, with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 63% and a right ventricular ejection fraction of 56%.

Impression: Large perimembranous ventricular septal defect with significant left-to-right shunt and resulting left heart volume overload. Recommend clinical correlation and evaluation for surgical closure.

Cardiac MRI shows regional wall motion abnormalities of the right ventricle, specifically microaneurysms and dyskinesis within the RV outflow tract and apex. The right ventricular end-diastolic volume is dilated at 115 ml/m², and the RVEF is reduced at 34%. Late gadolinium enhancement demonstrates transmural fibrosis of the right ventricular free wall, with minor involvement of the left ventricular lateral wall.

Impression: Features are highly suggestive of Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy (ARVC) with significant RV dilation, dyskinesis, and fibrofatty replacement. Recommend clinical integration with electrophysiology studies.

Fetal MRI at 22 weeks gestation reveals a defect in the squamous occipital bone. There is a midline occipital encephalocele with herniation of meninges and a small portion of dysplastic cerebellar tissue into the sac, measuring 2.1 x 1.8 cm. The ventricles show mild ventriculomegaly with an atrial measurement of 10.2 mm. Cortical sulcation is appropriate for 22 weeks gestation.

Impression: Midline occipital encephalocele containing meninges and dysplastic cerebellar tissue. Associated mild bilateral ventriculomegaly is present.

Fetal MRI at 35 weeks gestation demonstrates an appropriate late third-trimester brain development. The cerebral cortex shows a highly complex gyral pattern with prominent central, parietal, and temporal sulci, normal for 35 weeks. The lateral ventricles are symmetric, with atrial widths of 6.2 mm. The corpus callosum and cerebellar structures are fully mature and intact.

Somatic structures, including the lungs, liver, kidneys, and bowel, show no signs of abnormality. Impression: Unremarkable late-gestation fetal MRI demonstrating normal cortical maturation and structural development.

Fetal MRI at 26 weeks gestation reveals marked asymmetric dilation of the lateral ventricles. The right lateral ventricle atrial width measures 14.1 mm, indicative of moderate-to-severe ventriculomegaly, while the left atrium measures 11.2 mm. There is mild thinning of the posterior corpus callosum, although it is visible in its entirety. The sylvian fissures show appropriate opercularization for this gestational age.

No parenchymal hemorrhage, germinal matrix hemorrhage, or extra-axial fluid collections are detected. The posterior fossa structures appear normal. Impression: Significant right-sided fetal ventriculomegaly. Recommend serial follow-up ultrasounds and postnatal neurosurgical evaluation.

Brain MRI reveals cerebellar tonsillar herniation extending approximately 8 mm below the level of the foramen magnum. The tonsils appear peg-like and pointed, compressing the CSF space at the craniocervical junction. Additionally, there is a small, focal syrinx extending from C2 to C4 within the cervical spinal cord. The cerebral ventricles are normal in size and position.

Impression: Chiari I malformation with associated cervical spine syrinx. Correlation with clinical symptoms of headache, neck pain, or upper extremity sensory changes is recommended.
